1966-67

Jim Haynes (president)

13 entries · 29 index lines

April1966

President Kelly Thompson approves the constitution

The proposed constitution of the Associated Students of Western Kentucky University was completed in late March and approved on 1 April. The copy held by WKU Archives is dated 7 April 1966.

In the recordTopSCHOLAR - SGA Constitution

April1966

Thompson's approval letter is addressed to committee chair Reed Morgan

The archived copy of Thompson's approval letter names the organizing committee that drafted the constitution: Reed Morgan as chair, John Lovett as vice chair. Morgan's committee did the drafting; Jim Haynes was elected to lead the government it created six weeks later.

In the recordUA3/3/1, Letter to Organizational Committee for a Western Student Organization, 1 Apr 1966

26 April1966

Students ratify the constitution, 1,812 to 726

A four-day referendum. 2,538 students voted - a larger raw turnout than most SGA elections have managed since.

In the recordWKU SGA history

18 May1966

Jim Haynes elected first president

Seven weeks from presidential approval to a seated student president. Western Kentucky State College became Western Kentucky University on 16 June, so the university and its student government are almost exactly the same age.

In the recordWKU SGA history

29 September1966campus

The new government opens its first full year

The Herald's first issue of the fall reported the student senate ratifying a government appointment as the Associated Students began their first full academic year. Students had approved the constitution and elected officers the previous spring.

In the recordHerald 46:1, 29 Sep 1966

27 October1966campus

Doing well, but lacking communication

Midway through the fall semester the Herald judged that Associated Students leaders were performing well but were failing to communicate with the students they represented. It was the first public report card on the year-old government.

In the recordHerald 46:5, 27 Oct 1966

10 November1966campus

Government and administration meet on campus problems

The Herald reported Student Government Association leaders meeting with President Kelly Thompson to discuss campus problems, an early instance of the year-old government dealing directly with the administration.

In the recordHerald 46:7, 10 Nov 1966

9 March1967campus

Herald warns of a 'popularity bandwagon' in the spring election

A week before the presidential campaign opened, the Herald ran a piece by Fran Salyers arguing that popularity, not merit, was set to decide the Associated Students election.

In the recordHerald 46:16, 9 Mar 1967

16 March1967campus

Two vie for the presidency

The Herald reported two candidates seeking the Associated Students presidency, with campaigns for the organization's second presidential election set to open the following Monday.

In the recordHerald 46:17, 16 Mar 1967

4 May1967campus

Swearing-in set for May 10

The Herald announced that newly elected Associated Student officers would be sworn in on May 10, 1967, completing the organization's first full transfer of leadership.

In the recordHerald 46:22, 4 May 1967

12 May1967campus

First year judged: organization, progress, apathy

Reviewing the government's first year, the Herald found organization and progress alongside persistent student apathy. The same issue carried president-elect William Menser's plans for 1967-68 and a letter arguing that the Associated Students really worked.

In the recordHerald 46:23, 12 May 1967

18 May1967campus

Herald presses students to vote as the year closes

Days after the outgoing administration's year-end review, the Herald ran a piece headlined 'Goof Government Needs Student Vote,' pressing students toward greater turnout as Menser's incoming administration took over.

In the recordHerald 46:24, 18 May 1967

30 May1967campus

Dean Keown proposes a budget for the new government

Dean of Students Charles Keown sent President Kelly Thompson a memo proposing a student fee structure to create a budget for the Associated Student Government. He attached fee models gathered from universities across the South and Midwest.

In the recordUA3/3/1 Keown memo, 30 May 1967

1967-68

William Menser (president)

18 entries · 49 index lines

14 September1967

Menser and President Thompson open the school year together

The first Herald of the 1967-68 year carried a joint welcome to students headlined "Dr. Kelly Thompson, William Menser Welcome Students." The same issue ran an item headed "Associated Student Government Events Set," laying out the organisation's calendar for the coming term.

In the recordHerald 47:1, 14 Sep 1967

14 October1967campus

Rodes-Harlin Hall opens as a nine-story women's dorm

The Herald covered the opening of Rodes-Harlin Hall, a new nine-story women's residence hall, as campus construction continued to expand housing capacity.

In the recordHerald 47:6, 14 Oct 1967

2 November1967

Herald floats a student seat on the Board of Regents

A Herald article headlined 'Ward Favors Student on Board of Regents' reported support for putting a student on the Board of Regents, months before Western sent lobbyists to Frankfort or a bill reached committee.

In the recordHerald 47:10, 2 Nov 1967

2 November1967

ASG sponsors a Friday dance

The same issue that floated a student regent seat also reported the Associated Student Government sponsoring a campus dance that Friday.

In the recordHerald 47:10, 2 Nov 1967

8 December1967

ASG survey of student activity preferences

The Associated Students published a survey of what activities students wanted, reported by Ellen Bennett in the same issue as a Herald piece commending the government's efforts and coverage of the Kentucky Intercollegiate Press Association backing a proposal for student representation.

In the recordHerald 47:14, 8 Dec 1967

8 December1967

Kentucky Intercollegiate Press Association backs student representation

The statewide student press association came out for a proposal for student representation, reported in the same Herald issue as the Associated Students' activity survey.

In the recordHerald 47:14, 8 Dec 1967

8 December1967

Associated Students survey students on activity preferences

The Herald reported the results of an Associated Students survey under the headline "Associated Students' Survey Reveals Activity Preferences." The same issue carried a letter headed "Commends Associated Student Government's Efforts."

In the recordHerald 47:14, 8 Dec 1967

8 December1967

State press association backs student representation proposal

The 8 December 1967 Herald reported that the Kentucky Intercollegiate Press Association had come out in support of the proposal for student representation. The item ran alongside the paper's coverage of Associated Students activity that week.

In the recordHerald 47:14, 8 Dec 1967

8 February1968

A bill to put a student on the Board of Regents reaches committee

Reported by Ron Lawrence. Western had sent lobbyists to Frankfort for it earlier that month. The same issue carries students berating dorm rules and a letter headed 'Wanted: Work for Judicial Council'.

In the recordHerald 47:18, 8 Feb 1968

22 February1968

Herald questions ASG's Judicial Council as students organize a book swap

Bill Martin's column questioned the Judicial Council's work, while the same issue reported the Associated Student Government directing a student book swap.

In the recordHerald 47:20, 22 Feb 1968

29 February1968

WKU sends lobbyists to Frankfort for a student on the Board of Regents

The same Herald issue carries a tuition increase, a discussion group on major issues before the Associated Student Government and a committee investigating women's dormitory rules. This is the origin of the student regent seat.

In the recordHerald 47:20 [21], 29 Feb 1968

29 February1968

Associated Students discussion group takes up major campus issues

The Herald announced that major issues would be heard in an Associated Student Government discussion group. The same issue reported that Western had sent lobbyists in support of a bill to place a student on the Board of Regents, and carried coverage of a tuition increase.

In the recordHerald 47:20 [21], 29 Feb 1968

4 April1968

William Menser becomes WKU's first student regent

Two months after the bill was in committee, the Herald reported that Menser 'assumes duties as Regent Board Member'. The seat carried no vote at first. The same issue opens candidate declarations for the next student government election.

In the recordHerald 47:26, 4 Apr 1968

11 April1968

Filing reveals few candidates for the spring election

Alana White reported that filing for Associated Student Government offices turned up few candidates, in the same issue as a piece urging that criteria for the offices be voiced.

In the recordHerald 47:27, 11 Apr 1968

29 April1968

Menser discusses the head fee

The same issue that opened coverage of the Straeffer-Whitley race to succeed him carried a piece on outgoing president Menser discussing the student head fee. The archive does not yet hold the article's text.

In the recordHerald 47:28, 29 Apr 1968

29 April1968

Herald analyzes ASG's past performance under Menser

A retrospective headlined 'Past Performance of Associated Student Government Analyzed' ran as Menser's term ended, in the same issue as the Straeffer-Whitley presidential campaign coverage. The archive does not yet hold the article's text.

In the recordHerald 47:28, 29 Apr 1968

29 April1968

Herald reviews the Associated Student Government's record

As Menser's term drew to a close the Herald ran an assessment headed "Past Performance of Associated Student Government Analyzed." It appeared in the same issue as the campaign coverage for the officers who would succeed him.

In the recordHerald 47:28, 29 Apr 1968

9 May1968

Bill Straeffer wins the presidency; the Herald calls the election a failure

The issue reporting Straeffer's win also carries an editorial headed 'Elections Illustrate Faults, Indifference'. Turnout anxiety shows up in the second contested election the organisation ever held.

In the recordHerald 47:30, 9 May 1968

1968-69

Reed Morgan (role unresolved) · Bill Straeffer (president) · Paul Gerard, III (student regent)

10 entries · 10 index lines

29 April1968

Straeffer and Whitley vie for the presidency

The Herald's pre-election coverage set out the field: Bill Straeffer against Charles Whitley for president, Terry Gilpin against Bob Van Corbach for vice president, and contested races down to secretary, treasurer, and congressman at large.

In the recordHerald 47:28, 29 Apr 1968

2 May1968

Straeffer elected president, 1,732 to 1,098; turnout 34 percent

The Associated Students' internal election-results memo lists the full slate: Bill Straeffer over Charles Whitley for president, Terry Gilpin over Bob Van Corbach for vice president, Becky Cooper over Mary Miller for secretary, Tonii Rizzo over John Combs for treasurer, and John Cobelli and Janie Heathcoat elected congressmen at large over Billy Goodman and Scott Phillips. Total turnout was 2,894 votes, about 34 percent of enrollment.

In the recordUA3/3/1 Memo Re: Results of Election, Ron Beck, 3 May 1968Read it here

3 October1968campus

Committees go to work

The Herald reported Associated Students committees swinging into action as the year began. The same issue noted that booking problems still plagued the group's entertainment calendar.

In the recordHerald 48:3, 3 Oct 1968

5 December1968campus

Judicial Council begins hearing cases

The Associated Students Judicial Council was hearing student cases, the Herald reported, an early exercise of the judicial power the young government claimed under its constitution.

In the recordHerald 48:12, 5 Dec 1968

9 January1969campus

Bringing speakers and shows to the Hill

The Herald reported the Associated Students working to bring speakers and entertainment to campus, alongside notice of an upcoming Associated Students dance.

In the recordHerald 48:15, 9 Jan 1969

13 February1969campus

A buffer against campus turmoil

As campus unrest spread nationally, the Herald suggested the Associated Student Government could deter turmoil at Western. The same issue reported president Bill Straeffer moving to discontinue the Greek-oriented Campus Favorites election.

In the recordHerald 48:17, 13 Feb 1969

27 February1969campus

Paul Gerard profiled as student regent

Herald writer Bruce Tucker profiled student regent Paul Gerard, and the paper reported a committee appointed to study revision of the Associated Students constitution.

In the recordHerald 48:19, 27 Feb 1969

Election Tuesday as declarations continue

Declarations of candidacy continued as the Associated Students election was set for the following Tuesday.

In the recordHerald 48:21, 13 Mar 1969

Straeffer and Gilpin review their year

The Herald ran the outgoing administration's own account of its year under the headline 'Associated Students Produces Year of Advancement,' alongside a companion piece on Straeffer and Gilpin reviewing their term.

In the recordHerald 48:28 [29], 8 May 1969

22 May1969campus

Zielke and Porter outline the coming year

Incoming leaders Larry Zielke and David Porter outlined the coming Associated Students administration for the Herald, closing the 1968-69 transition.

In the recordHerald 48:30, 22 May 1969

1969-70

Paul Gerard, III (student regent) · Larry Zielke (president)

13 entries · 25 index lines

25 March1969

Genzianelli and Zielke clash for the presidency

The Herald's Associated Students election special edition covered a two-way presidential race between Frank Genzianelli and Larry Zielke, and a separate race for the second officer spot between John Lyne and David Porter.

In the recordHerald 48:23, 25 Mar 1969

22 May1969

Zielke and Porter outline the coming administration

With Larry Zielke elected president and David Porter as his second officer, the Herald ran their plans for the 1969-70 Associated Students administration. The same issue covered President Kelly Thompson's resignation announcement.

In the recordHerald 48:30 [31], 22 May 1969

22 May1969campus

President Kelly Thompson announces his resignation

Thompson, who had approved the Associated Students constitution in 1966, announced he would step down as WKU's president. The Herald covered it in the same issue as the incoming Zielke-Porter student administration.

In the recordHerald 48:30 [31], 22 May 1969

7 October1969

Associated Student Congress endorses the Vietnam Moratorium

The Herald called it a bold step. The clearest early example of the body taking a position outside the campus fence - the same argument that returns in 2017 and 2023.

In the recordHerald 49:5, 7 Oct 1969

4 November1969campus

New constitution sent back for study

The Associated Student Government returned its proposed new constitution for further study while limiting how long the review could run. The same issue reported the group enlisting merchants for a student discount plan.

In the recordHerald 49:13, 4 Nov 1969

7 November1969

Students start grading the faculty

An ASG committee compiled the results of Western's first student teacher-evaluation effort. The Herald had already editorialised demanding the tabulation move faster.

In the recordHerald 49:11, 7 Nov 1969

9 December1969campus

ASG urges a probe of student housing

The Associated Student Government urged an investigation of student housing, one of the fall's most pointed challenges to university policy.

In the recordHerald 49:20, 9 Dec 1969

13 January1970campus

Congress joins the fight against the superboard

The Associated Students Congress joined the fight against a proposed state superboard for higher education, and the Herald's editorial page argued the same week that the student regent deserved a vote.

In the recordHerald 49:24, 13 Jan 1970

10 February1970

'Associate' regents want voting power

Two pieces in one issue: Associated Students seeking voting rights for the student regent, and student and faculty 'associate' regents pressing for a vote. An editorial calls for broad support of Senate Bill 75. Two years in, the seat was still symbolic.

In the recordHerald 49:26, 10 Feb 1970

13 March1970campus

Lyne wins the presidency before the race begins

John Lyne won the Associated Students presidency before the race began, his bid unopposed. The same issue reported the legislature dropping the bill that would have given student regents a vote, under a headline that lawmakers had kept students impotent.

In the recordHerald 49:35, 13 Mar 1970

24 April1970campus

Four constitution changes go to a vote

The Associated Students Congress moved to seek ratification of four constitution changes, and the Herald saluted vice president David Porter as the government's unsung hero.

In the recordHerald 49:43, 24 Apr 1970

8 May1970campus

ASG figures in the Kent State week delegations

During the Strike Western! demonstrations after the Kent State shootings, John Lyne and Larry Zielke were among the students who presented resolutions to President Dero Downing and Dean Charles Keown on May 8, and both sat with the group that received the university's response on May 11.

In the recordWKU Timeline: Strike Western!

16 May1970campus

Congress endorses Downing's reply to protesters

As the Strike Western! week wound down, the Associated Student Congress unanimously endorsed President Dero Downing's reply to the protesters, aligning the elected student government with the administration's answer to the demonstrations.

In the recordHerald 49:49, 16 May 1970

1970-71

John Lyne (president)

13 entries · 29 index lines

13 March1970

John Lyne wins the presidency before the race begins

No opponent filed against Lyne for the 1970-71 Associated Students presidency, and the Herald reported him elected without a contest.

In the recordHerald 49:35, 13 Mar 1970

27 March1970

Doug Alexander captures the vice presidency

Alexander beat Steve Tichenor for the Associated Students vice presidency in the vote held the week after Lyne's uncontested presidential win.

In the recordHerald 49:39, 27 Mar 1970

28 August1970

Regents seat eight students on the Academic Council

An editorial framed it as the Regents opening doors to student expression in academics. Representation was arriving faster in the curriculum committees than on the board itself.

In the recordHerald 50:1, 28 Aug 1970

27 October1970

A resolution on the women's curfew, five months after Kent State

The Associated Student Congress passed a curfew resolution; the Herald reported abolition was unlikely that year and editorialised that the curfew was obsolete. The letters page in the same issue is almost entirely students arguing about Kent State.

In the recordHerald 50:17, 27 Oct 1970

Congress funds Kunstler and Devlin lectures, plans new constitution

The Associated Student Congress passed a lecture bill funding campus appearances by William Kunstler and Bernadette Devlin, and the Herald reported the Congress was drafting a new constitution.

20 November1970

Congress endorses a proposed constitution

The Associated Student Congress endorsed a proposed new constitution, continuing the reform effort launched two weeks earlier. The same issue previewed William Kunstler's scheduled Monday lecture, funded by the Congress's 6 November bill.

With filing open for the spring elections, the Herald reported twenty student government offices going begging for candidates.

ASG's Free University of no-cost, no-credit evening courses continued for another year, though with fewer courses than before.

An ASG housing survey urged improvement in dormitory conditions, part of a fall agenda that also included a committee on part-time student opportunities and a push for paper recycling.

The Herald's opening issue reported the Board of Regents extending dormitory visitation and approving a $29.8 million budget at the board's first session of the year.

27 September1974campus

Keffer wins freshman vote; Consolo names eight to congress

The Herald reported that Jay Keffer won the freshman election for the top freshman post. In the same issue, ASG president Jeff Consolo tabbed eight students for seats in the ASG congress, and the Academic Council heard a proposal for more student votes.

In the recordHerald 50:9, 27 Sep 1974

15 October1974campus

Protesters urge ASG revamping

Protesters urged a revamping of the Associated Student Government. The same issue carried Janet Steen's report that ASG ecology projects were non-existent.

In the recordHerald 50:14, 15 Oct 1974

19 November1974campus

ASG schedules Kiss and initiates concert hour

ASG scheduled the rock band Kiss and initiated a concert hour, part of its role booking campus entertainment that fall. The concert program later became a major source of financial trouble for the organization.

In the recordHerald 50:24, 19 Nov 1974

21 January1975campus

ASG rescues the Student Volunteer Bureau

ASG agreed to administer the Student Volunteer Bureau. The Herald reported that the bureau was rescued by the student government's action.

In the recordHerald 50:30, 21 Jan 1975

7 February1975campus

Budget troubles threaten ASG entertainment role

The Herald reported that financial difficulties might force ASG to drop its entertainment duties, and the ASG congress heard the treasurer's budget explanation. Columnists Dave Allen and Craig Griffith examined the organization's budget problems in the same issue.

In the recordHerald 50:35, 7 Feb 1975

Quorum failures halt ASG twice in one week

ASG action was halted twice during the week by a lack of quorum. A Herald editorial said the confusion in ASG signaled a need for change.

Primary canceled; constitutional change approved

The primary election for Associated Student Government was canceled, and the student government approved a constitutional change. A letter writer in the same issue criticized the Herald's coverage of ASG.

Big concert, big loss

An ASG concert drew 4,300 people but lost $7,000, the Herald reported, opening a money argument that ran through the fall.

In the recordHerald 51:7, 19 Sep 1975

ASG suggests a campus bank

ASG suggested creating a campus bank for students, one of the new administration's early service proposals.

In the recordHerald 51:11, 3 Oct 1975

Budget approved amid concert debate

The ASG budget won approval as concerts were discussed, two weeks after the money-losing season opener had put the program under scrutiny.

In the recordHerald 51:15, 17 Oct 1975

Fund misuse charges aired

Charges of ASG fund misuse were heard in the same week the congress voted to create an activities committee and a letter writer attacked the organization.

In the recordHerald 51:17, 24 Oct 1975

25 November1975campus

A budget remedy and a book exchange

The Herald weighed whether a new ASG budget offered a remedy, and reported a spring semester book exchange to be co-sponsored by ASG and Veterans on Campus. President Steve Henry moved to change the concert proposal the same week.

In the recordHerald 51:26, 25 Nov 1975

12 December1975campus

Petition drive seeks support

ASG sought student support with a petition and prepared to hear appeals over its concert policy as the fall semester closed.

In the recordHerald 51:30, 12 Dec 1975

26 March1976campus

Faulk impeachment hearings open as campaign begins

The Associated Student Government began impeachment hearings against congress member Gerard Faulk the same week candidates for the spring election, including Christy Vogt, were set to speak to students. An editorial the same issue held up Associated Student Government's troubles as a cautionary example for the university's newly forming Faculty Senate.

In the recordHerald 51:49, 26 Mar 1976

In the recordHerald 51:51, 2 Apr 1976

9 April1976campus

Election season and an acquittal

During the spring election season ASG acquitted congress member Gerard Faulk in an internal proceeding, and the Herald polled voters on the races.

9 April1976campus

Christy Vogt wins the ASG presidency

The Herald reported Christy Vogt's win in the Associated Student Government presidential election under the headline "Christy Vogt Wins Election," with Vogt's own "Winner Says Thanks" running in the same issue. The paper reported the result the same week Gerard Faulk was acquitted in his impeachment case.

In the recordHerald 51:53, 9 Apr 1976

27 April1976campus

Herald supplement recaps a year of ASG wins

A special supplement to the Herald, paid for and written by the Associated Student Government, summed up the outgoing Henry administration's year: women's hours abolished with ASG's backing, better intramural facilities credited to ASG resolutions, a new ASG discount card program, a second campus site for cashing checks, and a Veterans on Campus book exchange. The supplement also printed the year's roster of congress members and its bills and resolutions, and carried Christy Vogt's own piece on laundry facility improvement.

30 April1976campus

The congress approved a tentative budget at the final ASG meeting of the year, and the Herald assessed how Steve Henry's year had required balancing his twin jobs as student regent and ASG president.

1976-77

Christy Mollozzi (president)

11 entries · 53 index lines

7 September1976campus

ASG creates constitutional revision committee

The Associated Student Government congress passed Bill 2, creating a committee charged with revising the organization's constitution. Constitutional revision remained on the ASG agenda for the rest of the school year and appeared again among proposed amendments and a spring referendum bill.

In the recordSGA Records (UA66), Bill 2 - Constitutional Revision Committee, 7 Sep 1976

26 October1976campus

ASG asks WKU for a student minimum wage

The congress adopted Resolution 13, proposing that Western institute a minimum wage policy for all student employees. It was part of a heavy fall docket that also included resolutions on parking, laundry services, non-smoking areas and residence hall change machines.

In the recordSGA Records (UA66), Resolution 13 - Minimum Wage, 26 Oct 1976

9 November1976campus

Seals and Crofts concert loses ASG $3,800

The Herald reported that the Seals and Crofts concert set the Associated Student Government back $3,800. Concert finances would remain a recurring sore point for ASG through the rest of the decade.

In the recordHerald 52:21, 9 Nov 1976

23 November1976campus

ASG recommends preregistration for all students

The Herald reported that ASG would recommend preregistration for all students. Advance registration was one of the four items president Christy Vogt later carried into her end-of-year recommendations to the administration.

In the recordHerald 52:25, 23 Nov 1976

15 February1977campus

Bill calls for ASG to evaluate itself

Bill 6 proposed that the Associated Student Government conduct a self-evaluation "for the purposes of transparency and improvement."

In the recordSGA Records (UA66), Bill 6 - ASG Evaluation, 15 Feb 1977

25 February1977campus

Discrimination resolution fails as 14 abstain

Fourteen members abstained as the Associated Student Government rejected a resolution on discrimination, the Herald reported. The same issue noted that filing for ASG posts would begin the following Monday.

In the recordHerald 52:43, 25 Feb 1977

8 March1977campus

ASG passes bill opposing tuition increase

The congress approved Bill 9, formally opposing a proposed tuition increase. The same March meeting produced Bill 8, which created a Complaint Committee to handle student grievances.

In the recordSGA Records (UA66), Bill 9 - Opposition to Tuition Increase, 8 Mar 1977

April1977campus

Four candidates open the race to succeed Vogt

The Herald previewed a crowded ASG election: Tom Blair, Kirt Grubbs, Mark McChesney and Bob Moore all sought the presidency, with voting set for a Tuesday primary. Three candidates ran for the administrative vice presidency and four for the activities post in the same election.

In the recordHerald 52:49, 1 Apr 1977

12 April1977

Vogt urges involvement as her term closes

With her term nearly over, president Christy Vogt wrote "Urges Involvement" for the Herald, days before Bob Moore's election to succeed her.

In the recordHerald 52:52, 12 Apr 1977

15 April1977

Bob Moore elected ASG president by 26 votes

One of the narrowest margins in the record. The same issue carries the outgoing president congratulating voters, the faculty asking for a say in hiring, and Western fighting a beer licence for a local pizzeria.

In the recordHerald 52:53, 15 Apr 1977

26 April1977campus

Vogt closes the congress with four recommendations

President Christy Vogt sent a letter closing the congress and thanking ASG members for their work. She left four items to recommend to the administration: constitutional revision, extended hours for student buildings, open visitation and advanced registration.

In the recordSGA Records (UA66), Christy Vogt Letter, 26 Apr 1977

8 September1977campus

ASG awaits approval of constitution changes

The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government was awaiting approval of changes to its constitution as the fall term opened. The story ran alongside a look at how ASG's concert booking process actually worked.

President Bob Moore publicly questioned how freshman class candidates were spending their campaign money. The Herald ran an editorial the same week, 'Bob Moore's Comment Isn't Good Politics,' pushing back on his remark.

25 October1977campus

'A$G?' - Moore questions freshman campaign spending

President Bob Moore publicly questioned spending by freshman candidates, in a story the Herald headlined 'A$G?'. The paper answered with an editorial arguing that Moore's comment was not good politics, and Moore wrote back disputing it.

In the recordHerald 53:18, 25 Oct 1977

The Associated Student Government named David Bass its new vice president. The same issue carried Moore's letter disputing the Herald's editorial on candidate spending.

ASG and the Interhall Council backed a coed dorm and abolition of the door-ajar visitation rule. The vote followed weeks in which the two bodies weighed a dorm petition and the Herald urged ASG to represent students in the dorm protest.

President Dero Downing announces his resignation

Downing, who had led WKU since 1969, announced he would step down effective 31 December 1978. Vice President John Minton took over as interim president the following January while the Board of Regents searched for a successor.

1979-80

James Hargroave (president)

13 entries · 37 index lines

12 April1979

830 students vote in the ASG primary; the Herald runs a defence of not voting

The Associated Student Government's spring primary drew 830 voters and put the open-house policy on the ballot. The same issue carried a piece justifying student apathy in ASG voting - the paper had moved from scolding non-voters to explaining them. This primary elected the officers who took office for 1979-80; it was previously misfiled under 1978-79.

In the recordHerald 54:54, 12 Apr 1979

August1979campus

Donald Zacharias sworn in as WKU's sixth president

Zacharias, previously executive assistant to the chancellor of the University of Texas system, took office as WKU's sixth president at the opening of the academic year; he was formally installed the following spring.

In the recordWKU Timeline: Donald Zacharias

30 August1979

ASG head Jamie Hargrove profiled at year's start

The Herald profiled the Associated Student Government head under the headline that he believed students were interested, in the same issue that introduced the new president's wife, Tommie Zacharias, to campus.

In the recordHerald 55:2, 30 Aug 1979

30 August1979campus

Hargrove opens the year saying students are interested

Associated Student Government head Jamie Hargrove told the Herald he believed students were interested in their government as the year opened. A week later ASG heard its 1979-80 budget and discussed changing its delegate policy.

In the recordHerald 55:2, 30 Aug 1979

13 September1979campus

ASG weighs expanding hall representation

The Associated Student Government considered expanding residence hall representation in its congress, in the same issue reporting the Board of Regents set to consider a two-year budget request.

In the recordHerald 55:5, 13 Sep 1979

20 September1979campus

Seats bill passes after revision under pressure

A bill on Associated Student Government seats passed after being revised under pressure, expanding on earlier talk of broader residence hall representation. The Herald called the representation bill a small step in the right direction.

In the recordHerald 55:7, 20 Sep 1979

November1979campus

ASG rejects move to close Diddle Hall

The Associated Student Government rejected a move to close Diddle Hall dormitory. The vote came amid a fall of housing debates that later included a push to make Keen Hall a coed dorm.

In the recordHerald 55:19, 1 Nov 1979

13 November1979

Resolution 79-10 seeks staff for scholarship administration

The Associated Student Government passed Resolution 79-10, urging the university to assign staff to administer academic scholarships.

In the recordSGA Resolution 79-10, Academic Scholarship Expansion

29 November1979campus

ASG proposes an activity fee for part-time students

ASG proposed a part-time student activity fee. The proposal came as the Board of Regents weighed budget requests for the coming biennium.

In the recordHerald 55:25, 29 Nov 1979

21 February1980campus

ASG considers moving its spring elections

The Associated Student Government considered changing the date of its spring elections. The discussion took place against campus anger over a proposed tuition increase.

In the recordHerald 55:40, 21 Feb 1980

17 April1980campus

Fuller and Irons win the presidential primary

Steve Fuller and Tim Irons emerged as victors in the ASG presidential primary, from a field of three that also included David Rue. Candidates had been certified earlier in the month.

In the recordHerald 55:53, 17 Apr 1980

24 April1980campus

Steve Fuller elected ASG president

Steve Fuller, Mark Wilson and Greg Zoeller were elected to the top Associated Student Government jobs. The Herald wrote that persistence had paid off in Fuller's campaign, while runner-up Tim Irons looked to the future after losing.

In the recordHerald 55:55, 24 Apr 1980

May1980campus

New ASG officers and members sworn in

The new Associated Student Government officers and members were sworn in. ASG and the Interhall Council were also conducting student polls as the year closed.

In the recordHerald 55:57, 1 May 1980

1982-83

Sandra Norfleet (student regent) · Margaret Ragan (president)

19 entries · 48 index lines

28 January1982

ASG sets up a council to settle its own disputes

The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government had appointed a council to decide disputes inside the organization. The story ran two weeks after the same reporter, Kevin Francke, covered the resignation of ASG president Marcel Bush.

In the recordHerald 57:35, 28 Jan 1982

11 February1982

ASG and the University Center Board both ask for more money

The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government and the University Center Board both wanted larger budgets and planned to submit requests. Two weeks later the paper ran a piece arguing that the Center Board outshone ASG.

In the recordHerald 57:39, 11 Feb 1982

16 February1982

Norfleet wins the student regent runoff

No candidate won a majority in the February 9 student regent primary, forcing a runoff. Sandra Norfleet won the runoff on February 16.

In the recordHerald 57:41, 18 Feb 1982

April1982

ASG endorses William Natcher

The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government had backed William Natcher. The same issue previewed the ASG presidential primary set for the following Tuesday, and five days later the paper editorialized that endorsing was not wise for ASG.

In the recordHerald 57:51, 1 Apr 1982

8 April1982

Ragan and Sargent survive the ASG primary

Margaret Ragan and Glenn Sargent survived the Associated Student Government presidential primary, emerging from a five-way field.

In the recordHerald 57:53, 8 Apr 1982

15 April1982

Norfleet's short regent term nears its end

The Herald noted that the student regent's two-month term was already nearing its end, a reminder of how short a stopgap the office had been.

In the recordHerald 57:55, 15 Apr 1982

20 April1982

Ragan wins the presidency in a repeated election

The first general election was voided, and Margaret Ragan won the Associated Student Government presidency in the repeated election held April 20. She and the other new officers were sworn in before the month was out.

In the recordHerald 57:57, 22 Apr 1982

26 August1982

Ragan opens the year promising major ASG changes

Monica Dias reported that major ASG changes were envisioned by Margaret Ragan. The story ran in the Herald's second issue of the fall semester and was the paper's first substantial account of her plans.

In the recordHerald 58:2, 26 Aug 1982

2 September1982

ASG considers a Wall of Fame

Monica Dias reported that the Associated Student Government was considering a Wall of Fame. A week later the Herald followed with a report that the wall looked promising.

In the recordHerald 58:4, 2 Sep 1982

18 November1982

ASG approves a coed housing bill

Monica Dias reported that the Associated Student Government had approved a coed housing bill. The measure built through the fall: ASG and the Interhall Council polled students on coed housing in September, and ASG formally proposed it on 10 November.

In the recordHerald 58:25, 18 Nov 1982

9 December1982

ASG breaks from the student legislature

Monica Dias reported that the Associated Student Government had broken from the student legislature. The break did not last, and by February 1984 the Herald was reporting that the Kentucky Intercollegiate State Legislature might join ASG again.

In the recordHerald 58:29, 9 Dec 1982

13 January1983

No quorum, so ASG does not meet

The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government failed to reach a quorum and did not meet. It was the first ASG item the paper carried after the winter break.

In the recordHerald 58:32, 13 Jan 1983

3 February1983

ASG floats a shuttle service, and Ragan explains the split with the regent seat

The same issue that carried President Margaret Ragan's Herald piece explaining that the ASG presidency and student regent seat were now separate positions also reported ASG was considering a shuttle service, the proposal put to a student vote the following week.

In the recordHerald 58:38, 3 Feb 1983

10 February1983

Grade plan passes; students vote for a shuttle

ASG passed a grade plan, and 206 students voted for a campus shuttle service.

In the recordHerald 58:40, 10 Feb 1983

March1983

24 elected to Senate

Twenty-four students were elected to the Associated Student Government Senate, the same issue reporting increased dormitory hours had been proposed.

In the recordHerald 58:45, 1 Mar 1983

17 March1983

Constitution changes approved; filing opens

The Associated Student Government approved changes to its constitution, and ten students filed for offices ahead of the deadline. Dean Charles Keown publicly questioned the revisions the following week, as filings swelled to 68.

In the recordHerald 58:47, 17 Mar 1983

7 April1983

500 vote in the ASG primary

About 500 students voted in the Associated Student Government primary. The Herald's letters pages carried a steady stream of endorsements for presidential candidate Jack Smith.

In the recordHerald 58:53, 7 Apr 1983

14 April1983

Jack Smith wins the ASG presidency

Jack Smith won the presidency of the Associated Student Government, and students voted for the ASG constitutional revisions on the same ballot. The Herald had dared students to vote at all in a sardonic election day editorial.

In the recordHerald 58:55, 14 Apr 1983

28 April1983

ASG endorses a $15 athletic fee

The outgoing congress endorsed a $15 athletic fee. The vote came as the Board of Regents turned its focus to the budget.

In the recordHerald 58:59, 28 Apr 1983

1983-84

Jack Smith (president)

16 entries · 58 index lines

12 April1983

ASG election day: candidates court votes for the top offices

The Herald urged students to the polls for the Associated Student Government election. Beyond the presidential contest, candidates for ASG's other top offices - including Bob Shults, Laura McClellan, Traci Turner, Kim Binkley and Allan Kujala - each drew endorsement letters in the paper; the Herald index does not specify which office each sought.

In the recordHerald 58:54, 12 Apr 1983

23 August1983

Escort service returns; discount card floated

The Herald's opening issue reported that the student escort service would resume and that ASG might sponsor a discount card. Filing for freshman elections was set to begin September 19.

In the recordHerald 59:1, 23 Aug 1983

30 August1983

Smith opens with a "year of action"

Steve Paul reported that the Associated Student Government was planning for a year of action. The story ran in the third issue of the fall semester, a week after the Herald first reported that ASG might sponsor a discount card.

In the recordHerald 59:3, 30 Aug 1983

September1983

Discount card plan draws fire

ASG voted to study the discount card after the Herald editorialized that the organization should govern, not market cards. A week later the paper reported ASG would offer members a commission on card sales, prompting letters calling the plan cheap shots and old tricks.

In the recordHerald 59:4, 1 Sep 1983

8 September1983

ASG members to take a commission on discount cards

Steve Paul reported that the Associated Student Government would offer its members a commission on the discount cards. The same issue carried two critical columns aimed at ASG, Timi Flener's "Cheap Shots" and Connie Hoffman's "And Old Tricks."

In the recordHerald 59:5, 8 Sep 1983

13 October1983

ASG asks for cable television in dorm rooms

Steve Paul reported that the Associated Student Government wanted cable in dormitory rooms. The same issue ran a Lou Bloss editorial cartoon on an ASG penalty and a letter from Carl Davis disagreeing with an ASG proposal.

In the recordHerald 59:15, 13 Oct 1983

27 October1983

ASG passes incomplete-grade deadline proposal

The Associated Student Government passed its proposal on the deadline for incomplete grades, after tabling it the week before. The grade issue had occupied ASG since September.

In the recordHerald 59:19, 27 Oct 1983

3 November1983

Budget falls short as the grade plan passes

Craig Dezern and Steve Paul reported that the ASG budget would not cover its planned projects. The same issue reported that ASG had approved its grade plan, the change to the grading scale that ran through most of the year.

In the recordHerald 59:21, 3 Nov 1983

10 November1983

ASG takes up a university day-care center

Barry Rose reported that a university day-care center would be studied by the Associated Student Government. It joined study hall research and cable television among the service questions ASG picked up that fall.

In the recordHerald 59:23, 10 Nov 1983

6 December1983

ASG voids its own procedures amid growth

The Herald reported that ASG voided its own procedures, while also noting growth in membership and a congress weighing 14 proposals. The editorial page mocked the body with a cartoon, and Jack Smith wrote in to say the cartoon aggravated him.

In the recordHerald 59:27, 6 Dec 1983

12 January1984

Vice president William Chandler quits

Victoria Malmer reported that Associated Student Government vice president William Chandler had quit. Within a week the Herald reported that three people had been nominated for ASG positions.

In the recordHerald 59:29, 12 Jan 1984

14 February1984

Student legislature may rejoin ASG

The Kentucky Student Legislature delegation was reported possibly rejoining the Associated Student Government. Letter writers sparred the same day over whether the ASG stereotype was deserved.

In the recordHerald 59:38, 14 Feb 1984

23 February1984

The top ASG officers file for re-election

Mark Edelen reported that the top Associated Student Government officers were seeking re-election. The same issue reported that legislators were upset with ASG and that students were being asked to gripe, and it carried further responses to the alcohol poll plan.

In the recordHerald 59:41, 23 Feb 1984

20 March1984

Top four ASG offices decided without runoffs

The top four Associated Student Government spots were decided, the Herald reported, as ASG emphasized representation. About 450 students had voted in the primary the week before.

In the recordHerald 59:45, 20 Mar 1984

3 April1984

ASG polls students on beer and a campus pub

ASG began a student poll on the beer and campus pub issue on general election day. The Herald's editorial page argued the economics of the campus pub plan were faulty.

In the recordHerald 59:49, 3 Apr 1984

10 April1984

Low turnout may force a beer poll revote

Low turnout threatened to spur a revote in the ASG beer poll. The same issue reported president Jack Smith impersonating a bunny for the season.

In the recordHerald 59:51, 10 Apr 1984

1984-85

Jack Smith (president)

9 entries · 50 index lines

20 September1984

Four proposals made reality in the third week of class

The Herald reported that four Associated Student Government proposals had already been carried out, and that the congress was beginning a study of a student book exchange. The exchange went on to become the running project of the year.

In the recordHerald 60:7, 20 Sep 1984

27 September1984

The grade scale proposal is denied

ASG's proposal for a new grade scale was denied, one week after the congress's early run of successes. It was the first setback of the fall reported in the Herald's coverage.

In the recordHerald 60:9, 27 Sep 1984

18 October1984

ASG wants less general education

The congress went on record wanting a reduction in general education requirements. It was an early instance of the body intervening in curriculum policy, three years before the fights over the General Education Task Force.

In the recordHerald 60:15, 18 Oct 1984

8 November1984

LaMont Jones drops out of a revote

LaMont Jones withdrew from an ASG revote, and the same issue carried an editorial cartoon on the organization. A disputed election requiring a revote marked the low point of the fall semester.

In the recordHerald 60:19, 8 Nov 1984

31 January1985

Education cuts loom and the book exchange stalls

ASG weighed a fight against state education cuts, while its book exchange venture looked likely to pause for the summer. Both stories ran in the same late-January issue.

In the recordHerald 60:34, 31 Jan 1985

14 February1985

Apathy as an editorial cartoon

'Voter Apathy Can be Solved' ran alongside a cartoon on election apathy and a report that a 24-hour open house was under discussion.

In the recordHerald 60:38, 14 Feb 1985

28 February1985

Four file for congress president

A fourth candidate filed for ASG congress president and a debate was set, as the spring filing period opened. The same issue carried letters both applauding an ASG bill and requesting its support.

In the recordHerald 60:42, 28 Feb 1985

28 March1985

McKinney and Watkins take the primary

Mitchell McKinney and Chris Watkins rode their experience to victory in the ASG primary. The congress also passed a resolution on grade point averages the same week.

In the recordHerald 60:47, 28 Mar 1985

11 April1985

Jack Smith ends his term

The Herald marked the end of Jack Smith's presidency with a news story, an editorial crediting his enthusiasm with reviving interest in ASG, and an editorial cartoon. Mitchell McKinney had been elected the new president the week before.

In the recordHerald 60:51, 11 Apr 1985

1985-86

Mitchell McKinney (president)

24 entries · 45 index lines

14 February1985campus

An apathy editorial greets a 24-hour open house debate

The Herald ran an apathy editorial and cartoon aimed at student government alongside a report on debate over 24-hour open house policy in the dorms.

In the recordHerald 60:38, 14 Feb 1985

21 March1985

Dueling op-eds spar over forcing a bill

The Herald ran a pair of opposing opinion pieces, both headlined "Associated Student Government Shouldn't Force Bill," one by future ASG president Mitchell McKinney and the other by Jamie Morton.

In the recordHerald 60:45, 21 Mar 1985

28 March1985

McKinney and Watkins win the ASG primary

Mitchell McKinney and Chris Watkins won the Associated Student Government presidential primary over a field that included candidate Stan Reagan.

In the recordHerald 60:47, 28 Mar 1985

4 April1985

McKinney elected president; a legislative group rejoins ASG

Mitchell McKinney was elected Associated Student Government president. The same issue reported that an unnamed legislative group had rejoined ASG.

In the recordHerald 60:49, 4 Apr 1985

24 September1985

ASG abolishes its Finance Committee

The congress voted to abolish its own Finance Committee, a structural change later reversed in part when a Financial Advisory Council was written into the bylaws the following spring.

In the recordSGA Bill 85-1-F, Abolishment of Finance Committee

12 October1985

ASG orders its own student discount card

The congress passed legislation calling for ASG to produce its own student discount card, one of several consumer-service ideas the group pursued that fall.

In the recordSGA Bill 85-15-F, Production of Own Student Discount Card

31 October1985

A 20-vote margin and a GPA debate

About 20 votes separated the top two finishers in a fall ASG election, and the congress debated setting a grade-point average requirement for its own members. Both stories ran in the same late-October issue.

In the recordHerald 61:19, 31 Oct 1985

5 November1985

Alcohol on campus studied again

ASG returned to the question of alcohol on campus, an issue that had already produced a student poll and a campus pub debate in 1984. The congress opened a new study of the policy.

In the recordHerald 61:20, 5 Nov 1985

21 November1985

A shuttle to the mall

The congress discussed running a shuttle service from campus to the mall. It was one of several consumer-service ideas, alongside student discount cards, floated that fall.

In the recordHerald 61:25, 21 Nov 1985

12 December1985

Lighting proposal defeated

Student government defeated a campus lighting proposal in the last week of the fall semester. It was one of the few outright defeats of legislation reported that year.

In the recordHerald 61:30, 12 Dec 1985

23 January1986

Fall-break bill narrowly passes

A bill calling for a fall break narrowly passed ASG. The proposal drew an opposing editorial in the next issue calling the extra break impractical and not needed.

In the recordHerald 61:35, 23 Jan 1986

30 January1986

No day off for Martin Luther King Day

ASG rejected a proposal to dismiss classes for the Martin Luther King holiday, one week after passing the fall-break bill. The King holiday question returned to the congress the following year.

In the recordHerald 61:37, 30 Jan 1986

4 March1986

McKinney withdraws from re-election

Mitchell McKinney pulled out of the race for a second term as ASG president. The same issue carried a piece arguing that student government needed a strong leader.

In the recordHerald 61:46, 4 Mar 1986

20 March1986

Library hours proposals, and elections delayed a week

ASG proposals asked for more library hours, and the spring elections were pushed back a week. The same issue carried dueling letters on whether the organization was in trouble.

In the recordHerald 61:48, 20 Mar 1986

25 March1986

College representative seats created

The congress created major/minor college representative seats within its own membership.

In the recordSGA Bill 86-19-S, Voting of Representatives for Colleges

April1986

ASG revises its membership application

The congress adopted a revised application process for SGA membership.

In the recordSGA Bill 86-21-S, Adoption of New Application

April1986

ASG asks regents to attend a meeting

The congress asked that Board of Regents members attend and speak at one SGA meeting during their term.

In the recordSGA Bill 86-22-S, Attendance of Regents at Meetings

April1986

ASG seeks chains for Pearce-Ford Tower windows

The congress asked for chains to be placed on Pearce-Ford Tower windows so they could be opened.

In the recordSGA Bill 86-26-S, Placing of Chain on Windows

2 April1986

Financial Advisory Council written into the bylaws

The congress incorporated the Financial Advisory Council into the ASG bylaws, months after abolishing its own Finance Committee.

In the recordSGA Bill 86-3-S, Incorporation of Councils into By-Laws

3 April1986

Outgoing congress commends President McKinney

The outgoing congress passed a bill commending the work of SGA president Mitchell McKinney as his term ended.

In the recordSGA Bill 86-13-S, Commendation of President

10 April1986

Pranks and accusations mar the races

The Herald reported that pranks and accusations had marred the ASG races, and printed the election results in the same issue. Tim Todd emerged from the field as the new president.

In the recordHerald 61:54, 10 Apr 1986

15 April1986

ASG pushes for a campus welcome sign

The congress pushed for a welcome sign to be placed at the intersection of Normal Drive and University Boulevard.

In the recordSGA Bill 86-36-S, Placing of Welcome Sign on Campus

15 April1986campus

ASG commends outgoing President Minton

The congress passed a bill commending outgoing WKU president John D. Minton for his service to the university.

In the recordSGA Bill 86-39-S, Commendation of Dr. John D. Minton

8 August1986campus

Regents honor McKinney at term's end

The WKU Board of Regents included a resolution honoring outgoing ASG president Mitchell McKinney, alongside honors for Georgia Bates and outgoing WKU president John Minton, at its August meeting - held the same day Kern Alexander was named the university's new president.

In the recordBoard of Regents minutes, 8 Aug 1986

1986-87

Timothy Todd (president)

8 entries · 49 index lines

4 August1986

Twenty years of amendments consolidated into one document

The constitution of the WKU Associated Students with amendments - the only surviving snapshot of how the 1966 framework had been patched over two decades. A Judicial Council roster for 1986-87 survives alongside it.

In the recordTopSCHOLAR - SGA Constitution

11 September1986

A $12,100 budget and a retreat with the university president

ASG approved a $12,100 budget, planned a phone outreach effort to hear students' ideas and needs, and announced a retreat featuring university president Kern Alexander. All three stories ran in the second week of the fall semester.

In the recordHerald 62:5, 11 Sep 1986

18 September1986

A minor change in voting

ASG sought a minor change in its voting procedures early in the fall term. It was the first structural tinkering of the Todd presidency.

In the recordHerald 62:7, 18 Sep 1986

5 March1987

Rules suspended, bills passed

The congress suspended its rules to pass a batch of bills in a single meeting. The rush came as the spring filing period for elections was opening.

In the recordHerald 62:45, 5 Mar 1987

19 March1987

Martin Luther King bill splits the congress

A Martin Luther King bill passed the congress with members split by the argument, a year after ASG had rejected dismissing classes for the holiday. The same issue reported that Tim Todd and Greg Elder would battle again for the presidency.

In the recordHerald 62:46, 19 Mar 1987

2 April1987

Attendance drops after the speeches

The Herald reported that ASG attendance fell off once campaign speeches had been heard. An accompanying piece warned voters that talk was cheap in the presidential race.

In the recordHerald 62:50, 2 Apr 1987

9 April1987

An amendment dies of low member turnout

A constitutional amendment was defeated because too few members turned up to vote on it. The failure came in the same week as the presidential election.

In the recordHerald 62:52, 9 Apr 1987

14 April1987

The Herald calls the race for Elder; the index calls it no contest

On election day the Herald endorsed challenger Greg Elder as the better choice to lead ASG, ran a letter calling the organization impotent, and headlined the race itself as no contest. The indexed issues that survive do not record the published result; the SGA plaque carries Todd through 1988 on a two-year plate.

In the recordHerald 62:53, 14 Apr 1987

1987-88

Timothy Todd (president)

9 entries · 70 index lines

1987

Not enough candidates to fill the ballot

ASG races faced a candidate shortage; one report notes a candidate entered a race to help a rival rather than to win. The same issue has ASG tabling a phone bill after amendment.

In the recordHerald 62:48, 1987

10 September1987

Dropping the intercollegiate legislature considered

ASG considered dropping its membership in the intercollegiate legislature, while the Herald warned that sharing an officer with Interhall Council could mean trouble for both groups. An editorial the following week argued the Kentucky Intercollegiate State Legislature was worth keeping as a way to promote ideas.

In the recordHerald 63:5, 10 Sep 1987

October1987

Crosswalk resolution passes

The congress passed a resolution calling for a crosswalk. Campus safety items, including new screens for dormitory windows, filled much of the fall agenda.

In the recordHerald 63:11, 1 Oct 1987

27 October1987

Getting tough on absenteeism

ASG moved to get tough on absenteeism after a member lost his seat the week before. The Herald was simultaneously reporting that apathy was killing both ASG and the Residence Hall Association.

In the recordHerald 63:18, 27 Oct 1987

10 November1987

Constitutional amendments up for a vote

Constitutional amendments went before the body in November, in the same season the congress was pushing for required teacher evaluations. It was the third straight year of structural revision attempts.

In the recordHerald 63:22, 10 Nov 1987

23 February1988

ASG explains its empty seats

The organization publicly cited its reasons for the vacancies in its ranks, and four congress positions had been filled at a single meeting earlier that month. Days later an editorial told the body it needed better ideas, not gimmicks.

In the recordHerald 63:42, 23 Feb 1988

31 March1988

Ragland and Whitehouse win the primaries

Shannon Ragland and Scott Whitehouse won the ASG presidential primaries, narrowing a field of seven. The same issue reported passage of a proposal requesting a memorial area on campus.

In the recordHerald 63:50, 31 Mar 1988

7 April1988

Whitehouse elected; condom machines approved

Scott Whitehouse won the ASG presidential election, in an issue that also reported the congress approving condom machines for campus. The election coverage ran alongside editorials saying oversight and closed minds had marred the process.

In the recordHerald 63:52, 7 Apr 1988

14 April1988

Bruce Cambron calls for a new election

Bruce Cambron called for a new election a week after the results, following coverage of votes cast for a write-in candidate that ASG was told it could not ignore. The dispute carried into the following fall.

In the recordHerald 63:54, 14 Apr 1988

1988-89

Scott Whitehouse (president)

9 entries · 41 index lines

1988

A formal reaction to the General Education Task Force

ASG filed a written response to a proposed overhaul of general education requirements - one of the earliest surviving examples of student government intervening in curriculum rather than campus life.

In the recordTopSCHOLAR - Documents/Reports/11

15 September1988

Write-in campaigns banned

ASG approved a ban on future write-in campaigns, five months after write-in votes had thrown its own presidential election into dispute. An editorial the next issue said the block showed ASG was not listening.

In the recordHerald 64:7, 15 Sep 1988

29 September1988

Freshman election turnout called pretty good

Turnout in the ASG freshman election was reported as "pretty good." The same issue said the organization was working to make the importance of voting register with students.

In the recordHerald 64:11, 29 Sep 1988

6 October1988

Cambron takes his election complaint to the president

Bruce Cambron, who had called for a new election in April, talked to university president Thomas Meredith about the ASG election. The spring's disputed result was still alive six months on.

In the recordHerald 64:13, 6 Oct 1988

3 November1988

Half the open slots filled; shelters for shuttle stops

ASG filled half of its open congress seats and sought shelters and seats for campus shuttle stops. The following week the Herald editorialized that ASG's efforts directly helped and served students.

In the recordHerald 64:21, 3 Nov 1988

12 December1988

The weeklong Thanksgiving break is dropped

ASG dropped its push for a weeklong Thanksgiving break, three weeks after voting to seek one. In the same issue, members rated their own organization as average.

In the recordHerald 64:28, 12 Dec 1988

16 February1989

An extra study day recommended

ASG recommended adding an extra study day before exams. The proposal followed January efforts to find a way to print teacher evaluations.

In the recordHerald 64:39, 16 Feb 1989

2 March1989

More movie hours wanted

The congress asked for more movie hours on campus. It was one of the quality-of-life items that filled the spring agenda before election season.

In the recordHerald 64:43, 2 Mar 1989

13 April1989

Amos Gott edges Lynn Groemling

Amos Gott narrowly defeated Lynn Groemling in the ASG presidential race. The campaign season had drawn complaints from candidates about the brief primary and an editorial warning that name recognition should not decide the race.

In the recordHerald 64:49, 13 Apr 1989

1989-90

Amos Gott (president)

9 entries · 46 index lines

1989

Resolution 89-3-F asks for AIDS education

Under Resolution 89-3-F, ASG corresponded with administrators requesting education on AIDS, HIV and sexually transmitted diseases. The letters survive in the SGA records alongside the year's other resolution correspondence on mace sales, larger diplomas and a food services committee.

In the recordTopSCHOLAR SGA Reports 52

24 August1989

Gott gets a jump on the semester

The Herald reported that Amos Gott had gotten a jump on the ASG semester, opening his presidency before classes settled in. A companion piece urged students to participate in the organization.

In the recordHerald 65:2, 24 Aug 1989

12 September1989

A budget tiny compared to other schools

The Herald reported that ASG's budget was tiny compared to student governments at other schools. Two days later the congress approved joining a new board but admitted it could not afford the membership.

In the recordHerald 65:6, 12 Sep 1989

17 October1989

Student government goes to Glasgow

Student government went to the WKU Glasgow campus, and the congress agreed to look again at a Public Interest Research Group. Both stories ran in the same mid-October issue.

In the recordHerald 65:16, 17 Oct 1989

9 November1989

Extended library hours

Correspondence between President Amos Gott, Howard Bailey, Sally Ann Strickler and Michael Binder. Resolutions went out as letters to named administrators and answers came back.

In the recordTopSCHOLAR - Documents/Reports

30 November1989

PIRG sunk over its fee system

ASG voted down the proposed Public Interest Research Group, saying its fee system was the culprit. The decision ended a semester of on-and-off consideration of the group.

In the recordHerald 65:27, 30 Nov 1989

22 January1990

The Downing University Center flagpole

One item in a working inventory of the job that year: the flagpole, the stadium press box, a dispute involving a local pizza vendor and a proposed budget for the Board of Student Body Presidents.

In the recordTopSCHOLAR - Documents/Reports

29 March1990

Congress votes to expand

ASG voted to expand its congress, a week after reporting it might add representatives. A follow-up story said classes and student groups would get more voice in the organization.

In the recordHerald 65:49, 29 Mar 1990

12 April1990

Withdrawals save an invalid primary

Candidates withdrew from the ASG races, saving a primary that would otherwise have been invalid; only two candidates were running for president. The Herald had already reported that interest in the organization might be lower, illustrated by a cartoon of student government in an empty room.

19 April1990

Michael Colvin elected Associated Student Government president

Colvin won the Associated Student Government's presidential election, the Herald reported under the headline "Michael Colvin Aces Associated Student Government Election."

In the recordHerald 65:55, 19 Apr 1990

The same Herald issue that reported Colvin's election win reported the Associated Student Government was seeking an increase to the student activity fee.

WKU's Board of Regents met in special session and approved the university's 1990-91 operating budget, tuition rates, and personnel changes ahead of Colvin's term.

In the recordWKU Board of Regents, special meeting, 30 May 1990

23 August1990

Colvin wants to make ideas reality

The Herald introduced Michael Colvin as the new ASG leader who wanted to make ideas reality. The profile opened the organization's year in the second issue of the fall.

In the recordHerald 66:2, 23 Aug 1990

13 September1990

Glasgow's student body budget cut

ASG cut the budget of the WKU Glasgow associated student body. The move came a year after the main campus organization had helped Glasgow change its constitution.

In the recordHerald 66:7, 13 Sep 1990

29 November1990

ASG passes resolution for left-handed desks

The Associated Student Government passed Resolution 90-10-F, requesting that a left-handed desk be provided in each classroom. The Herald reported the vote in its 29 November 1990 issue, alongside news that a companion resolution on excused absences had been killed the same week.

In the recordSGA Legislation, Resolution 90-10-F, "Left Handed Desks"

29 November1990

ASG kills resolution on earthquake-prediction absences

The Associated Student Government killed Resolution 90-12-F, which had asked that student absences tied to Iben Browning's widely publicized forecast of a major New Madrid Fault earthquake be excused. Browning had predicted the quake for on or near 3 December 1990; it prompted regional anxiety and some school closures, but no earthquake occurred. The Herald reported the resolution's defeat in its 29 November 1990 issue.

In the recordSGA Legislation, Resolution 90-12-F, "Excused Absences for Earthquake Prediction"

29 November1990

Left-handed desks pushed; excused absences killed

ASG pushed for left-handed desks in classrooms and killed a resolution on excused absences in the same stretch of meetings. The two items closed out the fall legislative calendar.

In the recordHerald 66:27, 29 Nov 1990

1991

In the recordSGA Legislation, Bill #91-3-S, "ASG to Join Hilltopper Athletic Foundation"

1991

ASG overhauls its by-laws, including veto-override procedure

In the spring term the Associated Student Government passed a cluster of by-law bills: Bill #91-4-S suspended the by-laws to allow a vote on a pending matter, Bill #91-5-S amended the by-laws on how resolutions could be submitted, and Bill #91-6-S changed the by-laws on overriding a presidential veto. The new override procedure was tested weeks later when the Senate's emergency-kit resolution survived a veto on 14 March 1991.

1991

Students held a campus vigil as the Gulf War approached

Two officers step down

Amos Gott and Van Hodge stepped down as ASG officers, and the remaining officers clashed over comprehensive exams in the same issue's coverage. Two weeks later Karl Miller was picked as public relations vice president.

In a single February issue, ASG wanted to cap tuition increases, proposed an overhaul of Detrex registration, and planned lobbying to protect financial aid. It was the broadest policy week of the Colvin year.

2 April1991

Herald previews four ASG candidates

The Herald's "Meet the Candidates" feature previewed four contenders in the spring Associated Student Government elections: Heather Falmlen, Rob Evans, Van Hodge, and Dan Knowles. Falmlen went on to win the race.

In the recordHerald 66:51, 2 Apr 1991, "Meet the Candidates"

11 April1991

Heather Falmlen wins the ASG presidency amid election protests

Falmlen won the Associated Student Government presidential election in results the Herald reported under the headline "Heather Falmlen Wins Amid Associated Student Government Election Protests." The same issue covered a rival group's call to boycott the election, an editorial calling the contest "immature antics," and a complaint that the Herald's own coverage had been biased.

In the recordHerald 66:54, 11 Apr 1991

University newsletter confirms Falmlen holds both offices

WKU's own "On Campus" newsletter reported Heather Falmlen as both Student Regent and Associated Student Government President, a contemporaneous confirmation that the two offices - separately elected two decades earlier - were held by the same person entering her term.

The Associated Student Government passed Resolution 91-2-F, sponsored by the Student Affairs committee, requesting a one-way fare option on the Big Red Shuttle for infrequent riders. In the recordSGA Legislation, Resolution 91-2-F, "Modified Shuttle Fare"

The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #91-11-F, proposing to change the organization's slogan, in the same fall that it voted to rename itself from the Associated Students to the Student Government Association.

Health tops the agenda; more money for the environment

Heather Falmlen opened the year with a student health issue at the top of her agenda, and ASG budgeted more money for environmental efforts. Both stories ran in the first week of the fall semester.

Fighting the city's noise ordinance

ASG resolved to fight Bowling Green's noise ordinance. It was the organization's most direct engagement with city government in years.

In the recordHerald 67:5, 12 Sep 1991

24 September1991

Officers go to the city's meeting

ASG officers attended a city meeting to press the noise ordinance fight, and the organization restarted its voter registration drive. A recycling resolution had its first reading the week before.

In the recordHerald 67:8, 24 Sep 1991

15 October1991

Fall ASG senate and freshman elections held

The Herald covered the Associated Student Government's fall elections on 10 October, and a separate freshman senator election on 15 October; the paper's abstracts do not preserve the results.

In the recordHerald 67:13, 10 Oct 1991, "Associated Student Government Elections Tuesday"

29 October1991

ASG asks that Iracane not be re-elected regents chair

The Associated Student Government passed Resolution 91-6-F, authored by Mark Miller and Eric McWilliams and sponsored by Mistianna Holcomb, asking that Joe Iracane not be re-elected chair of the Board of Regents. The resolution's text stated that Iracane, chairman for eight consecutive years, was under investigation by the FBI, the IRS and U.S. attorneys in Indiana and Kentucky over an alleged $6 million payment to Pyramid Mining Co. in return for contracts and a separate alleged $14,500 payment to the company for a consulting contract; it also accused him of overstepping into day-to-day university operations reserved for the president under the Board's bylaws. The resolution asked student regent Heather Falmlen to vote against him. No source found reports the investigation's outcome. The same day's Herald covered the vote under "Associated Student Government Opposes Joseph Iracane."

In the recordSGA Resolution 91-6-F, "Board of Regents Chair Term Limit"

31 October1991

ASG asks the regents to elect a new leader

ASG urged the Board of Regents to elect a new leader in place of chairman Joseph Iracane, two days after the Herald reported the organization's opposition to him. It was a rare direct challenge to the university's governing board.

In the recordHerald 67:19, 31 Oct 1991

6 November1991campus

Regents re-elect Iracane despite ASG's resolution

A week after the Associated Student Government asked the Board of Regents not to re-elect Joe Iracane as chair, the board did so anyway. The university's own newsletter reported the result under "Joe Iracane Re-elected to Chair Regents."

In the recordOn Campus 1:16, 6 Nov 1991, "Joe Iracane Re-elected to Chair Regents"

12 December1991

A mailing asks parents to back the health service

The Residence Hall Association and ASG sent a joint mailing asking parents to support the campus health service. It closed out the health-focused fall Falmlen had promised in August.

In the recordHerald 67:29, 12 Dec 1991

28 January1992

ASG introduces a bill for a student regent advisory committee

The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #92-01-S, authored by Greg Butler, Mistianna Holcomb, Melony Jones and Melissa Maggard and sponsored by the Public Relations committee, proposing a Student Advisory Committee - made up of the class presidents, a representative from each college and the executive council as ex-officio members - to brief the student regent on Board of Regents agenda items and canvass student opinion before each meeting, two days before the Herald reported the plan.

In the recordSGA Legislation, Bill #92-01-S, "Development of Advisory Committee for Student Regent"

30 January1992

ASG plans a committee on student access to the regent

The Herald reported the Associated Student Government was planning a committee aimed at securing student access to WKU's regent, amid a statewide debate over how regents were selected.

In the recordHerald 67:34, 30 Jan 1992, "Associated Student Government Plans Regent Committee"

30 January1992

Editorial cartoon targets Falmlen

The same Herald issue ran an editorial cartoon, "Ventriloquist's Dummy" by Patrick Richardson, with Falmlen as its subject.

In the recordHerald 67:34, 30 Jan 1992, "Editorial Cartoon Heather Falmlen Ventriloquist's Dummy"

2 April1992

ASG resolves to support football despite budget cuts

The Associated Student Government passed Resolution 92-7-S, declaring its support for the WKU football program in spite of budget cuts. The resolution's own text argued the university had already awarded 67 football scholarships it would be contractually bound to honor even if the program were suspended, calling a suspension that still paid non-playing scholarship athletes an unnecessary expense. This entry corrects the resolution's date: an earlier record in this archive gave 4 February 1992, but the resolution itself is dated introduced 2 April 1992, shortly before the Board of Regents' 1 May vote to keep the program.

In the recordSGA Legislation, Resolution 92-7-S, "Support of Football Program"

7 April1992

Associated Students votes to become the Student Government Association

The body voted to rename itself on 7 April and students ratified the change in a referendum on 14 April. It took effect that autumn.

In the recordWKU SGA history

7 April1992

The primary is canceled

The ASG primary election was canceled, with too few candidates to require one, and a parking bill sat in committee the same week. The general election went ahead the following Tuesday.

In the recordHerald 67:50, 7 Apr 1992

16 April1992

Joe Rains wins big as 1,200 turn out

Joe Rains won the presidential election by a wide margin, with about 1,200 students casting votes. The same ballot carried the constitutional amendments students had voted on two days earlier, including the name change.

In the recordHerald 67:53, 16 Apr 1992

21 April1992

Rains to oversee the change to SGA

The Herald reported that incoming president Joe Rains would oversee the transition from the Associated Student Government to the Student Government Association. Student reaction to the spring's parking bill was reported as varied in the same issue.

In the recordHerald 67:54, 21 Apr 1992

May1992campus

Board of Regents votes to keep football

The Board of Regents voted to keep the football program, following months of budget pressure that had prompted the ASG's February resolution of support.

In the recordHerald, 1 May 1992, "Board of Regents Votes to Keep Football"
