1992-93

Joe Rains (president)

17 entries · 33 index lines

9 April1992

Herald previews the race and the rename referendum

The Herald previewed the Associated Student Government presidential race under "Mistianna Holcomb, Joe Rains Vying for Presidency," profiled candidate Susan Mitchell under "Susan Mitchell Has a Fresh Perspective," and reported that students would soon vote on a referendum to rename the Associated Student Government the Student Government Association. No source found confirms what office Mitchell sought or whether she won it.

In the recordHerald 67:51, 9 Apr 1992

14 April1992

Joe Rains elected SGA president as the ASG-to-SGA renaming took effect

Rains won a contested Associated Student Government presidential election covered by the Herald under the headline "Associated Student Government Needs Joe Rains," alongside a rival editorial cartoon depicting him as Darth Vader and profile pieces on candidates Mark Miller, Mistianna Holcomb and Melony Jones. The same ballot carried the referendum renaming Associated Students as the Student Government Association.

In the recordHerald 67:52, 14 Apr 1992

14 April1992

Turnout worries and candidate profiles filled the ballot issue

The same issue that reported Rains' win ran the Herald's concern piece "Many Students Won't Vote" alongside profile pieces on the other candidates: "Mark Miller's Involvement Makes Him a Leader," "Mistianna Holcomb Takes a Stand for Students," and "Melony Jones Loved & Respected by Peers."

In the recordHerald 67:52, 14 Apr 1992

21 April1992

Rains takes office with a rename to carry out

The Herald reported that incoming president Joe Rains would oversee the change from Associated Student Government to Student Government Association, which students had ratified by referendum the week before. The new name took effect that fall, making Rains the first president to serve under it.

In the recordHerald 67:54, 21 Apr 1992

25 August1992campus

Fall opened with a new logo and discount cards

At its first meeting of the fall on August 25, 1992, the student government discussed a new logo, student discount cards, a voter registration drive and committee assignments. The group was still transitioning from the Associated Student Government name to SGA, and its minutes from this year appear under both titles.

In the recordSGA Records: Meeting Minutes, 25 Aug 1992

3 September1992

The renamed SGA elects its representatives

In its first weeks under the new name, the Student Government Association held elections for its representatives. The Herald covered the vote at the start of the fall semester.

In the recordHerald 68:4, 3 Sep 1992

6 October1992

Support gathers for a rally

The Herald's index for this issue records the new SGA winning support for a campus rally that October, under the headline "Student Government Association Gets Support for Rally."

In the recordHerald 68:12, 6 Oct 1992

13 October1992campus

Resolution asked WKU to spare academics from budget cuts

Resolution 92-7-F asked the university to exempt academic units from a round of proposed budget cuts. State funding pressure ran through the whole fall; the same weeks produced repeated plans for a student rally in Frankfort.

In the recordSGA Records: Resolution 92-7-F, 13 Oct 1992

13 October1992campus

President Meredith addressed the student congress

WKU President Thomas Meredith came to the October 13 meeting to talk about computers, laundry facilities, cable television, lighting and Potter Hall. The same minutes record discussion of budget cuts, homecoming elections, a newsletter and joint forums with the Residence Hall Association.

In the recordSGA Records: Meeting Minutes, 13 Oct 1992

20 October1992campus

Congress honored the Lady Toppers

Resolution 92-8-F honored the WKU women's basketball team for its runner-up finish in the NCAA tournament. It was one of a string of numbered resolutions the congress produced that fall on subjects from drop-add fees to parking.

In the recordSGA Records: Resolution 92-8-F, 20 Oct 1992

19 November1992

An invitation to get involved

An opinion piece by Paul Weathers urged students to get involved in the Student Government Association, part of the Herald's running commentary on the body during its first semester under the new name.

In the recordHerald 68:23, 19 Nov 1992

December1992campus

Just Ask Joe radio program and Project Western

The December 1 minutes record plans for a Just Ask Joe call-in radio program, the Project Western campus cleanup, a President for a Day event, recycling bins and student health insurance. The meeting closed out a semester dominated by tuition and budget worries.

In the recordSGA Records: Meeting Minutes, 1 Dec 1992

10 December1992

Rains pushed SGA to back a student escort service

SGA president Joe Rains argued the organization should support a campus student escort service, the Herald reported.

In the recordHerald 68:27, 10 Dec 1992

11 December1992

University Senate honored Rains for a Frankfort budget-cut rally

The WKU University Senate adopted Resolution R92.11, commending SGA president Joe Rains for taking part in a rally at the state capitol in Frankfort asking the legislature to stop cuts to higher-education funding. TopSCHOLAR records the resolution's history running from 11 December 1992 to its adoption on 29 January 1993.

In the recordWKU University Senate, Resolution R92.11

2 February1993campus

Meredith returned to pitch Potter Hall as a student service center

President Thomas Meredith addressed the February 2 meeting about campus laundry, cable television and turning Potter Hall into a student service center. Members also discussed tuition increases, resignations and general education requirements.

In the recordSGA Records: Meeting Minutes, 2 Feb 1993

13 April1993campus

Spring closed with elections and Earth Day plans

The April 13 meeting took up the budget, spring elections, the annual banquet, a one-card ID system, smoking policy, Adopt-a-Spot and Earth Day. It was the last full meeting recorded in the digitised minutes for the year.

In the recordSGA Records: Meeting Minutes, 13 Apr 1993

22 April1993

Donald Smith rolls to victory

The Herald called the spring election with the headline "Student Government Association Election: Donald Smith Rolls to Victory." Smith would succeed Rains for the 1993-94 term.

In the recordHerald 68:54, 22 Apr 1993

1993-94

Donald Smith (president)

18 entries · 86 index lines

31 August1993

A delayed constitution reading

The fall semester opened with a stumble. The Herald reported that a scheduled reading of the SGA constitution had been delayed, in the same issue that covered rising tempers over campus parking.

In the recordHerald 69:3, 31 Aug 1993

7 September1993

A new constitution came up first

Bill 93-1-F, introduced at the second meeting of the fall, proposed amendments to the SGA constitution. Constitutional revision stayed on the agenda through October, alongside the tuition rally the congress was planning.

In the recordSGA Records: Bill 93-1-F, 7 Sep 1993Read it here

16 September1993

Congress changes approved

The SGA approved changes to its congress in September while freshmen debated for open positions. The Herald covered both in a single mid-September issue.

In the recordHerald 69:7, 16 Sep 1993

12 October1993

Congress planned a tuition rally

The October 12 meeting discussed a tuition rally, the budget, the Plus System and parking. The rally kept appearing in the minutes for the next month as tuition increases moved through the state process.

In the recordSGA Records: Meeting Minutes, 12 Oct 1993Read it here

26 October1993

Bill recognized President's Scholars

Bill 93-4-F proposed formal SGA recognition of President's Scholars at WKU, one of the seventeen numbered pieces of legislation the fall 1993 congress produced.

In the recordSGA Records: Bill 93-4-F, 26 Oct 1993Read it here

November1993

At least seventeen numbered resolutions in one semester

Resolutions 93-4-F through 93-20-F survive in the correspondence files - the fullest single-semester record in the collection, and the best available answer to how much a WKU student senate actually passes in a working term.

In the recordTopSCHOLAR - Documents/Reports

9 November1993campus

Bill funded emergency phones on campus

Bill 93-6-F proposed purchasing and installing emergency telephones on campus. The Herald was still reporting on SGA's security phones the following February, and campus lighting and safety stayed on the agenda into the spring.

In the recordSGA Records: Bill 93-6-F, 9 Nov 1993Read it here

30 November1993campus

Memorial trees for students who die while enrolled

Bill 93-12-F proposed planting memorial trees in tribute to students who die while enrolled at WKU. It capped a heavy late-November run of legislation that also included child care grants for non-traditional students, a book exchange and opening the Downing University Center computer lab during finals.

In the recordSGA Records: Bill 93-12-F, 30 Nov 1993Read it here

14 December1993

Executive Council pressed the administration on holiday housing

The SGA Executive Council, acting on Resolution 93-18-F, wrote to administrators Katherine Tolbert, Dave Parrott, John Osborne and Ann Stathos asking the university to address housing for students during holiday breaks.

In the recordSGA Records: Correspondence - Resolution 93-18-F, 14 Dec 1993Read it here

1994

SGA wrote guidelines for its public forums

The association adopted written guidelines governing how it would run student public forums, formalizing a process that had previously run ad hoc.

In the recordSGA Records: Guidelines for SGA Public Forums, Jan 1994Read it here

8 February1994

Let's work together for change

The Herald ran an opinion piece under the heading "Let's Work Together for Change" and put the question of how SGA could reach more students to its People Poll. The paper also ran a Stacy Curtis editorial cartoon offering a "recipe for better representation."

In the recordHerald 69:35, 8 Feb 1994

17 February1994campus

President for a Day swapped a student into Meredith's office

The Herald reported that student Angelo Rodriguez would switch places with President Thomas Meredith through SGA's President for a Day program. The same issue covered SGA's security phones on campus and a proposal to let students retake C grades that was killed in committee.

In the recordHerald 69:37, 17 Feb 1994

3 March1994

A resolution on class attendance

An SGA resolution covered by the Herald would have let students skip class, reported under the headline "Attendance: Student Government Association Resolution Would Let Students Skip Class."

In the recordHerald 69:41, 3 Mar 1994

8 March1994campus

A $3 fee to support the Big Red Card

Resolution 94-4-S proposed a three dollar student fee to support the Big Red Card program. The card system and its fees ran through the minutes for the rest of the spring.

In the recordSGA Records: Resolution 94-4-S, 8 Mar 1994Read it here

29 March1994campus

Willard's resignation reached the floor

The March 29 meeting took up the resignation of basketball coach Ralph Willard along with the Big Red Card fee, teacher evaluations, emergency telephones, campus lighting and the coming elections. Dialogue Day and Adopt-a-Spot rounded out a crowded agenda.

In the recordSGA Records: Meeting Minutes, 29 Mar 1994Read it here

14 April1994

A disputed primary

The Herald reported that presidential candidate Scott Sivley had not followed SGA and university procedures during the election, in the same issue that carried the tallied results of the primary. The episode ran alongside the paper's get-out-the-vote editorial coverage.

21 April1994

1994-95

Robert Evans (president)

15 entries · 65 index lines

19 April1994

Evans defeats Sivley for the SGA presidency

Rob Evans faced Scott Sivley at the polls on election day; the Herald reported the same day that Sivley had been warned by SGA for violating the organization's campaign policies. Evans and running mate Tara Higdon won.

In the recordHerald 69:52 [51], 19 Apr 1994, "Student Government Association Elections: Scott Sivley vs. Rob Evans at Polls Today"

19 April1994campus

Campus assesses storm damage

The Herald reported that WKU's campus suffered less damage than the surrounding city after a tornado, the same week as the SGA election.

In the recordHerald 69:52 [51], 19 Apr 1994, "Storm; Campus Suffered Less Damage than City"

August1994

Fall 1994 membership roster filed

SGA filed its list of representatives for the fall 1994 semester, part of the organization's routine paperwork under the Evans administration.

In the recordSGA Records: Membership List Fall 1994Read it here

15 August1994

Evans sworn in as student regent

The Board of Regents' quarterly meeting swore in Robert Evans, Joy Gramling and Cornelius Martin, and carried resolutions of appreciation for outgoing officers Donald Smith - the previous SGA president and student regent - and Monnie Hankins.

In the recordWKU Board of Regents, quarterly meeting, 15 Aug 1994

8 September1994

The 1994-95 budget passes

The SGA approved its budget for the year in early September, reported by the Herald under "Student Government Association Approves Budget for 1994-95."

In the recordHerald 70:5, 8 Sep 1994

November1994

Expanded shuttle service draws attention

The Herald reported that expanded Big Red Shuttle bus service, a route the Student Government Association had pushed to extend, was drawing enthusiasm from local stores along its new stops.

In the recordHerald 70:19, 1 Nov 1994

November1994

An editorial defends the memorial trees

The same issue carried the opinion piece "Don't Destroy Trees," addressing the fate of the memorial trees the SGA had established the previous year to honor students who died while enrolled.

In the recordHerald 70:19, 1 Nov 1994

November1994

Resolution asks for grades before the "W" deadline

SGA passed Resolution 94-11-F, asking that students be given a grade before the end of the withdrawal ("W") period so they could make an informed decision about dropping a class.

In the recordSGA Resolution 94-11-F, Examination Prior to end of "W" PeriodRead it here

8 November1994

Bill seeks an SGA listing in the phone book

SGA introduced Bill 94-8-F, asking that a Student Government Association directory section be added to the university's telephone book.

In the recordSGA Bill 94-8-F, Student Telephone DirectoryRead it here

24 January1995

Security phone tops SGA's spring to-do list

The Herald reported a new security phone, a shuttle stop, and the memorial trees on the Student Government Association's agenda, under "New Security Phone, Shuttle Stop, Trees Lead to Student Government's To Do List." The same issue reported a mystery caller had been scaring students with stalking and harassment, the incident that would shape the spring campaign two months later.

In the recordHerald 70:32, 24 Jan 1995, "New Security Phone, Shuttle Stop, Trees Lead to Student Government's To Do List"

28 February1995

SGA discusses escort service, campus cleanup

SGA's regular meeting took up the student escort service, a "President for a Day" promotion, a campus cleanup, and open positions on the body.

In the recordSGA Meeting Minutes, 28 Feb 1995Read it here

11 April1995

Campus security shapes the spring campaign

The Herald reported that being stalked had influenced candidate Tara Higdon, putting campus security at the center of the spring election coverage.

In the recordHerald 70:51, 11 Apr 1995

20 April1995

Tara Higdon moved up as turnout moved down

The Herald reported the spring election under the headline 'Tara Higdon Moves Up; Voting Down,' recording both the choice of the next president and a drop in voter participation. The election closed out the 1994-95 administration.

In the recordHerald 70:54, 20 Apr 1995

25 April1995

The Herald called visibility the key to SGA's success

As the year ended, the Herald ran an editorial package on the association, pairing a Stacy Curtis cartoon of student government in a glass box with the editorial 'Visibility Key to Student Government Association Success.' It was a summing-up of a year in which the paper pressed SGA to be seen doing its work.

In the recordHerald 70:55, 25 Apr 1995

27 April1995

A new beginning

The Herald's transition piece, "Tara Higdon Sees New Beginning," marked the handover from Robert Evans to his elected successor at the end of the academic year.

In the recordHerald 70:56, 27 Apr 1995

Two more emergency phones

September coverage included an SGA dress code and a piece headlined "Tara Higdon Seeks Student Interest in Group," as the new president worked to draw students into the organization.

Presidential pay compared

The Herald reported that pay for student government presidents was higher at other schools, an early airing of a compensation question that would recur in later decades.

In the recordHerald 71:20, 2 Nov 1995

23 January1996campus

A student credited SGA for its trees

A Herald opinion piece ran under the headline 'Student Government Association Doing Good Job with Trees,' crediting the association's campus planting work. Trees and campus grounds were among the group's most visible projects that year.

In the recordHerald 71:32, 23 Jan 1996

8 February1996

A skywalk at the bottom of the Hill

SGA proposed a skywalk at the bottom of the Hill, and the Herald also reported the organization bringing emergency phones to campus in the same issue. The skywalk would quickly draw editorial fire.

In the recordHerald 71:37, 8 Feb 1996

8 February1996campus

SGA proposed a skywalk at the bottom of the Hill

The Herald reported SGA's proposal for a pedestrian skywalk at the bottom of the Hill, and the same issue covered its push to bring emergency phones to campus. The skywalk became the most argued-about SGA idea of the spring.

In the recordHerald 71:37, 8 Feb 1996

13 February1996

The Herald pushes back

Five days after the skywalk proposal, the Herald told SGA to "ditch the pie-in-the-sky idea," and its letters page carried Richard Malek's charge that the organization acted as a "puppet" group. Another letter defended officers Horace Johnson and Kristen Miller against the label "hair-brained."

In the recordHerald 71:38, 13 Feb 1996

13 February1996campus

The skywalk drew fire within a week

Five days after the proposal, the Herald ran a column telling SGA to 'ditch' the 'pie-in-the-sky' skywalk idea, and a letter in the same issue called the association a 'puppet' group. The episode set the combative tone of the spring semester.

In the recordHerald 71:38, 13 Feb 1996

A new store on campus

SGA proposed a new store on campus, reported by the Herald in early March as the organization kept generating campus improvement ideas through the spring.

In the recordHerald 71:44, 5 Mar 1996

A campus store proposal followed

SGA proposed a new store on campus, the Herald reported, as the association kept generating campus improvement ideas through the spring. A week earlier the paper had covered its wish to see the next university president promoted from within.

Longer visitation hours

SGA asked the university for longer residence hall visitation hours, one of the quality-of-life requests that defined the organization's agenda that spring.

Four candidates ran for the top office

In the recordHerald 71:48, 28 Mar 1996

18 April1996

Few turn out for the election that chose Miller

The same Herald issue that declared "It's Kristen Miller's Time" also ran the headline "Few Turn Out for Election," continuing the decade's pattern of falling voter participation in SGA races.

A retreat opens the year

The Herald reported that an SGA retreat provided the opportunity for new discussion and legislation, setting the agenda for Kristen Miller's term before classes had fully begun.

In the recordHerald 72:1, 20 Aug 1996

Officers sworn in at the first fall meeting

The August 27 meeting swore in officers and took up the retreat, an open house, the budget and homecoming. It opened the first full year of minutes in the digitised record since 1994.

29 August1996

A plan to drive party-goers home

The Herald reported "Kristen Miller Makes Plan to Drive Party-Goers Home," the earliest indexed coverage of the safe-ride idea that became Provide-A-Ride. The same issue reported SGA giving more money to campus clubs.

In the recordHerald 72:4, 29 Aug 1996

17 September1996campus

SGA created a Technology Committee

The September 17 meeting created the SGA Technology Committee and discussed intramural facilities, photocopiers in dorms and Campus Clean Up. Student email accounts and other technology questions recur in the fall's minutes.

24 September1996

Roller blades, skateboards, and a technology push

A September 24 meeting took up campus rules on roller blading and skateboards alongside Provide-A-Ride, a voter registration drive, a bonfire, Big Red Roar, the budget, and student email accounts.

In the recordSGA Meeting Minutes, 24 Sep 1996

The Herald reported SGA proposing more campus lighting while a resolution was vetoed. Campus lighting had been a steady SGA cause since the earlier emergency phones push.

Thirty years of student government

More student seats at the games

SGA secretary Jamie Fite wrote to interim president Barbara Burch requesting additional student seating in Diddle Arena and Smith Stadium. The letter survives in the SGA records collection.

The ten-point scale fight begins

Resolution 97-6-F called for reinstatement of the ten-point grade scale, and Resolution 97-5-F addressed charitable organizations and solicitation of funds the same evening. The grading fight would run on for years at WKU.

In the recordWKU SGA legislation archive, 1997 (archived 2003)

Bill 97-1-F funded a Summer Job and Internship Career Fair, the first bill of the fall session under Keith Coffman.

In the recordWKU SGA legislation archive, 1997 (archived 2003)

A crosswalk on Dogwood Drive

One of a run of outgoing letters in these years covering student seating at athletic events, ice machines in residence halls, campus safety, professors posting office hours, food court hours, housing scholarships for off-campus students and student health services.

Designated driver cards

Bill 97-3-F funded designated driver cards, extending the safe-ride agenda begun under Kristen Miller into a second year. The same week brought a bill to buy typewriters for the library.

Paper towels for the Downing University Center

Resolution 97-9-F asked that paper towels be placed in the restrooms of the Downing University Center. It is one of only two pieces of legislation from the year in the digitised SGA collection.

11 November1997

A November flood of resolutions

Between November 2 and 18 the congress passed at least fifteen numbered resolutions, covering a speed hump for the Regents Avenue lot, fifteen-minute parking spaces, working ID scanners, new sidewalks at Thompson and Grise, ice machines, soap and sanitary restrooms in residence halls, picnic tables, bicycle racks and recognition for honors graduates. It is one of the densest legislative months in the surviving 1990s record.

In the recordWKU SGA legislation archive, 1997 (archived 2003)

Picnic tables for the bottom of campus

Resolution 97-23-F requested picnic tables for the campus area near Zacharias Hall, Meredith Hall and Pearce-Ford Tower. Its numbering shows the congress had produced at least 23 fall resolutions by mid-November.

1999-00

Amanda Lich (president)

23 entries · 58 index lines

8 April1999

Jones and Coates square off amid a pizza-party dispute

The Herald's pre-election issue covered the presidential race between Will Jones and Amanda Coates, alongside a report that SGA was questioning an election-eve pizza party Jones had held, a debate over eliminating the rule requiring a year of SGA experience to run for office, and a heated treasurer's race between Ryan Morrison and Joe Matheis.

In the recordHerald 74:49, 8 Apr 1999

15 April1999

A turbulent election puts Amanda Coates in office

The Herald's coverage of the spring SGA election was headlined "Turbulent Elections Complete"; the same issue carried an opinion piece, "Student Government Association Offers No Leadership," challenging the incoming administration to prove itself.

In the recordHerald 74:51, 15 Apr 1999Read it here

15 April1999

Recount narrows Coates and Martin's win to three votes

Amanda Coates and running mate Cassie Martin initially led Will Jones and Kara Yeckering 616-611 for president and vice president; after the Coates-Martin ticket asked for a recount to be sure of the win, the recount that night found an even closer margin, 614-611. A write-in ticket of Dwight Campbell and Kerri Richardson finished third with 145 votes. Total turnout was 1,436 students.

In the recordHerald 74:51, 15 Apr 1999Read it here

15 April1999

Matheis survives a flier scandal to win vice president of finance

Joe Matheis defeated Ryan Morrison 700-688 for vice president of finance in the campaign's most contentious race. Two hours after the initial result, SGA's judicial council placed the race under review after fliers Matheis had distributed turned up left on classroom desks and in computer labs overnight, violating election code; the council warned Matheis could lose the seat if he had not made a good-faith effort to collect them. The council let the result stand the next day, and Morrison filed a complaint with the judicial council disputing that decision, saying fliers were still on desks in Garrett and the fine arts center.

In the recordHerald 74:51, 15 Apr 1999Read it here

15 April1999

Griffey and Bastin win the remaining executive seats

Brandon Griffey defeated Amanda Kirby 729-652 for vice president of administration, and Matt Bastin defeated Duan Wright 806-570 for vice president of public relations, completing the 1999-2000 executive slate.

In the recordHerald 74:51, 15 Apr 1999Read it here

15 April1999

A letter to the editor questions an SGA probe of racially charged campaign fliers

A Herald letter to the editor reported that fliers reading "Vote for Will Jones in Racism," written in black ink, had circulated in dorms during the campaign, and that SGA opened an investigation into whether they were racially motivated. The letter's author named Jones - described as the first Black candidate for SGA president in years - as a suspect despite his denial of any involvement, and questioned whether the investigation was following proper procedure rather than targeting him by assumption. No source found reports how, or whether, the investigation was resolved.

In the recordHerald 74:51, 15 Apr 1999Read it here

SGA considered Bill 99-10-F, creating a new SGA position of Information Technology Director.

In the recordSGA Bill 99-10-F, Information Technology Director

15 September1999

SGA created an Information Technology Director

Bill 99-10-F created the SGA position of Information Technology Director, and the same month produced a bill amending the constitution to include website guidelines. The association was formalising its web presence as the decade closed.

In the recordSGA Records: Bill 99-10-F, 15 Sep 1999

28 September1999

A senior awards banquet and hall of distinguished seniors

Bill 99-5-F established a senior awards banquet and a hall of distinguished seniors, with a companion bill creating an ad hoc committee to run the event. A Meet Your Dean reception bill passed through the same September meetings.

In the recordSGA Records: Bill 99-5-F, 28 Sep 1999

12 October1999

Students vote for R&B acts

SGA ran a student vote on Rhythm & Blues concert programming for campus, reported by the Herald under "Students Vote for R&B."

In the recordHerald 75:13, 12 Oct 1999

26 October1999

Congress asked WKU to keep Jerry Wilder

Resolution 99-1-F requested that Jerry Wilder remain vice president of Student Affairs. The Herald reported the following week that SGA members opposed the move in Student Affairs.

In the recordSGA Records: Resolution 99-1-F, 26 Oct 1999

2 November1999campus

Topline, a toll-free campus activity line

Resolution 99-4-F proposed creating a toll-free activity phone line called Topline. The same weeks produced resolutions on WKU banners and suggestion boxes in residence halls.

In the recordSGA Records: Resolution 99-4-F, 2 Nov 1999

4 November1999

Members took the Student Affairs fight public

The Herald reported that Student Government Association members opposed the administrative move in Student Affairs. The story followed the congress's resolution asking that Vice President Jerry Wilder be retained.

In the recordHerald 75:20, 4 Nov 1999

11 November1999

SGA endorsed ending Flip Friday

A fall resolution endorsed the schedule proposed by the Class Schedule Review Committee to do away with Flip Friday. It was the association's formal word on one of the era's odder scheduling experiments.

In the recordSGA Records: Resolution 99-F, 11 Nov 1999

18 November1999

Keep our voice: a rally at Wetherby

About fifty students gathered outside the Wetherby Administration Building to urge the university to retain both the Vice President of Student Affairs and the Dean of Student Life positions, chanting "It's not your choice. Keep our voice." The SGA's own account said president Ransdell appreciated how the students conducted themselves and would keep an open mind.

In the recordWKU SGA site, V.P. of Student Affairs Update (archived 2000)

30 November1999

VarsityBooks.com came to the SGA website

Bill 99-17-F had SGA join VarsityBooks.com and post a link from its website, and a same-day bill extended library hours during finals week. The dot-com partnership marked the first e-commerce deal in the digitised SGA record.

In the recordSGA Records: Bill 99-17-F, 30 Nov 1999

2000

Provide-A-Ride in full operation

During this year SGA ran Provide-A-Ride as a free service giving safe and sober rides anywhere in the Bowling Green and campus area on Thursday and Friday nights from 11 p.m. to 2 a.m. A fifteen-passenger blue van answered calls within about fifteen minutes, and all a rider needed was a valid Western ID.

In the recordWKU SGA site, Provide-A-Ride (archived 2000)

22 February2000

The faculty evaluations campaign opens

President Amanda Coates opened a campaign to publish faculty evaluations as a tool for students choosing professors, starting with a February 22 meeting with the university president and the Faculty Senate chair. The SGA published a step-by-step timeline running through a March 23 presentation to the full Faculty Senate, saying it did not want to win the tool at the expense of unnecessarily upsetting faculty.

In the recordWKU SGA site, Faculty Evaluations (archived 2000)

28 March2000

Martin and Wright battle to succeed Coates

The Herald reported that Cassie Martin and Duan Wright were competing to succeed Amanda Coates as SGA president in the spring election.

In the recordHerald 75:47, 28 Mar 2000

4 April2000

Resolution 00-2-S: publish the evaluations

Resolution 00-2-S, authored by Amanda J. Coates and Adam Howard and sponsored by the Legislative Research Committee, asked the Faculty Senate to approve a mandatory SGA-sponsored faculty evaluation to be published beginning in fall 2000. Its attached questionnaire asked practical questions such as whether an instructor takes attendance, offers extra credit or gives comprehensive finals.

In the recordWKU SGA site, Resolution 00-2-S (archived 2000)

4 April2000

SGA proposed its own faculty evaluations

Resolution 00-2-S proposed creating an SGA faculty evaluation to help students select courses, reviving an idea the congress had pushed since the mid-1990s. It is the last piece of spring 2000 legislation in the digitised collection.

In the recordSGA Records: Resolution 00-2-S, 4 Apr 2000

11 April2000

Two tickets make their case to succeed Coates

In the campaign's final week the Herald covered both tickets on the ballot to succeed Coates: Duan Wright with running mate Dwight Campbell, and Cassie Martin with running mate Leslie Bedo, each laying out a platform on the SGA's current issues.

In the recordHerald 75:51, 11 Apr 2000

18 April2000

Martin elected; faculty evaluations move forward

As Coates's term ended, the Herald's post-election coverage reported Cassie Martin had won the SGA presidency, running an opinion piece titled "Cassie Martin Must Stand Up on Tough Issues," and separately confirmed the SGA-sponsored faculty evaluations Coates's administration had pushed would be conducted and published starting that fall.

In the recordHerald 75:53, 18 Apr 2000

14 April2000

Martin-Bedo ticket won SGA presidency

Students elected Cassie Martin, a junior from Glasgow, as SGA president for 2000-2001, a post that also made her the student representative on Western's Board of Regents. Her ticket with vice presidential candidate Leslie Bedo defeated Duan Wright and Dwight Campbell by 654 votes to 541 in the Thursday election. In the only other contested race, Amy Caswell defeated Billy Lyons 706 to 461 for finance vice president, while Adam Howard and Leslie McClard ran unopposed for the administration and public relations vice presidencies.

SGA Congress opened its fall 2000 session

SGA's congress held its first meeting of the fall semester on Tuesday, August 29 at 5 p.m. in Downing University Center room 305. The body met every Tuesday during the semester, and the organization invited students to pick up membership applications in the SGA office on the first floor of DUC.

27 October2000

Regents raised athletics fee over Martin's dissent

The Board of Regents voted 8-2 to raise the $16 student athletic fee by $40 in January 2001 and another $40 in fall 2001, to fund a Diddle Arena renovation, a larger football budget for WKU's move to the Gateway Conference, and the athletic department's budget shortfall. Student Regent Cassie Martin and Faculty Regent Mary Ellen Miller cast the two votes against. Martin said she understood the need for the funding but questioned the timing and the amount, and disagreed with raising student fees in the middle of an academic year.

WKU took student health service back in-house

WKU announced it would return to self-operation of its campus student health service after its contractor, Collegiate Health Care, notified employees it would be out of business at the end of the day. The university hired the clinic's 17 employees on a temporary basis through the end of the spring semester, and the vice president for Student Affairs promised students would see no reduction in health services.

2001-02

Leslie Bedo (president)

13 entries · 50 index lines

18 August2001

Bedo questions timing of 9 percent tuition increase, then votes for it

WKU's Board of Regents voted on Friday, August 17 to raise tuition 9 percent starting in fall 2002, the first tuition hike in university history devoted entirely to faculty and staff pay. Student Regent Leslie Bedo said she was troubled that the vote came before students officially began fall classes, telling the board it sent a message that the university would slide the increase through before students could respond. Despite her concerns, Bedo joined the unanimous vote approving the increase, which raised in-state undergraduate tuition $138 a semester, from $1,422 to $1,560.

In the recordDaily News, 18 Aug 2001

7 September2001campus

Regents approve $32.5 million Diddle Arena bond deal funded by student athletics fee

The Board of Regents approved an agreement with the City of Bowling Green to sell up to $32.5 million in bonds to renovate E.A. Diddle Arena, with the university repaying the debt service through its student athletics fee. Planned improvements included air conditioning, new seating, luxury boxes, expanded parking and a pedway from new parking areas to the arena. The renovation was scheduled to run from April to September 2002.

In the recordWKU News, 7 Sep 2001

13 September2001campus

Students organize candlelight vigil after September 11 attacks

Two days after the September 11 attacks, WKU held a student-organized candlelight vigil at the Ivan Wilson Fine Arts Center Amphitheater as part of a slate of campus responses. The university also planned a faculty forum at Van Meter Auditorium, opened the Faculty House for reflection and counseling, created a condolences message board to send to New York and Washington, and scheduled a blood drive for September 27.

In the recordWKU News, 13 Sep 2001

Bedo presses parking issue after WKU land purchase collapses

Negotiations for WKU to buy the Forest Park Trailer Park for 400 to 500 new parking spaces broke down over price, even as the Diddle Arena renovation was set to eliminate about 200 spaces permanently. SGA President Leslie Bedo said several regents had voted to increase the student athletics fee on the basis that student parking would grow, and that the promised parking expansion had been put on hold. She argued more students parked on campus than attended basketball games and called more parking imperative.

2002-03

Jamie Sears (president)

11 entries · 42 index lines

22 August2002campus

Record enrollment of 17,500 strains campus

Western opened the fall with enrollment ballooning to 17,500, nearly 1,000 more students than the year before and a 20 percent increase since 1997. President Gary Ransdell warned that growth would be "painful" amid decreased state funding, and the Board of Regents approved a 10.4 percent tuition increase for 2003-04.

In the recordHerald, 22 Aug 2002

19 September2002

Members demand answers on missing gazebo money

SGA members Brooke Smith, Dana Lockhart and Sam Stinson petitioned congress over $28,000 they said was unaccounted for, including about $5,000 that a April 2001 bill had set aside to build an on-campus gazebo that never appeared. President Jamie Sears said of the gazebo fund, "I have absolutely no idea where that money went." The petition was withdrawn after the executive council formed an ad hoc financial review committee.

In the recordHerald, 19 Sep 2002

24 September2002

Herald editorial blasts SGA over 'Gazebo-Gate'

The Herald's 11-member editorial board attacked SGA leaders over what it called "Gazebo-Gate," saying the money had gone to computers for the SGA office instead of the promised gazebo. It called leaders' ignorance about the missing money "shameful" and challenged Sears by name to "do her job" and provide real answers, writing that "I don't know" did not cut it.

In the recordHerald, 24 Sep 2002

October2002

Gazebo funds traced to SGA general fund

Vice president of finance Ross Pruitt reported that the $13,000 SGA had put toward the gazebo mistakenly went back into the organization's general fund and was spent on other things, including computers for SGA. Sears said she and former student activities director Scott Taylor decided over the summer where the leftover budget money would go, with other executive council members consulted by email. Pruitt said leaders from the past two administrations shared the blame, saying "I didn't do my homework."

In the recordHerald, 1 Oct 2002

24 October2002

Congress votes down enrollment cap resolution

SGA congress rejected by a large margin a resolution asking Western to implement an enrollment cap, with Sears among those calling the measure too drastic. The failed proposal argued the university and state budgets had not kept pace with enrollment growth from 14,543 students in 1997 to about 17,770. Provost Barbara Burch and President Ransdell both said a cap was not the best answer to the growth problem.

In the recordHerald, 24 Oct 2002

5 December2002

Three resolutions pass on faculty pay, enrollment, parking

SGA passed two resolutions responding to a shortage of 75 faculty members and the lowest-paid faculty in the state, asking that unbudgeted tuition surplus money, about $800,000 that year, be used to hire faculty, and encouraging President Ransdell to create a task force on enrollment. A third resolution requested a change to the policy that gave Hilltopper Athletic Foundation donors student parking spaces, including the Grise Hall lot, at basketball games.

In the recordHerald, 5 Dec 2002

6 February2003

Freshman committee appointments tabled

SGA tabled Sears's proposal to appoint three freshmen, Tim Howard, Katie Dawson and Robert Watkins, as the student members of a joint University Senate and SGA enrollment growth committee. Sears said she picked freshmen so they could serve the committee's expected two to three year life, but critics including associate justice Dana Lockhart said the appointments would make it hard for SGA to be taken seriously.

In the recordHerald, 6 Feb 2003

4 March2003

SGA joins Frankfort rally against budget cuts

About 200 students from six public universities rallied at the state Capitol against cuts to higher education, after the Kentucky House passed a budget cutting Western's funding by more than $1 million. Western sent a delegation of roughly 20 people including SGA members, organized through the board of Kentucky's student body presidents. Sears said 17 people "took the initiative to get on the bus."

In the recordHerald, 4 Mar 2003

4 March2003

Congress puts $3 radio fee referendum on ballot

SGA unanimously approved a bill placing a referendum on the April 2-3 general election ballot letting students vote on a $3 student fee for campus radio station Revolution 91.7-WWHR, which was operating on a $7,000 budget unchanged since 1998. Executive vice president John Bradley, who championed the measure, said it would empower students and boost voter turnout. A yes vote would send the fee recommendation to the Board of Regents for a final decision.

In the recordHerald, 4 Mar 2003

8 April2003

Bradley elected president; 2,014 vote

A total of 2,014 students voted in the spring SGA election, with results announced shortly after 1 a.m. Friday by chief justice Holly Skidmore. Paducah junior John Bradley won the presidency unopposed with 1,662 votes, Patti Johnson beat Dana Lockhart 1,185 to 685 for executive vice president, and Jessica Martin beat Shawn Peavie 1,056 to 686 for vice president of administration. The $3 WWHR radio fee referendum passed 1,066 to 765 and moved to the Board of Regents.

In the recordHerald, 8 Apr 2003

29 April2003

SGA closes year after 55 pieces of legislation

SGA held its last meeting of the year on April 22, having heard and debated more than 55 pieces of legislation, including a resolution that earmarked funds for new benches across campus. Sears counted the Frankfort rally among the year's greatest accomplishments, and the Revolution 91.7 fee measure stood as the first student referendum in SGA history, awaiting a final Board of Regents vote on May 9. President-elect Bradley said the high election turnout was the semester's best moment and pledged to fight student apathy the next year.

In the recordHerald, 29 Apr 2003

2003-04

John Bradley (president)

11 entries · 49 index lines

19 August2003

Bradley opens the year with cost, safety and involvement goals

New SGA president John Bradley opened the fall by naming low education costs his first goal and warning that fees for the proposed Greek Village should not be passed to the whole student body. SGA created an Ambassador Council to visit student organizations weekly, and planned its first forum of the semester on campus safety, an issue Bradley had worked on as a member of the Campus Safety Task Force formed after the death of freshman Katie Autry. The first congress meeting of the semester was set for August 26 in Downing University Center.

In the recordHerald, 19 Aug 2003

25 September2003

SGA lines up against plus/minus grading

SGA members voiced concern at their Tuesday meeting over a plus/minus grading system proposed in the University Senate by economics professor Brian Strow. Bradley said he planned to oppose it, reporting that the state's other student body presidents had urged him to fight it, and the Academic Affairs committee prepared a student questionnaire on the change. Chief Justice Troy Ransdell argued the system would penalize students who scored best.

In the recordHerald, 25 Sep 2003

30 October2003

Congress urges students to vote as grading petition circulates

SGA unanimously passed a resolution recommending that Western students vote in the November 4 state election and research the candidates' stands on higher education, suspending the bylaws so it could pass before the vote. Members also reported that the petition against plus/minus grading had gathered 350 signatures with more petitions in circulation, and SGA planned a Homecoming tent on the Downing University Center south lawn.

In the recordHerald, 30 Oct 2003

2004

The Constitutional Convention rebuilds the body

Three branches - Executive Cabinet, Senate and Judicial Council - drawn from the student body at large. The most consequential clause is the quietest: every enrolled student became a member of SGA with the right to vote in its elections.

In the recordWKU SGA history

29 January2004

SGA organizes for a higher education rally in Frankfort

SGA prepared to join student governments from across Kentucky at a February 5 rally at the state Capitol against cuts to higher education funding, with slogans such as "Don't Balance the Budget on Our Backs" and students asked to wear backpacks. Congress approved $650 for transportation and reserved 47 spots for the trip. Bradley conceded change that year might be "unreasonable" to expect but said rallying could affect the future.

In the recordHerald, 29 Jan 2004

5 February2004

SGA budget frozen as Western absorbs $5.6 million in cuts

SGA announced at its Tuesday meeting that its budget, along with the Campus Activities Board's, had been informally frozen while Western worked out how to cut $5.6 million ordered by Gov. Ernie Fletcher's administration. SGA held $65,309.52 in its 2003-04 budget at the time, plus about $7,400 in an Aramark contract and foundation accounts that were not affected. Bradley said congress could still pass legislation requiring money, with the director of student activities deciding whether funds were available.

In the recordHerald, 5 Feb 2004

18 March2004

Nick Todd elected SGA president as 1,232 students vote

Vice president of finance Nick Todd won the SGA presidency with 772 votes to Jessica Martin's 424, in a two-day online election in which 1,232 students voted. Katie Dawson won executive vice president with 778 votes and Evelina Petkova won administrative vice president with 692, with the first elected senate under the new constitution chosen at the same time. Bradley said he was disappointed by the turnout, and the winners were set to be sworn in at the SGA banquet on April 27.

In the recordHerald, 18 Mar 2004

18 March2004

Congress buys stepping stones for muddy campus paths

SGA unanimously approved legislation allocating $200 from its campus improvements account for stepping stones near Mass Media and Technology Hall, Tate Page Hall and Southwest Hall, where student foot traffic had worn dirt and mud paths. The bill's authors, Shawn Peavie and Sarah Cecil, said sidewalks had been considered but were too expensive. In the same meeting a straw poll on a proposed dorm Internet service fee drew 3 votes in support, 11 against and 11 abstentions.

In the recordHerald, 18 Mar 2004

8 April2004

SGA races to spend its remaining $45,000

With about $45,000 left of its original $105,000 budget for 2003-04, SGA moved to spend the remainder before the semester ended, since leftover funds would go to offset budget cuts across the university rather than carry over. Officers attributed the surplus partly to frugality during the spring budget freeze, and Todd suggested putting the money toward campus improvements such as benches or shuttle shelters. SGA also sponsored a dining services forum that week with Auxiliary Services and Dining Services officials.

In the recordHerald, 8 Apr 2004

15 April2004

Disputed 9-8 vote clouds the first speaker of the senate election

Congress elected constitution author Robert Watkins as the first speaker of the senate by 9 votes to 8 over Brittany Fausey, with 17 of 20 members present voting. The result was immediately questioned because the new constitution was unclear on whether two-thirds of eligible voters or of total membership was required, and three members present were barred from voting under a judicial council ruling. Martin warned of a "semester of frustration" if the dispute was not resolved at the year's final meeting, while Fausey declined to challenge the result.

In the recordHerald, 15 Apr 2004

20 April2004

The president-elect is investigated before he takes office

The Herald reported an investigation into missing funds from an SGA dining account. Articles of impeachment were drafted against the president-elect's existing finance post but the judicial council found the two-week process could not finish before the term ended. Because state law governs the student regent seat, the new constitution required a separate special election to fill it.

In the recordHerald, April 2004

2004-05

Patti Johnson (president)

11 entries · 46 index lines

20 April2004

SGA judicial council fielded impeachment bid against president-elect Todd

Days before new officers were due to be sworn in on April 27, SGA's judicial council found that $611 was missing from the SGA Aramark Dining Dollars account, which had started the academic year with $5,000 and had about $1,200 left. Senator Josh Collins drafted articles of impeachment against Todd's outgoing vice presidency of finance, but the council ruled a two-week impeachment process could not be completed before he left that office regardless. Only Todd, outgoing president John Bradley and adviser Charley Pride held cards to the account.

In the recordHerald, 20 Apr 2004 - "SGA President-Elect Under Investigation" (Wayback)

24 August2004

SGA president Nick Todd resigned amid funds investigation

Nick Todd, elected SGA president in March with 772 of 1,232 votes cast, submitted his resignation in July, citing personal conflicts within the association. The former vice president of finance had come under investigation in April for the misuse of more than $600 in an SGA Dining Dollars account. Executive Vice President Katie Dawson acted as president until a new election set for Sept. 14-15.

In the recordHerald, 24 Aug 2004

26 August2004

Internal audit recommended Todd repay SGA money

WKU's Office of the Internal Auditor reported that $872 in questionable purchases were made from the SGA Dining Dollars account between August 2003 and May 2004, mostly small buys at campus restaurants with no receipts. The report recommended that Todd reimburse the money, plus $71 for a charge made with the SGA purchasing card after a spring break car rental. Campus police determined no police action was necessary.

In the recordHerald, 26 Aug 2004

2 September2004

Patti Johnson emerged as the only candidate in the special election

At a meeting for students interested in running in SGA's September special elections, Marion senior Patti Johnson, the previous year's executive vice president, was the only student to show interest in the presidency. She said she decided to run because of "the turmoil within the organization." Applications were also taken for the 23 open senate seats ahead of online voting on Sept. 14-15.

In the recordHerald, 2 Sep 2004

21 September2004

Dean of Student Life contradicted Todd on sanctions

Howard Bailey, dean of Student Life, said Todd had been sanctioned by judicial affairs in July over the alleged misuse of university funds, disputing Todd's public claim that losing access to the Dining Dollars card was the only action taken against him. Bailey said federal privacy law barred him from revealing the sanctions. Todd acknowledged he was also no longer allowed to handle any SGA funds.

In the recordHerald via Wayback, 21 Sep 2004

23 September2004

SGA approved a $110,000 budget

SGA approved a $110,000 budget for the 2004-05 academic year, up from $105,000 the year before, despite earlier expectations of a $15,000 to $17,000 cut under the university's budget reduction plan. Most of the money went toward operating fees, campus improvements and organizational aid. Adviser Charley Pride credited steady enrollment growth for the increase.

In the recordHerald via Wayback, 23 Sep 2004

28 September2004

Johnson sworn in as president after winning 1,291 votes

Patti Johnson was sworn in as SGA president at the organization's fall reception on Sept. 23, after receiving 1,291 votes in the uncontested online election held Sept. 14 and 15. The 23 new senators were seated in the first fall senate election held under SGA's new constitution. Johnson was due to be sworn in as student regent at the Oct. 29 Board of Regents meeting.

In the recordHerald via Wayback, 28 Sep 2004

16 November2004

SGA proposed a faculty evaluation pilot to the University Senate

SGA prepared to propose a two-year pilot program to the University Senate that would add five questions on matters such as office hours, punctuality and textbook use to faculty evaluations and post the answers on TopNet for students. Senator Josh Collins wrote the proposal with Troy Ransdell and Morgan Phelps after SGA scaled back an earlier push to release entire evaluations. The questions could appear on evaluations at the end of spring 2005 if the study was approved.

In the recordHerald via Wayback, 16 Nov 2004

17 March2005

Katie Dawson elected SGA president for 2005-06

Executive Vice President Katie Dawson defeated Senate Speaker Josh Collins 1,268 to 472 in the spring election's only contested race to become the next SGA president. Students also passed a package of 40 constitutional amendments 1,193 to 262 and voted 1,019 to 669 to ask the Board of Regents to institute a $9 per semester Talisman yearbook fee. Mason Stevenson and Melissa Paris won the two vice presidencies unopposed, and all 25 senate candidates on the ballot were elected.

In the recordHerald via Wayback, 17 Mar 2005

31 March2005campus

Goodrum found not guilty in Katie Autry murder trial

A jury in Owensboro found Lucas Goodrum, 23, of Scottsville not guilty of the May 2003 murder of Pellville freshman Melissa "Katie" Autry, who was set on fire in her Poland Hall dorm room and died three days later. The verdict came March 21 after three hours of deliberation, ending a three-week trial that had been moved from Warren County. Stephen Soules had earlier pleaded guilty to murder, rape, sodomy, arson and robbery and expected life in prison.

In the recordHerald via Wayback, 31 Mar 2005

14 April2005

SGA funded the Buy-A-Book program

SGA passed legislation 22-2 on April 5 allocating $2,000 to the Buy-A-Book program, and the University Bookstore pledged to match the amount. The bill by senator Katharine Pettit was amended unanimously to help 20 students who needed financial assistance buying textbooks instead of 10. Recipients were to be chosen by the academic affairs committee based on a required essay and need.

2005-06

Katie Dawson (president)

11 entries · 42 index lines

2005

The plus/minus grading fight

An Institutional Research report on plus and minus grading, a protest broadside, a post-winter-term student survey and an SGA handbook all survive - one of the few academic-policy campaigns documented from research through to public agitation.

In the recordTopSCHOLAR - Documents/Reports

20 November2005campus

WKU launched its centennial celebration

Western kicked off a 14-month celebration of its 1906 founding on Saturday, Nov. 19, dedicating three new campus landmarks including Centennial Plaza. SGA President Katie Dawson spoke at the plaza dedication, offering her own meaning of the school slogan "The Spirit Makes the Master."

In the recordDaily News, 20 Nov 2005

8 December2005

SGA closed the fall with 10 pieces of legislation

The Herald reported that SGA passed 10 pieces of legislation in the fall semester, fewer than in previous fall semesters. Its legislation brought bikes, a cancer documentary and iPods to Western. The same issue reported that a senator named Johnson had been elected the new speaker of the senate.

In the recordHerald, 8 Dec 2005 (via Wayback)

February2006

SGA took up a proposed $45 construction fee

At its first regular meeting of the spring semester, SGA discussed a proposed $45-per-semester fee to pay for a campus-wide wireless network, a new health center and renovations to the Ivan Wilson Center for Fine Arts. President Katie Dawson supported the fee, and Western's chief financial officer estimated it would raise about $1.4 million a year.

In the recordDaily News, 1 Feb 2006

8 February2006

Ransdell asked SGA for a resolution backing the fee

WKU President Gary Ransdell came to the SGA meeting and urged senators to pass a resolution supporting the proposed $45 fee, which the Board of Regents would vote on April 7. Dawson sat on that board as student regent, and SGA officers said a supporting resolution was likely within a few weeks.

In the recordDaily News, 8 Feb 2006

3 March2006

Executive vice president aired an internal rift

Executive Vice President Mason Stevenson read a letter at the SGA meeting saying some members trying to protect their political interests had "thwarted" SGA's mission to improve Western. The letter outlined his concerns about relations between the executive and legislative branches.

In the recordHerald, 3 Mar 2006 (via Wayback)

16 March2006

Senate put $2,000 toward SGA's 40th anniversary party

Two bills devoting $2,000 to a party for SGA's 40th anniversary passed unanimously at the group's Tuesday meeting. The Herald reported the organization planned a campus-wide party to mark four decades of student government at Western.

In the recordHerald, 16 Mar 2006 (via Wayback)

8 April2006

Regents approved the fee; Dawson's senior exemption failed

The Board of Regents voted 9-1 to approve the $46-per-semester construction fee, with Dawson abstaining, and rejected 10-1 her proposal to exempt next year's seniors, an idea she had raised at a student forum the week before. Dawson said that although she supported the fee, she could not vote for it with so many seniors counting on the exemption.

In the recordDaily News, 8 Apr 2006

13 April2006

Rob Watkins elected SGA president

Bowling Green senior Robert Watkins won the online election for SGA president after spending more than a week seeking supporters who would vote on TopNet. He defeated Berea junior Kara Ratliff, and the results were announced Tuesday at a crowded Revolution 91.

In the recordHerald, 13 Apr 2006 (via Wayback)

20 April2006

Executive board issued its first veto of the year

After the Tuesday senate meeting, the SGA executive board vetoed a bill that would have financed community- and campus-oriented projects through civic engagement grants, the first time it exercised its veto power that year. The Herald reported the grants were "a reality for only about 30 minutes" and that time restraints halted an appeal of the veto.

In the recordHerald, 20 Apr 2006 (via Wayback)

20 April2006

Herald editorial attacked SGA misspending

A Herald editorial titled "SGA misspending" said members should not have to be "motivated by a giveaway to show up for meetings." It noted that the opinion page had devoted considerable space in recent weeks to both positive and negative aspects of SGA, which it said could and should be an important organization on campus.

In the recordHerald, 20 Apr 2006 (via Wayback)

2006-07

Robert Watkins (president)

12 entries

5 September2006

Fifth SGA opened its year, swore in eight senators

At the first meeting of that year's Senate, called to order with 8 of 18 senators present, eight new senators were sworn in: Chris Anderson, Diane DeRosa-Reynolds, Leah Keys, Amanda Kidd, Suzie Moghaddam, Seth Norman, Tori Theiss and Christa Wilcox. Administrative Vice President Amanda Allen reported $30,000 in organizational aid for the year, and the senate nominated committee heads and Judicial Council members, including Matt Holland as chief justice. The minutes record Jeanne L. Johnson delivering the executive vice president's report.

In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 5 Sep 2006 (TopSCHOLAR)Read it here

24 October2006

SGA tightened its budget after leaving $24,000 unspent

The Herald reported that SGA had left about $24,000 of its $115,000 budget unspent at the end of 2005-06, money that returned to Western's general fund. Administrative Vice President Amanda Allen said SGA was cutting money from areas where it went unspent, adding almost $10,000 to organizational aid and $3,000 to the miscellaneous fund. Allen called the previous year a bad budgetary year but also a learning year.

In the recordHerald, 24 Oct 2006 (Wayback)

25 October2006

SGA-run referendum showed students favored the I-A football move

In an online referendum SGA arranged alongside the homecoming queen election, 64.6 percent of voting students, 1,095, supported WKU's proposed move to Division I-A football, with 600 against. A total of 2,136 students voted in the poll, and the 1,695 who answered the football question represented about 9 percent of enrollment. SGA President Rob Watkins, who held the student seat on the Board of Regents, said the poll would help him define a position but noted the homecoming tie-in likely drew football-friendly voters.

In the recordDaily News, 25 Oct 2006

2 November2006

SGA senate unanimously passed a resolution backing the I-A move

SGA members unanimously passed a resolution saying they supported the move to Division I-A football, following the student referendum result. Watkins, as student regent and SGA president, still would not say what his own position was before the regents' vote.

In the recordHerald front page, 5 Nov 2006 (Wayback)

28 November2006

Watkins resigned as SGA president and student regent

SGA's own senate minutes record that president and student regent Rob Watkins's resignation was formally read into the meeting at the senate's regularly scheduled Tuesday session, with senators told Jeanne Johnson would be sworn in as president at the Dec. 5 Winter Banquet. Senators had voiced concerns about Watkins at an unannounced 10 p.m. meeting the evening before. A Herald front-page account (Wayback, 2 Dec 2006) covered the same resignation but gave the date as 30 November; this entry follows the primary senate minutes, which date the reading of the resignation to 28 November, leaving students without representation on Western's governing board for at least a month.

In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 28 Nov 2006 (TopSCHOLAR)Read it here

28 November2006

Senate passed Books for Africa bill and a printing-quota resolution

At the same Nov. 28 meeting where Watkins's resignation was read into the record, the senate unanimously passed Bill 11-06-F, sponsored by Lucas Humble, to collect textbooks the university bookstore would not buy back and send them to Africa. Senators also unanimously passed Resolution 08-06-F, sponsored by Seth Norman, backing a university study of a computer-lab printing quota after administrators told SGA's Student Affairs committee how many pages some students were printing.

In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 28 Nov 2006 (TopSCHOLAR)Read it here

28 November2006campus

Senate heard Douglas Keen Hall was next for renovation

In a University Committees report to the senate, a member reported that the Student Life Foundation had discussed campus housing renovations and that Douglas Keen Hall would be the next residence hall to be renovated, within about three years. The same report covered a Budget Council discussion of rolling several student organizations' budgets, including SGA's, into the university's base budget.

In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 28 Nov 2006 (TopSCHOLAR)Read it here

5 December2006

Senate tabled two resolutions for lack of quorum at Winter Banquet meeting

With 16 of 31 senators present, the senate lacked quorum to act on Resolution 09-06-F on vending machine prices and Resolution 10-06-F on special events parking, so both were tabled. Executive Vice President was listed vacant, since Jeanne Johnson had moved into the presidency after Robert Watkins's resignation. The Judicial Council reported meeting on the time requirements for the student regent seat. Winners of the Outstanding Senator and Outstanding Committee Member awards, chosen by secret ballot, were announced later that evening at the Winter Banquet.

In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 5 Dec 2006 (TopSCHOLAR)Read it here

27 January2007

Fill-in SGA leader Jeanne Johnson challenged tuition plan at regents meeting

The Board of Regents approved a 7.8 percent tuition increase for 2007-08, bringing tuition and fees to $6,417 a year including the higher athletics fee. Jeanne Johnson, a junior economics and finance major from Marion described as a fill-in for the former SGA president, opposed the size of the increase for online and distance-learning courses, though she had no vote. She said 'We know tuition increases are inevitable' but argued distance learners should not carry that burden.

In the recordDaily News, 27 Jan 2007

February2007

Johnson won the student regent election; SGA seated a full senate

Jeanne Johnson, SGA president and Marion junior, won the special election for Western's vacant student regent seat with 688 votes, 41 percent of ballots cast. The same Herald issue reported that SGA began the spring semester with its first full senate attendance since fall 2004.

In the recordHerald front page, 3 Feb 2007 (Wayback)

24 April2007

Provost rejected plus/minus grading; Johnson credited SGA's campaign

Provost Barbara Burch told the University Senate she would not implement the plus/minus grading system the senate had passed 36-23 in March. SGA President Jeanne Johnson said she was grateful for the decision, noting SGA had raised awareness and led student protests, and pledged that students would keep fighting if the issue returned. She said 'I'm confident that the students' opinions have been expressed.'

In the recordHerald, 24 Apr 2007 (Wayback)

2 May2007

SGA banquet closed the year and swore in 2007-08 officers

At its annual banquet on May 1, SGA presented awards and swore in officers for 2007-08, with Jeanne Lynn Johnson of Marion becoming the new SGA president and student regent and receiving the Dero Downing Award. Johnathon Boles of Elizabethtown became executive vice president, Kayla Shelton speaker of the Student Senate, and Cherieth Lea Lineweaver administrative vice president. Amanda Beth Allen received the Charles A. Keown Award, SGA's highest honor.

In the recordWKU News, 2 May 2007 (Wayback)

2007-08

Jeanne Johnson (president)

13 entries · 47 index lines

13 September2007

Fall senate election drew 25 candidates for 20 seats

SGA reported record interest in its fall senate election, with 25 students running for 20 available seats, the most applications President Jeanne Johnson said she had ever seen. Elections were set for Sept. 19 and 20 through TopNet, with an informational table in Downing University Center on Sept. 18. Public relations director Liz Goddard said more competition would produce harder workers.

In the recordHerald, 13 Sep 2007

2 October2007

SGA co-sponsored mock gubernatorial election

SGA and the Office of the Secretary of State co-sponsored a mock gubernatorial election at Centennial Mall as part of Secretary of State Trey Grayson's Civic Literacy Initiative of Kentucky. The 127 students who voted chose challenger Steve Beshear over incumbent Gov. Ernie Fletcher, 74 to 50. President Jeanne Johnson and Executive Vice President Johnathon Boles called the event a success.

In the recordHerald, 2 Oct 2007

18 October2007

Resolution demanded more state funding for Western

At its Oct. 9 meeting SGA passed a resolution asking the state government to appropriate more money to Western, which had received 54 percent of the funding the Council on Postsecondary Education recommended for fiscal year 2008. President Jeanne Johnson argued that tuition increases to cover the shortfall hurt students. The resolution stated Western needed the full recommended amount to meet its 2020 educational goals.

In the recordHerald, 18 Oct 2007

18 October2007

SGA organized Walk Out Western budget protest

SGA sponsored Walk Out Western, asking students to leave class at 12:20 p.m. on Oct. 25 for a rally at the Colonnade to protest state budget cuts, with empty seats meant as a message to Frankfort legislators. President Gary Ransdell said he could not condone students walking out of class and doubted a single-campus protest would affect state funding. Johnson said other state universities declined to join but were watching how it worked at Western.

In the recordHerald, 18 Oct 2007

25 October2007

Committee proposed $1,995 educational video subscription

SGA's Academic Affairs Committee, chaired by Drew Eclov, prepared legislation to buy a roughly $1,995 subscription to United Streaming, a Discovery Channel-owned site with about 45,000 educational video clips that Eclov called a version of YouTube for higher education. The committee planned to survey students and professors before bringing it to a vote. SGA also scheduled a vote on a resolution placing $1,000 in a field trip fund to support learning outside the classroom.

In the recordHerald, 25 Oct 2007

November2007

Athletics director asked SGA for help on football attendance

Athletics Director Wood Selig came to the SGA meeting to ask senators for ideas on getting more students to football games as Western moved to the Football Bowl Subdivision, which required an average attendance of 15,000 to keep bowl eligibility. Senators suggested advertising on Western's website and Facebook rather than email, and later game times. Executive Vice President Johnathon Boles, who sat on a faculty advisory committee for athletics, arranged the consultation.

In the recordHerald, 1 Nov 2007

15 November2007

SGA planned Listen Up Legislators lobbying campaign

SGA began laying groundwork for Listen Up Legislators, a spring lobbying campaign in which senators would meet legislators one-on-one in Frankfort to push for university funding, after the Council on Postsecondary Education recommended a $174 million increase for public universities. Chief of staff Skylar Jordan said the traditional February rally had not worked, pointing to Western receiving only 54 percent of the recommended increase. Other state student governments expressed interest in coordinating lobbying dates.

In the recordHerald, 15 Nov 2007

31 January2008

Spring session opened with ONE Campus bill

At its first spring meeting on Jan. 29, SGA introduced legislation by Senators Matt Vaughan and Doug Tate asking the senate to recognize Western as a ONE Campus, part of the national campaign against global AIDS and extreme poverty. SGA also released its spring schedule, including Listen Up Legislators on Feb. 14, the Frankfort rally for higher education on Feb. 20 and the annual banquet on April 29. In the semester's opening handout, Executive Vice President Johnathon Boles pointed members to the constitution's purpose of serving the student body equally.

In the recordHerald, 31 Jan 2008

20 February2008

Fifty senators write down what a lobbying trip felt like

After a student rally at the Capitol in Frankfort, dozens of SGA members each filed an individual written reflection, archived one per person. The richest first-person source in the entire collection.

In the recordTopSCHOLAR - Frankfort rally reflections

April2008

Spring election closed amid low-turnout criticism

Voting for three executive seats and 28 senate seats ended after a one-week campaign that candidates criticized as part of SGA's low-involvement problem; turnout had been 1,424 the year before and 1,376 the year before that. Red Towel Party presidential candidate Tedde Harden promised to rework what he called outdated election codes, while opponent Johnathon Boles agreed campaign time should be extended. President Jeanne Johnson said her administration inherited the codes and had tried new turnout methods, including extra credit for attending the debate.

In the recordHerald, 1 Apr 2008

17 April2008campus

Ransdell announced 9 percent tuition increase

President Gary Ransdell announced at campus forums that he would recommend a 9 percent tuition increase for 2008-09, abandoning a plan to hold increases at 6 percent. The change followed a state budget crisis in which Gov. Steve Beshear ordered a 3 percent cut to postsecondary education in December 2007 and proposed an additional 12 percent, later reduced by the General Assembly to 3 percent. Ransdell said the swing from expected state revenue was about $11 million to $12 million.

In the recordHerald, 17 Apr 2008

24 April2008

Student regent Johnson opposed scale of 9 percent tuition increase

The Board of Regents approved a 9 percent tuition increase for 2008-09 and finalized $2.5 million in cuts to the 2007-08 budget. Louisville regent Larry Zielke moved to cap the increase at 6 percent and push the General Assembly for more funding instead; SGA President and student regent Jeanne Johnson seconded the motion, but it died with only two votes. Johnson also argued the $370,000 budgeted for the Honors College should be reduced, saying the college benefited only 900 students and other students should not have to pay for it.

In the recordHerald 83:51, 29 Apr 2008 - "Regents approve 9 percent tuition increase, finalize 07-08 budget cuts"

18 July2008

Johnson's regent term ended as Boles took the board oath

The Board of Regents read a resolution thanking Jeanne Johnson for her service as the board's student member from April 27, 2007 to July 18, 2008, calling her term one of "able leadership, faithful service, and dedication." Johnathon Boles, who had already been installed as SGA president that spring, took the oath of office as student regent the same day, formally completing the transition between administrations.
