2008-09

Johnathon Boles (president) · Kayla Shelton (president)

11 entries · 41 index lines

4 September2008campus

Shots fired outside Pearce-Ford Tower put dorms on lockdown

Campus police responded to a report of shots fired at about 3 a.m. Saturday in the Pearce-Ford Tower parking lot, where a witness said a man got out of a vehicle, fired a gun and drove away. Police found shell casings but no damage, no one was hurt, and all dorms went into lockdown after the incident.

In the recordHerald, 4 Sep 2008

18 September2008

Fall senate election drew above-average turnout

SGA seated nine new student senators after a two-day fall election in which 18 candidates competed. Seven seats had been open, four reserved for freshmen, and two more opened when two senators resigned the Monday before the vote. A total of 687 students voted, which President Johnathon Boles said was higher than the average for a fall election.

In the recordHerald, 18 Sep 2008

13 November2008

Boles and Smiley appointed to governor's college affordability group

Gov. Steve Beshear appointed SGA President Johnathon Boles and SGA member Kevin Smiley to the student committee of his College Access Work Group, which was charged with recommending ways to make Kentucky higher education more affordable. The two traveled to Frankfort for the committee's first meeting, where they raised the impact of textbook costs, which Boles put at an average of $800 a year.

In the recordDaily News, 13 Nov 2008

19 November2008

Senate voted to launch a Textbook Subsidy Program

The SGA senate voted to contribute $500 to start a Textbook Subsidy Program, an effort developed with the University Bookstore, which pledged another $500, to build an endowment that would lower textbook costs for students. The senate also created a program board of nearly 20 members, including Boles, bookstore representatives and members from each college, to work out funding and distribution.

In the recordDaily News, 19 Nov 2008

4 December2008

SGA made its first mid-year budget cut

Facing a state shortfall that required the university to cut about 4 percent of its budget, SGA cut $4,100 from its $110,000 budget, the first time it had cut its budget in the middle of an academic year. Boles and Administrative Vice President Reagan Gilley chose to cut a $2,600 surplus from the fall retreat and $1,500 from organizational aid, protecting scholarships and Provide-A-Ride. Boles said he was working to get charter buses to send students to a Feb. 3 rally in Frankfort against higher education budget cuts.

In the recordHerald, 4 Dec 2008

29 January2009campus

Ice storm hit campus, injuring a student and closing regional campuses

A winter storm coated campus in ice during the week of Jan. 27, part of the second-largest power outage recorded in Kentucky. A falling tree limb struck a sophomore near Grise Hall, who was treated and released, and WKU canceled classes at its Elizabethtown, Owensboro, Glasgow, Fort Knox and Radcliff campuses as well as evening classes on the main campus. AT&T cell outages kept officials from reaching students by text message.

In the recordHerald, 29 Jan 2009

12 February2009

Judicial Council ordered a special student regent election over executive dissent

After Boles' resignation left the student regent seat empty, the SGA Judicial Council voted 2-1 on Feb. 10 to hold a special election on Feb. 24 and 25. Chief Justice Lisa Kappler cast the dissenting vote, calling the constitution's requirement a gray area, and Executive Vice President Skylar Jordan presented a letter arguing the election was unnecessary. President Kayla Shelton said she supported the council's decision.

In the recordHerald, 12 Feb 2009

12 February2009

Chief Justice Lisa Kappler resigned

SGA Chief Justice Lisa Kappler resigned Thursday night in a letter sent to President Kayla Shelton and student activities director Charley Pride, saying she wanted to spend more time on school and family. Shelton said she hoped the senate would vote on a new chief justice at the next meeting because the special election for student regent was two weeks away.

In the recordHerald, 12 Feb 2009

26 February2009

Reagan Gilley won the special student regent election

Administrative Vice President Reagan Gilley, a Pineville senior, defeated Speaker of the Senate Nate Eaton 477 votes to 224 in the special election for student regent, with 701 students voting. The seat had been vacant for 26 days after former President Johnathon Boles resigned on Jan. 30 for health reasons; Executive Vice President Kayla Shelton had taken his place as president but not as regent.

In the recordHerald, 26 Feb 2009

16 April2009

Kevin Smiley won the SGA presidential election

The Herald reported Kevin Smiley's win in the spring SGA presidential election under the headline "All Smiles, Kevin Smiley Wins Student Government Association Election," ending Kayla Shelton's term as the president who had finished out Johnathon Boles's 2008-09 year. Smiley took office as president and student regent for 2009-10.

In the recordCollege Heights Herald 84:46, 16 Apr 2009

23 April2009

SGA negotiated removal of proposed $30 per-credit-hour fee

SGA and university officials agreed to strike a proposed $30 fee for every credit hour over 15 from the Board of Regents agenda, replacing it with a proposal to raise the add/drop fee from $20 to $50. SGA canceled a planned protest after the compromise, and Student Regent Reagan Gilley called the outcome "really a win-win for everyone."

In the recordHerald, 23 Apr 2009

2009-10

Kevin Smiley (president)

11 entries · 32 index lines

4 September2009

Smiley nominates his brother as chief of staff

SGA President Kevin Smiley announced Danville sophomore Eric Smiley, his brother, as his nominee for chief of staff, a paid voting position on the executive cabinet. Former executive vice president Skylar Baker-Jordan called the nomination "completely unethical," while Smiley said he chose his brother because he had no previous political agenda. The senate was set to vote on all nominations Sept. 8, with a two-thirds majority needed for approval.

In the recordHerald, 4 Sep 2009

15 September2009

Fall election opens; SGA gives $2,000 to Residence Hall Association

At the Sept. 15 senate meeting, Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman reported that SGA gave $2,000 from its budget to the Residence Hall Association. President Kevin Smiley announced that voting in the fall SGA election had started on TopNet, with polls open until Wednesday night and results announced about midnight. Smiley also urged senators to join the Campus Safety Walk, in which participants looked for dimly lit or overgrown areas on campus.

In the recordHerald, 15 Sep 2009

14 October2009

SGA sponsors forum on new tailgating policy

About 30 people attended an SGA-sponsored forum where students and administrators discussed Western's amended tailgating policy, which banned vehicles from campus lawns on game days. Howard Bailey, vice president for student affairs, told students the policy would stay the same, and Speaker of the Senate Wade Pierce suggested tent giveaways to ease the transition. President Kevin Smiley said he was pleased with the attendance and that SGA would keep questioning the policy.

In the recordHerald, 14 Oct 2009

20 October2009

Three senators resign over publications committee appointment

Senators Michel Stephens, Emmett Stephens and Daniel Shaw resigned at the Oct. 20 meeting. Michel Stephens cited President Kevin Smiley's nomination of Greg Capillo to the Student Publications Committee, which helps choose the Herald's editor-in-chief, saying the pick was not based on merit or experience. Smiley called the accusations of favoritism and corruption unfounded and said the seats would stay vacant until he appointed replacements for senate approval.

In the recordHerald, 20 Oct 2009

10 November2009

Judicial Council removes senator for unexcused absences

Chief Justice Stuart Kenderes reported that the Judicial Council removed Senator Theodore Harden, a graduate student from Otisville, N.Y., from SGA for excessive unexcused absences; Harden did not attend the council meeting to defend himself. The council also reviewed Senator Vashae Swope for absences but voted to let her remain. Attendance guidelines were posted in the SGA office window, and Rachel Wilcox was approved as a new senator at the same meeting.

In the recordHerald, 10 Nov 2009

11 December2009campus

WKU begins weighing a smoke-free campus

After the University of Kentucky and the University of Louisville went smoke-free, the Faculty Welfare Committee of Western's University Senate prepared a smoking survey for students, faculty and staff to take in February. SGA President Kevin Smiley said he would encourage the whole campus to take the survey, and President Gary Ransdell said he would look to SGA, the University Senate and Staff Council for direction on any policy.

In the recordHerald, 11 Dec 2009

27 January2010

Two more senators resign; Frankfort rally buses announced

At the Jan. 27 meeting, Aaron Pawley and Eileen Forsythe resigned as senators, Pawley because of a difficult course load and Forsythe because she was studying abroad in England. President Kevin Smiley announced free buses to carry 75 students to a Feb. 9 rally in Frankfort where advocates from Kentucky's public universities would lobby legislators on higher education funding. Western student Colton Jessie was slated to speak at the rally.

In the recordHerald, 27 Jan 2010

2 February2010

SGA organizes trip to Rally for Higher Education

SGA and the Provost's office offered free bus transportation for 75 students to the Rally for Higher Education on Feb. 9 at the Kentucky State Capitol, a year after winter weather derailed the previous attempt. Students who registered through the SGA website received an excused absence, and the rally included a chance to meet lawmakers and hear an address from Gov. Steve Beshear.

In the recordHerald, 2 Feb 2010

22 February2010

Senate passes funding bills for baseball, a sorority event and study abroad

At its Feb. 22 meeting the senate unanimously passed a funding bill and, with single dissents apiece, a bill funding the baseball program and a $1,300 allocation for an Alpha Kappa Alpha event. It also unanimously approved several study-abroad reimbursement bills and confirmed Daniel Shaw as parliamentarian, along with a new Academic Affairs committee chair nominee and a new Student Affairs chair.

In the recordSGA senate minutes, 22 Feb 2010

23 March2010

SGA passes election codes and two funding bills

The senate passed the spring 2010 election codes, a bill giving $500 to the Agriculture Students Striving for Effective Tomorrows conference for high school students, and a bill designating $1,200 for lodging for FIJIs Across America, in which eight Phi Gamma Delta members planned to cycle across the country for Alzheimer's research. Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman reported that all but three approved organizations had received their organizational aid checks.

In the recordHerald, 23 Mar 2010

April2010

Colton Jessie elected SGA president for 2010-11

Bowling Green junior Colton Jessie won the SGA presidency with 63 percent of the vote, taking 726 votes to 424 for Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman, on a platform of sustainability, handicap accessibility and changing the tailgating policy. Kendrick Bryan was re-elected executive vice president with 731 votes to Currie Martin's 415, and Wade Pierce ran unopposed for administrative vice president with 1,016 votes. Results were announced at midnight Wednesday.

In the recordHerald, 1 Apr 2010

2010-11

Colton Jessie (president)

11 entries · 26 index lines

14 September2010

SGA raised scholarship budget to $20,000

After running out of scholarship money the previous year, SGA increased its scholarship budget from $12,000 to $20,000 and lowered general senate funding from $20,000 to $12,000 to cover the change. Study abroad awards were capped at $500 for a semester trip and $250 for a winter or summer term so more students could receive money. SGA also finalized a new study away scholarship for travel inside the country and set aside $400 for it in the winter term.

In the recordHerald, 14 Sep 2010

23 September2010

Twelve senators elected in fall election with 847 voters

Twelve students won seats in the fall senate election, in which 847 total voters cast ballots on TopNet. Keyana Boka, Natalie Broderick and Eppiphanie Benton were elected freshman senators, running unopposed, while 25 students competed for the at-large seats. Winners included Diego Leal Ambriz, who would run for president that spring.

In the recordHerald, 23 Sep 2010

19 November2010

Ransdell brought $49 million DUC renovation plan to SGA

President Gary Ransdell and head architect Jeff Stivers told SGA at its Nov. 16 meeting that officials were moving ahead on a plan to completely renovate Downing University Center at a cost of up to $49 million. Students would pay about $140 extra per year in fees for up to 20 years, and Ransdell promised students would be involved in every decision. SGA had to pass resolutions on the design and fees before the Board of Regents could approve the project.

In the recordHerald, 19 Nov 2010

7 December2010

SGA funds extended library hours for finals week

The senate approved $600 to keep the library open until 2 a.m. during finals week, covering extra staff time and lighting. President Colton Jessie said continuing the service was never in question, calling finals "an important time for students."

In the recordHerald, 7 Dec 2010

10 December2010

Senate tabled DUC resolution over lack of student input

Senators tabled the bill supporting the DUC renovation at the Dec. 7 meeting, saying they had not received enough student input just three weeks after learning of the project. Jessie backed the delay, saying he wanted to hear students' voices before moving forward, even though it pushed SGA's presentation to the Board of Regents from January 21 to April 22. Campus Improvements Chair Kaylee Egerer said many students did not yet know they would pay $140 a year for the project.

In the recordHerald, 10 Dec 2010

11 February2011

Herald reported Greeks held 40 percent of SGA seats

The Herald reported that 21 of SGA's 50 members belonged to Greek organizations, more than 40 percent, while less than 8 percent of the student body was in a fraternity or sorority. Sixteen of the 21 were fraternity men, and two fraternities, Sigma Chi and Lambda Chi Alpha, accounted for nine of them. Officers defended the imbalance, and the story noted SGA's operating budget for 2010-11 was $121,335, drawn from tuition.

In the recordHerald, 11 Feb 2011

22 February2011

SGA unanimously passed DUC renovation resolution

SGA unanimously passed the resolution supporting DUC renovations at its Feb. 22 meeting, the bill's second reading. Project costs were capped at $49,128,545, with a student fee of up to $70 per semester for 20 years and $1.5 million per year from WKU. The resolution, authored by Kaylee Egerer, asked for assurance of a 24-hour study space and called for construction to begin as soon as possible while interest rates were low.

In the recordHerald, 22 Feb 2011

March2011

SGA members joined Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort

SGA members traveled to Frankfort on March 1 for the annual Rally for Higher Education, where SGA secretary Katie Stillwell was the keynote speaker representing students statewide. Her speech urged legislators to protect money already set aside for higher education. Jessie, the previous year's keynote speaker, joined chief of staff Charlie Harris and other state SGA officers for a lunch with Gov. Steve Beshear.

In the recordHerald, 1 Mar 2011

April2011

Administrative Vice President Wade Pierce to hand post to fraternity brother

Pierce, who chaired the organizational aid committee, said he would be succeeded as administrative vice president by Devon Hilderbrandt, his committee co-chair and his "little brother" in Lambda Chi Alpha. Hilderbrandt ran unopposed in that spring's election.

In the recordHerald, 1 Apr 2011

7 April2011

Stephens won presidency with 56 percent of 1,066 votes

Billy Stephens, a junior from Hawesville, defeated senior Diego Leal Ambriz for SGA president, taking 56 percent of the 1,066 total votes in results announced just after midnight on April 7. Kendrick Bryan was re-elected executive vice president and Devon Hilderbrandt won administrative vice president, both unopposed. All 35 senate candidates were elected to the 36 open seats, each needing just one vote to win.

In the recordHerald, 7 Apr 2011

6 May2011

Senate tabled tobacco-free campus resolution

After nearly 45 minutes of debate, the senate tabled a resolution supporting a tobacco-free campus until the next semester. The resolution rested on a survey of more than 400 students in which 47.82 percent supported a ban, but senators argued the survey was biased because tombstones displaying the dangers of smoking had been laid outside DUC the day it was given. The campus improvements committee then said it would not support a ban until the two-year on-campus living requirement was removed.

In the recordHerald, 6 May 2011

2011-12

Billy Stephens (president)

11 entries · 50 index lines

6 September2011

Senate reconvenes, appointments confirmed, tobacco vote postponed

At the semester's first senate meeting, held after the previous week's session was canceled, senators postponed a vote on the tobacco-free campus resolution so new members could review it first. President Billy Stephens made all of his executive-branch, judicial-committee and committee-chair appointments in a single blanket vote that passed unanimously, and Speaker of the Senate Kaylee Egerer told senators to keep generating new ideas for their committees.

In the recordHerald, 7 Sep 2011

16 September2011

SGA passes tobacco-free campus resolution with housing condition

The SGA senate voted unanimously for a resolution supporting a campus-wide tobacco ban, but only if WKU dropped its requirement that students live on campus for two years. President Gary Ransdell had said the Board of Regents would not consider a ban until SGA, the University Senate and Staff Council all passed resolutions. SGA was the only body to attach the housing stipulation.

In the recordHerald, 16 Sep 2011

23 September2011

Fall senate election fills 11 seats with 977 votes cast

SGA announced its fall senator election results just after midnight on Thursday, with 11 new senators elected including Christopher Costa, Corey Johnson and Mallory Treece. Twenty students ran for the seats and 977 students voted. President Billy Stephens said he was happy with the turnout for a fall election and that he got the contested race he wanted.

In the recordHerald, 23 Sep 2011

30 September2011

SGA to lend iPads through WKU's Educational Resource Center

SGA partnered with the Educational Resource Center in Gary Ransdell Hall to provide two first-generation iPads for the ERC to load textbooks onto and lend out to students at no cost, part of President Billy Stephens' push to make the organization more visibly useful to students.

In the recordHerald, 30 Sep 2011

9 November2011

Senate defeats DUC name change resolution 19-8

A resolution to rename Downing University Center as Downing Student Union, written by campus improvements chair Keyana Boka, was voted down 19-8 with one abstention after a lengthy open debate. Executive Vice President Kendrick Bryan suggested putting the question on the spring ballot, but senators noted architects working on the DUC renovation would need an answer sooner.

In the recordHerald, 9 Nov 2011

15 November2011

Herald editorial tells SGA to drop renaming and keep its promises

The Herald editorial board wrote that SGA should focus on student issues rather than renaming a building honoring former president Dero Downing, who had recently died. It said Stephens had barely addressed his platform promises, including a dead day before finals and an improved Provide-a-Ride service, which had seen no visible progress since SGA cut ties with Franklin Taxi.

In the recordHerald, 15 Nov 2011

15 November2011

Two senators removed for absences; ten faced judicial review

Ten of SGA's 36 senators were called before the judicial board during the fall semester for excessive absences from senate and committee meetings. Two of them, Kevin Adams and Kevin Preston, were dismissed from the senate after failing to attend their judicial hearings, which the council interpreted as intent to resign. The rest received warnings, and Stephens said he would appoint replacements to the two empty seats.

In the recordHerald, 15 Nov 2011

18 November2011

SGA pays surprise $15,000 bill for previous year's Provide-A-Ride

SGA paid Parking Services a $15,000 retroactive payment for the prior year's Provide-A-Ride service after Parking Services found no record of the previous administration's payment. The money was split evenly between the organizational aid and student scholarship funds, $7,500 from each. Stephens said he was "shocked" by the bill, while 2010-11 president Colton Jessie insisted his administration had budgeted the money.

In the recordHerald, 18 Nov 2011

24 February2012

SGA approves $50,026 spring budget after $54,000 fall spending

The senate approved a spring 2012 budget of $50,026, divided among operations, public relations, executive programming and senate programming, with $10,500 set aside for organizational aid and $12,000 for scholarships. Chief of Staff Katie Stillwell told senators SGA had spent about $54,000 in the fall, $15,000 of it the retroactive Provide-A-Ride payment.

In the recordHerald, 24 Feb 2012

28 March2012

Chief of Staff Eric Smiley approved after Stillwell's resignation

The senate approved President Billy Stephens' choice of Eric Smiley as chief of staff after Katie Stillwell resigned the post; Smiley had served as chief of staff two years earlier under his brother Kevin Smiley's administration. The same meeting passed five bills, including two Organizational Aid grants of $500 each to six campus groups (the Chinese Students and Scholars Association, Geology Club, Chinese Music Club, Relay for Life, International Club and Baptist Campus Ministry), $500 toward the April 19 International Night, $398 reimbursing two Kindle Fires raffled at the WKU Student Research Conference, and $500 toward Big Red's trip to the 2012 Mascot Nationals. Senators also passed a resolution for a second campus cleanup on April 17 and moved $3,000 from general senate funds to Organizational Aid so SGA could spend down its budget before the semester's end; announcements noted that spring executive elections would open at 12:01 a.m. the next day.

In the recordHerald, 28 Mar 2012

30 March2012

Dodds elected SGA president for 2012-13; Boka and Alvey win uncontested VP races

Cory Dodds was elected SGA president for 2012-13 with 44 percent of the vote, over senator Corey Johnson with 35 percent and former senator Austin Wingate with 21 percent. Sophomore Keyana Boka was elected executive vice president and Cain Alvey administrative vice president; both vice-presidential races were uncontested.

In the recordHerald, 30 Mar 2012

2012-13

Cory Dodds (president)

15 entries · 31 index lines

6 September2012

Senate unanimously opposed the bi-term and per-credit-hour tuition proposal

SGA unanimously passed a resolution opposing an administration proposal to emphasize bi-term courses and shift tuition to a per-credit-hour model. Dodds argued the change would charge students more, since full-time students then paid for 12 hours but could enroll in up to 18. He called it a financial burden students should not have to bear.

In the recordHerald, 6 Sep 2012

25 September2012

Fall senate seats filled after two resignations

Two senators resigned over time commitments and student Shea Wyatt was named to fill in. New freshman senators Barrett Greenwell, Taylor Ruby, Cole McDowell and Paige Settles were sworn in along with Gatton Academy senator Linda Cruz and graduate senators Mark Reeves and Katie Martin.

In the recordHerald, 27 Sep 2012

13 November2012

SGA worked to restart a student government for the Glasgow campus

SGA officials traveled to WKU's Glasgow campus to help restart its dormant student representative body and connect it to main campus. Dodds said Glasgow students had no mechanism for their voices to be heard except contacting main-campus SGA. Roy Ratliff, nominated interim president of the Glasgow student body, said its top priority was establishing a writing center, for which the group had set aside $2,700.

In the recordHerald, 13 Nov 2012

14 November2012

Senate reviewed its budget and heard a retention pitch

Speaker of the Senate Christopher Costa opened the floor to Joelle Carter, assistant vice president for Retention and Student Services, who asked senators for ideas on keeping students enrolled to graduation, and SGA's current budget balance was distributed to members.

In the recordHerald, 14 Nov 2012

15 February2013

SGA passed its teaching assistant evaluation resolution

On Feb. 5 the senate passed a resolution creating teaching assistant evaluations, a program Dodds had campaigned on and drafted with his executive officers to pitch to Provost Gordon Emslie. Nicki Seay, chair of the Legislative Research Committee, wrote the bill, which aimed to make TA evaluation uniform across departments. The resolution next needed review by the Academic Quality Committee and approval by the University Senate.

In the recordHerald, 15 Feb 2013

20 February2013

Senate tabled a plus-minus grading resolution

Senator Hannah Garland's resolution to adopt plus and minus grades for high and low letter grades was tabled after public relations chair Mac Mullins argued for a more formal proposal and more student input first; a similar plan had drawn SGA resistance when the provost proposed it in 2007.

In the recordHerald, 21 Feb 2013

26 February2013

Senate amended the constitution, adding regional-campus seats

After two to three years of executive discussion, the senate passed most of a package of constitutional amendments, replacing class-year senate seats with college-based representation and guaranteeing seats for regional campuses such as Glasgow and Owensboro. A bylaw that would have made SGA members permanently ineligible for SGA-sponsored scholarships was stripped out and did not pass.

In the recordHerald, 1 Mar 2013

March2013campus

Provost Emslie cancelled the bi-term proposal SGA had opposed

Provost Gordon Emslie announced at the Feb. 21 University Senate meeting that he was dropping his bi-term emphasis proposal and had no plans to revive it, citing input from students and faculty. Both SGA and the University Senate had passed resolutions against it. Dodds said the revocation was in the student body's best interest, saying "I strongly opposed it."

In the recordHerald, 1 Mar 2013

19 March2013

SGA passed a resolution opposing the $150 Study Abroad application fee

The senate passed a resolution opposing a new $150 application fee for Study Abroad and Global Learning, set to begin with summer 2013 programs, arguing it could put program costs out of reach; the University Senate passed a similar resolution. A separate amendment proposed by Dodds to make SGA members ineligible for SGA-awarded Study Abroad scholarships failed. Dodds said 11 of the 125 such scholarships and grants that year had gone to SGA members, which he called a conflict of interest.

In the recordHerald, 19 Mar 2013

27 March2013

Executive candidates debate ahead of spring election

Outgoing President Cory Dodds opened a candidates' debate in Ransdell Hall Auditorium by describing to the audience how much influence the students elected to SGA's executive positions would actually have on WKU's campus, ahead of the election that would choose his successor.

In the recordHerald, 29 Mar 2013

4 April2013

Boka, Reeves and Seay won the spring executive elections

Executive vice president Keyana Boka was elected 2013-14 SGA president with 626 votes, 47 percent, over administrative vice president Cain Alvey with 419 votes and Austin Wingate with 300. Mark Reeves won executive vice president with 632 votes, 57 percent, over Brad Cockrel, and Nicki Seay ran unopposed for administrative vice president. Twenty-six student senators were also elected.

In the recordHerald, 4 Apr 2013

9 April2013

Judicial Council disqualified president-elect Boka, 3-2

In an emergency meeting, SGA's Judicial Council voted 3-2 to disqualify president-elect Keyana Boka after runner-up and outgoing administrative vice president Cain Alvey complained that a self-promotional email had gone to Honors College students at Boka's request, sent by Honors College graduate assistant Destiny Savage, violating the election code. The disqualification would have made Alvey, who had placed second in the April 4 vote, the incoming president; Boka said she would appeal.

In the recordHerald, 9 Apr 2013

16 April2013

Judicial Council declined to contest Bailey's reinstatement of Boka

In an emergency meeting, the Judicial Council unanimously decided not to challenge Bailey's memorandum reinstating Boka, saying it did not believe it had the power to do so, while expressing official disapproval. Chief Justice Seth Church called the intervention "a serious infringement on our autonomy" and said it set a bad precedent. Boka said the council had conflicts of interest and needed to be held accountable by a neutral party in the administration.

In the recordHerald, 16 Apr 2013

16 April2013

Costa stepped down as speaker; Settles elected to succeed him

Christopher Costa did not seek another term as speaker of the senate, and senators elected Paige Settles to replace him. The same meeting confirmed presidential appointments Roy Ratliff as senator-at-large and Jackie Stewart as associate justice, with Chief of Staff Travis Taylor and public relations chair Mac Mullins giving reports.

In the recordHerald, 17 Apr 2013

25 April2013campus

Senate opposed automatic athletic-fee increases ahead of C-USA move

The senate passed a resolution against the annual automatic increase in the student athletic fee, arguing the revenue-sharing WKU would gain on joining Conference USA that July would outweigh the roughly $40,000 the university lost annually in the Sun Belt. Executive vice president-elect Mark Reeves, who introduced it, said the resolution set a precedent against automatic fee increases generally.

In the recordHerald, 26 Apr 2013

2013-14

Keyanna Boka (president)

14 entries · 37 index lines

28 March2013

Presidential debate drew full field of candidates

Ahead of the spring 2013 election, outgoing president Cory Dodds opened a debate in Ransdell Hall Auditorium among presidential candidates Cain Alvey, Keyana Boka and Austin Wingate, plus executive vice presidential candidates Brad Cockrel and Mark Reeves and administrative vice presidential candidate Nicki Seay. Boka said SGA members needed better training in their roles, Alvey said the presidency's responsibilities went beyond the constitution, and Wingate, a former Speaker of the Senate, called for better representation across student groups.

In the recordHerald, 28 Mar 2013

10 September2013

Executive Council floated plus/minus grading, set fall calendar

At the Executive Council's weekly meeting, Executive Vice President Mark Reeves reported that the University Senate Council had discussed reviving a plus/minus grading system and that Provost Gordon Emslie was interested in SGA's support. The council set a Nov. 9 Picnic with the President for the presidents' council and deans, and swore in Samantha Johnson to an executive cabinet seat vacated by the resignation of Keith Watson.

In the recordSGA Executive Council minutes, 10 Sep 2013

11 September2013

SGA reviewed 24-hour dining, grading and registration proposals

SGA gave first read to a proposal for a 24-hour on-campus dining option, with the Organizational Aid Committee sponsoring the resolution and assistant vice president for auxiliary services Gary Meszaros set to attend the next meeting. Reeves told senators Provost Gordon Emslie was reviving a plus/minus grading proposal and had brought priority registration and major-declaration changes to University Senate.

In the recordHerald, 11 Sep 2013

12 September2013

Senate passed international student seat amendment

President Keyana Boka and executive vice president Mark Reeves authored a constitutional amendment adding a senate seat for Navitas or English as a Second Language international students. The Judicial Council had ruled an earlier version unconstitutional, but after a revision in an emergency meeting the Senate passed it with only two votes against. Boka said it would make WKU's SGA the first student government in the state with an international senate seat.

In the recordHerald, 12 Sep 2013

19 September2013

Fall election drew 564 voters, created international seat

A total of 564 voters cast ballots in the fall SGA election. A referendum creating the Navitas/ESL international student senate seat passed with 310 of 426 votes, or 73 percent. Six freshman senators were elected out of seven candidates, with Jay Todd Richey taking 27 percent of the vote, and most college senate seats went to unopposed candidates.

In the recordHerald, 19 Sep 2013

10 October2013

SGA finalized $125,000 budget

SGA finalized a $125,000 budget for the 2013-14 year, funded from student tuition at about $6.25 per student, after a planned funding increase did not come through. The organizational aid committee was allotted $30,000, with campus organizations able to receive up to $500 each. The executive discretionary fund held $5,900, part of which covered a Washington, D.C. higher education lobbying trip by Boka and Reeves.

In the recordHerald, 10 Oct 2013

31 October2013

Priority registration complaints spurred open forum

Student complaints over new two-tier priority registration rules, including a 16-credit-hour cap during the priority period, pushed SGA to schedule a Nov. 12 open forum with Provost Gordon Emslie. Honors College seniors told senator Tyler Scaff some were considering dropping the honors major over the change. Boka said she had no official stance yet, though SGA had earlier approved the change through Reeves's vote at University Senate.

In the recordHerald, 31 Oct 2013

5 November2013

Herald editorial faulted SGA over registration policy

A Herald editorial accused SGA of failing to represent students on the new priority-registration hour cap, saying executive vice president Mark Reeves voted for the policy at University Senate on Sept. 10 without SGA questioning or debating it first. The editorial argued SGA had one job, representing students, and had not done it on this issue.

In the recordHerald, 5 Nov 2013

7 November2013campus

Thompson Complex North Wing set to close permanently

Boka announced at the Tuesday SGA meeting that Thompson Complex North Wing, home to the biology and chemistry departments, would close permanently the next semester because the building could not be maintained over the winter. The building had been labeled for demolition since 2005, and its demolition along with renovation of the Center Wing was the university's top capital priority before the Kentucky General Assembly.

In the recordHerald, 7 Nov 2013

3 December2013

Judicial Council voided Talisman fee stance reversal

After the yearbook's budget was cut to $127,000, senator Chris Costa moved at the Nov. 19 meeting to revoke SGA's stance supporting a $9 student fee for the Talisman that students had approved on a 2005 ballot, and two-thirds of SGA voted to reverse the stance. The Judicial Council ruled Costa's motion unconstitutional on Nov. 21, and also ruled the original 2005 policy unconstitutional because it was never passed according to SGA policy. Talisman editors then met with Boka and SGA members to discuss long-term funding options.

In the recordHerald, 3 Dec 2013

6 February2014

SGA reconvened, planned Frankfort rally against budget cuts

At the first spring meeting, Boka announced a planned trip to Frankfort called "Rally for Retention" in response to WKU's $1.8 million state budget cut, with speeches and one-on-one meetings with legislators. Reeves warned that tough budget cuts were coming, and the body reviewed a proposal to revise the change-of-major advising process. Five members had resigned the previous semester, leaving the legislative research and public relations chairs among the vacant seats.

In the recordHerald, 6 Feb 2014

13 February2014

Executive Council nullified judicial appointment amendment

An amendment stripping the SGA president's sole power to appoint judicial council justices and raising the number of justices to seven passed at the Tuesday meeting, over Boka's objection that it bypassed presidential appointment and the senate. After the meeting the Executive Council reviewed the constitution and determined too few senators had attended for the vote to count, sending the amendment back to first read. The SGA office also temporarily moved to Garrett after flooding in Cravens.

In the recordHerald, 13 Feb 2014

26 February2014

Mid-year budget report showed $46,883 surplus

SGA's mid-year budget report showed a $46,883.62 surplus on its $125,000 budget. The Senate approved Bill 3-14-S allocating organizational funds and suspended its bylaws to pass Resolution 3-14-S supporting WKU's participation in the Campus Pride Index, and approved Hannah Neeper, Elizabeth Gribbins and AJ Stewart as new senators as six senate seats remained open.

In the recordHerald, 26 Feb 2014

May2014

Final meeting passed Good Samaritan resolution, funding bills

At the last meeting of the semester, Boka announced students would face a 4.8 percent tuition increase, about $209 more per semester for most, alongside a $4.2 million increase in student financial assistance. The Senate suspended its bylaws to pass a slate of bills funding Summer Term assistance, student organizations, student research and an Earth Week planting party. Resolution 6-14-S passed in support of adopting a Good Samaritan Policy protecting students who call 911 during drug or alcohol overdoses.

In the recordHerald, 1 May 2014

Keyana Boka - Student Government Association UA12/2/1 2014 Graduation Special Section

2014-15

Nicki Taylor (president)

13 entries · 34 index lines

28 August2014

SGA opened the year with a $21,000 scholarship program

SGA began the year under new president Nicki Seay, a Crofton senior, working alongside Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler and Executive Vice President Nolan Miles. The association expanded its summer and winter term need-based scholarship program from the previous year's $6,000 to $21,000, funded in part by an anonymous donation. Seay named student involvement, retention and graduation her first priorities.

In the recordHerald, 28 Aug 2014

2 September2014campus

Downing Student Union celebrated its community opening

WKU held a ceremonial community opening for Downing Student Union after a two-year, $49 million renovation; the building had opened to students the week before. Students paid $36 million of the cost through a $70-per-semester fee, and the renovation began as an SGA initiative in 2011. SGA President Nicki Seay attended alongside President Gary Ransdell and other officials.

In the recordHerald, 2 Sep 2014

25 September2014

Fall election drew 742 voters and seated 17 senators

SGA announced its fall election results around 12:20 a.m. in the Senate Chamber of Downing Student Union. There were 742 voters and 17 senators were elected, including three freshman senators led by Emily Pride with 281 votes. President Nicki Seay called the election very competitive, noting not everyone who ran won a seat.

In the recordHerald, 25 Sep 2014

15 October2014

Senate defeated a nonsectarian prayer policy resolution

After more than 20 minutes of debate, the senate defeated Resolution 4-14-F, which would have supported adopting the University Senate's nonsectarian public prayer policy for university-sponsored events. President Nicki Taylor said the senate was split three ways among nonsectarian prayer, sectarian prayer and no prayer at all. The same night, senators passed Bill 9-14-F allocating $250 in organizational aid to the Phi Gamma Delta fraternity.

In the recordHerald, 15 Oct 2014

20 November2014

Executive Cabinet vetoed the smoke-free campus resolution

The senate passed Resolution 11-14-F, supporting a smoke-free campus, on a 14-10 vote, but the SGA Executive Cabinet vetoed it after the meeting. Chief of Staff Seth Church argued it was unfair to ban smoking for students required to live on campus for two years. Senators retained the power to override the veto with a two-thirds vote.

In the recordHerald, 20 Nov 2014

4 December2014

Veto override failed; alcohol policy resolution passed

At the final meeting of the fall semester, the senate failed to overturn the Executive Cabinet's veto of the smoke-free resolution, and President Nicki Taylor read the cabinet's official veto statement citing enforcement, housing requirements and practicality. The senate then passed Resolution 13-14-F, supporting amendments to WKU's alcohol policy and Student Code of Conduct to let students 21 and older purchase and possess alcohol on campus. Co-author Jody Dahmer called the existing policy ineffective and hard to enforce fairly.

In the recordHerald, 4 Dec 2014

14 December2014

President Taylor addressed December graduates

SGA President Nicki Taylor spoke at WKU's December commencement, telling graduates to celebrate what they had accomplished: "You have the rest of your life to look forward to." She had opened the year in August under her previous surname, Seay, and was going by Taylor in Herald coverage by mid-October.

In the recordHerald, 14 Dec 2014

3 February2015

Limited smoking campus resolution passed 13-11

SGA passed Resolution 1-15-S, supporting a limited smoking campus, by a 13-11 vote. The resolution would restrict tobacco use to 39 designated areas that the Administrative Council would gradually phase out over three years, while leaving electronic cigarettes and smokeless tobacco unrestricted. Co-author Seth Church said it was roughly the fifth version of the resolution since the smoking debate began the previous semester.

In the recordHerald, 3 Feb 2015

4 February2015

President Taylor abstained on smoking vote as a sitting regent

The Bowling Green Daily News reported that Nicki Taylor, in addition to serving as SGA president, sat on the WKU Board of Regents, and abstained from an Executive Council vote on the smoking-campus proposal because of that seat.

In the recordBowling Green Daily News, 4 Feb 2015

3 March2015

SGA backed a $10 million parking garage funded by a $30 fee

SGA passed a resolution supporting construction of a new parking structure on part of Creason Lot, funded by a $30-per-semester tuition increase. Authors Zach Jones, Brian Chism and Nathan Cherry estimated the roughly 500-car garage would take about 18 months to build. Chief of Staff Seth Church objected that the plan was rushed and left out regional campuses.

In the recordHerald, 3 Mar 2015

4 March2015

Ransdell formally responded to four SGA resolutions

President Gary Ransdell emailed faculty and staff his official response to four SGA resolutions on limited smoking, campus alcohol sales, a new parking structure and a student fee for WKU Student Legal Services. He announced a six-person ad hoc committee to implement a limited smoking campus by the end of 2017 and a restaurant in the Garrett Conference Center that could serve beer in the evenings. He said the parking and legal services fees would need Board of Regents and Council on Postsecondary Education approval.

In the recordHerald, 4 Mar 2015

2 April2015

Jay Todd Richey won the SGA presidency, 874 votes to 524

Jay Todd Richey defeated senator Brian Chism for SGA president, 63 percent to 37 percent, or 874 votes to 524, with results announced about 20 minutes after TopNet polls closed at 11:59 p.m. Wednesday. Nolan Miles ran unopposed for a second term as executive vice president, and Liz Koehler won the administrative vice president race with 66 percent over J. William Berry. Twenty of 34 senatorial candidates won seats.

In the recordHerald, 2 Apr 2015

16 April2015

An election result challenged and upheld

Anonymous accusations alleged Jay Todd Richey had breached election codes on poster placement. The judicial council warned him against future violations and confirmed he had rightfully won.

In the recordHerald, April 2015

2015-16

Jay Todd Richey (president)

12 entries · 47 index lines

27 August2015

Richey outlined fall goals, MyCampusToo launch

Opening his first term, President Jay Todd Richey said he wanted more executive-cabinet and senate communication and more outreach to international students and regional campuses, and confirmed his campaign initiative MyCampusToo would launch that semester. Executive Vice President Nolan Miles said he would push senators to sit on university committees and revive the Dine with Decision Makers event.

In the recordHerald, 27 Aug 2015

15 September2015

SGA budget fell by $19,500

SGA's budget dropped $19,500 from the previous year, largely because a $15,000 private donation was not repeated and the university cut another $4,500 in reallocations. Organizational funding took the hardest hit, losing $9,000, and scholarship pools for Academic Affairs and Student Affairs each fell by more than $5,000. Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler reallocated $4,000 from organizational aid back into scholarships to soften the loss.

In the recordHerald, 15 Sep 2015

22 September2015

Senate voted to disapprove Confucius Institute approval process

The Student Senate voted overwhelmingly to pass a resolution disapproving of how the Confucius Institute building project was approved, after President Gary Ransdell signed the contract in China in December 2014 and the Board of Regents, including the Student Regent, voted on it more than a month later without full details disclosed. Richey said the vote was not meant to set a precedent beyond ensuring the Board had full information before acting.

In the recordHerald, 24 Sep 2015

18 November2015

Senate backed meningitis vaccine requirement, amended bylaws

The Senate unanimously passed Resolution 6-15-F supporting a meningococcal meningitis vaccination requirement for incoming freshmen in on-campus housing beginning with the class of 2020, and unanimously passed Bill 10-15-F amending SGA's bylaws. Richey reported that his fall listening tours of the regional campuses had gone well and turned up how different those campuses were from main campus.

In the recordHerald, 18 Nov 2015

3 December2015

Chief Justice resigned after censure hearing backlash

The Judicial Council unanimously declined to censure senator John Winstead, whom it had investigated over an "impeach Ransdell" sign and a mocking Facebook post about President Ransdell, ruling his actions were protected free speech. Winstead called the fact he was investigated at all "the problem I'm objecting to." Chief Justice Kelsey Luttrell then announced she would step down at the end of the semester, saying the council had been publicly ridiculed and lacked support from fellow SGA members.

In the recordHerald, 3 Dec 2015

28 January2016

Administration overrode student vote on pub name

Richey announced that administrators had renamed the future Garrett Conference Center pub "Topper Grill and Pub," setting aside the name students chose in SGA's "Dub the Pub" contest, Topper Tavern. Richey said Ransdell wanted to downplay the alcohol theme and called himself "very disappointed," saying the move made SGA question how much the administration listened to students. At the same meeting SGA introduced the RAVE Guardian campus safety app.

In the recordHerald, 28 Jan 2016

2 February2016campus

Ransdell announced retirement amid state budget cuts

President Gary Ransdell announced he would step down as WKU's ninth president on June 30, 2017, triggering a presidential search. The announcement came the same week new Gov. Matt Bevin ordered an immediate 4.5 percent cut to WKU's state funding and proposed a 9 percent cut, with future funding shifted to a performance-based pool. The changes framed much of SGA's advocacy for the rest of the year.

In the recordHerald, 2 Feb 2016

17 February2016

Senate opposed state tuition-freeze bill

The senate approved Resolution 2-16-S opposing Kentucky Senate Bill 75, which would have frozen resident tuition at 2015-16 levels for four years. Richey argued such freezes were "dangerous risks" that could wreck universities and cost students more in the long run. At the same meeting, Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler reported an expected 4.5 percent cut to SGA's own budget, about $1,301.

In the recordHerald, 17 Feb 2016

24 February2016

Senators lobbied legislators in Frankfort

SGA members traveled to Frankfort to lobby against state budget cuts that could slash WKU funding by as much as 9 percent, meeting with eight state officials. Senators pressed for smaller cuts and restoration of need-based aid, citing figures that about 15,000 students were denied need-based financial aid the prior year. Both chambers of the General Assembly recognized SGA for its participation.

In the recordHerald, 24 Feb 2016

2 March2016

Ransdell declined SGA's meningitis vaccine mandate

Richey read aloud a letter from Ransdell responding to Resolution 6-15-F, passed the previous semester, which supported requiring meningitis vaccinations for incoming freshmen living on campus starting with the class of 2020. Ransdell wrote that the university would highly recommend vaccination but "stop short of requiring it," citing a $143.77 cost for uninsured students at the Graves-Gilbert Clinic.

In the recordHerald, 2 Mar 2016

6 April2016

Senate passed guidelines for WKU's tenth president

The senate approved a resolution by John Winstead and Richey outlining what students wanted in WKU's tenth president, which Richey planned to use in his role on the presidential search committee. After debate, senators amended the sustainability clause to target improving WKU's AASHE STARS rating and voted to remove language about Jonesville "reparations" entirely, after disputing whether reparations or restitution was the right term.

In the recordHerald, 6 Apr 2016

20 April2016

Richey reelected in one of highest-turnout elections

Students reelected Jay Todd Richey as SGA president with 64 percent of the vote over Braxton Powell, in one of the highest-turnout elections in the association's history with 2,442 voters. Kate Hart, an Academic Affairs chairwoman and Richey's running mate, won executive vice president. Richey called the win "verification of promises kept."

In the recordHerald, 20 Apr 2016

2016-17

Jay Todd Richey (president)

10 entries · 16 index lines

20 April2016

Richey re-elected SGA president in high-turnout election

WKU students re-elected Jay Todd Richey as SGA president and elected Kate Hart as executive vice president in one of the highest-turnout elections in the association's history, with 2,442 voters. Richey defeated opponent Braxton Powell with 64 percent of the overall vote. Powell was elected a junior senator and his running mate Zach Jones a senior senator.

In the recordHerald, 20 Apr 2016

12 September2016campus

Ransdell condemns racist incidents after notes, vandalism

In the weeks before, racist notes had been left in a WKU assistant dean's office and a racial slur was scratched into a student's car following a parking dispute. President Gary Ransdell called the acts "cowardly" and "heinous," said they did not reflect the university's values, and called for campus dialogue on intolerance.

In the recordWKMS, 12 Sep 2016

13 September2016

Senators raise campus racism at first fall meeting

At the third meeting of the 15th Senate, student speakers Jeb Veeck, Francisco Serrano and Spencer Wells addressed the recent racist incidents on campus. Veeck suggested a Q&A session on the issue and Serrano urged senators to help end racism on campus.

In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 13 Sep 2016Read it here

12 October2016

Two SGA members resign amid racism complaint; investigation nullified

After Chief Justice Cody Cox told the Oct. 11 senate meeting he had received a complaint that several SGA members made racist remarks, senator Braxton Powell and justice John McKinney resigned the next morning, citing scheduling conflicts and personal reasons respectively; neither confirmed, denied, nor acknowledged any link between the resignations and the complaint. The Judicial Council's planned investigation was dropped because the students in question had already left SGA, and the organization never released the identities of the accused or the nature of the alleged remarks. President Richey and MyCampusToo chair Helen Vickrey issued a statement the next day condemning the alleged acts.

In the recordHerald, 17 Oct 2016

26 October2016

Senate rejected 2.0 GPA bill, backed housing diversity

SGA rejected a bill that would have let students vote to lower the organization's GPA requirement from 2.5 to 2.0, a change supporters said would make the body more representative; a Twitter poll found 61 percent of respondents opposed it. The senate also approved a resolution asking Housing and Residence Life to address the lack of diversity in on-campus housing under the university's 10-year housing plan.

In the recordHerald, 26 Oct 2016

30 November2016

SGA created Jonesville scholarship fund

The senate created a scholarship memorializing Jonesville, the African American community founded by freed slaves in the 1870s that stood on land now occupied by Smith Stadium, Nick Denes Field and Downing Student Union until WKU bought and demolished it in the late 1960s. Senators debated whether the award should go only to African American students as repayment for Jonesville's condemnation or be opened to all minority students.

In the recordHerald, 30 Nov 2016

12 April2017

SGA backed prioritizing faculty raises over construction

The senate passed a resolution supporting future faculty salary increases, written to mirror a concurrent resolution headed to the Faculty Senate and proposed by Administrative Vice President Hannah Neeper and Chief of Staff James Line. The resolution urged that salary increases be prioritized over future construction or renovation projects, citing WKU's second-to-last ranking in faculty pay among its 19 benchmark institutions in 2015 and a survey in which 57 percent of faculty rated their morale as poor or very poor.

In the recordHerald, 12 Apr 2017

18 April2017

Resolution 6-17-S passes 19-10-1

Senators Andrea Ambam and Brian Anderson wrote a resolution supporting reparations for Black students, calling for full and free access to WKU for all Black people and asking for a task force on test-optional and geographically weighted admissions. Modelled on a resolution passed at Wisconsin-Madison earlier that year.

In the recordDaily News, Apr 2017 (archived copy)Read it here

19 April2017

Andi Dahmer elected to succeed Richey

Louisville sophomore Andi Dahmer, a senator and chair of the MyCampusToo committee, was elected the next student body president, winning 930 of 1,579 votes cast against Kenan Mujkanovic's 305 and Lily Nellans's 212. Her running mates Savannah Molyneaux and Kara Lowry won executive vice president and administrative vice president. Dahmer said she would start with legislation on study abroad affordability and sensitivity training to improve retention among marginalized groups.

In the recordHerald, 19 Apr 2017

21 April2017

President Ransdell rejects the resolution

National wire coverage followed, along with a Tucker Carlson interview with Ambam and a wave of fabricated headlines claiming WKU had granted free tuition. Ransdell stated within days that it was not a university position. Both authors described it as a conversation starter.

In the recordFactCheck.org

2017-18

Andi Dahmer (president)

13 entries · 15 index lines

17 August2017campus

Dahmer joined national solidarity letter after Charlottesville

President Andi Dahmer was one of more than 120 college student body presidents nationwide who signed an open letter backing the University of Virginia after the violent Charlottesville protests, and said developing campus-wide "cultural competency training" was a goal for the semester.

In the recordHerald, 17 Aug 2017

31 August2017

First senate meeting passes constitutional amendments

SGA held its first senate meeting of the year and approved three of five proposed constitutional amendment bills, which then went to the student body for a vote in the fall elections. The passed bills added constitutional review duties to the Judicial Council, made the chief justice backup speaker of the senate, and required senators to post one office hour per week. Senators also debated Bill 5-17-F, which proposed limiting the legislative powers of the executive branch.

In the recordHerald, 31 Aug 2017

26 September2017

Senate passed a required sexual assault education resolution, 29-1

Resolution 1-17-F, co-authored by public relations chair William Hurst, S.A.V.E.S. chair Ashlyn Jones and three senators, supported adding a one-credit-hour sexual assault education course to freshman colonnade requirements, arguing existing options like HAVEN and Green Dot carried no penalty for skipping them. The senate also funded a "No-Shave November" beard contest and fixed the timing of constitutional-amendment elections in the bylaws.

In the recordHerald, 28 Sep 2017

24 October2017campus

Dahmer condemned a blackface Halloween incident at senate meeting

President Andi Dahmer opened the eighth meeting of the Senate by telling members that a student had worn blackface to a Halloween party the previous weekend and that it was not acceptable. She also hosted student body presidents from other Kentucky universities on campus that weekend and reminded senators that Herald reporters were allowed into all university committee meetings.

In the recordSGA Senate meeting minutes, 24 Oct 2017Read it here

9 November2017

SGA passes resolution supporting DACA students

At its Nov. 7 meeting the senate passed a resolution, co-authored by President Andi Dahmer and Francisco Serrano, standing in solidarity with WKU students who were DACA recipients. The measure passed 32-1 and was a revision of the clean DREAM Act resolution rejected the previous week, reframed to address only the WKU student community. Dahmer noted WKU was one of the last Kentucky schools to pass something of this nature.

In the recordHerald, 9 Nov 2017

29 January2018

Judicial Council censured PR committee chair over election-discrepancy complaint

At an emergency meeting, the Judicial Council took up a complaint public relations committee chair Will Hurst had raised at the Jan. 23 senate meeting, alleging the executive board failed its constitutional duty to advertise the fall election and citing a discrepancy in vote totals between constitutional amendments that passed and failed. The council found the executive board had complied with the constitution and issued a censure against Hurst; Dahmer said she was pleased the council had upheld the board's conduct. The censure was confirmed at the Feb. 6 senate meeting.

In the recordHerald, 29 Jan 2018

7 February2018

SGA members rally in Frankfort for higher education

About 20 WKU SGA members joined roughly 100 students from Kentucky's public universities at the Kentucky Board of Student Body Presidents' annual Rally for Higher Education on the Capitol steps in Frankfort on Feb. 6. Dahmer said the board of student body presidents had been working consistently since August to plan the rally.

In the recordHerald, 7 Feb 2018

13 February2018

Senate backed LGBTQ health curriculum, chair swap on Diversity committee

The senate unanimously passed a resolution supporting integrated LGBTQ health curriculum in WKU's medical education programs, co-authored by diversity and inclusion chair Mark Clark, chief of staff Conner Hounshell and administrative vice president Kara Lowry. Clark was approved as the committee's new chair after Corey Newsome stepped down over scheduling conflicts.

In the recordHerald, 14 Feb 2018

3 April2018

Dahmer announced she would not seek reelection

Citing tension in the senate that she called "almost toxic in nature" and that she attributed to partisan ideology in a body meant to be nonpartisan, Dahmer said in a Facebook post she would not run again and endorsed Conner Hounshell for president alongside Savannah Molyneaux and Kara Lowry, seeking reelection to their executive vice president and administrative vice president seats.

In the recordHerald, 4 Apr 2018

4 April2018

LGBTQ activists address senate after senator's remarks

Several LGBTQ student activists spoke to the senate on April 3 after Senator Dallas McKinney had cited the Bible on March 27, reading verses saying the "wicked" deserved death, as his reason for voting against Bill 13-18-S, which funded $250 for stoles for the Lavender Recognition Ceremony honoring LGBTQ graduates. The bill passed in the senate, and speakers including SGA member Brigid Stakelum and Diversity and Inclusion Committee Chair Mark Clark called the remarks dehumanizing and discriminatory.

In the recordHerald, 4 Apr 2018

18 April2018

Mayer wins presidency after disqualification reversed

Stephen Mayer was elected SGA president and student regent, with Garrett Edmonds as executive vice president and Harper Anderson as administrative vice president. Their MEA ticket had been disqualified on April 16 after a complaint over a Pepe the Frog meme in a campaign chalk drawing, but the Judicial Council reversed the disqualification to a suspension before results were announced. Mayer won 35 percent of the 2,378 votes cast in the presidential race, ahead of Conner Hounshell with 33 percent and Kenan Mujkanovic with 32 percent.

In the recordHerald, 18 Apr 2018

24 April2018

Dahmer details months of harassment

In a Herald investigation, Dahmer said members of SGA had cursed at her, called her derogatory names and exchanged group messages in a GroupMe called the "Justice Friends" wishing her harm over the fall and spring semesters, and that a profane note left on her car on Feb. 9 led her to file a WKU police report and avoid her residence hall for two weeks. Her case was reported to WKU's Title IX office, which told her the conduct did not meet the legal standard for harassment, and it was processed instead by the Office of Student Conduct, which issued no-contact orders against two senators.

In the recordHerald, 24 Apr 2018

May2018

Caboni announced Title IX review after Dahmer harassment report

University president Timothy Caboni said he would convene a faculty-staff-student committee, co-chaired by sociology professor Lauren McClain and counseling official Karl Laves, to review WKU's Title IX, Equal Employment Opportunity and Office of Student Conduct processes following the Herald's report on the harassment Dahmer said she experienced. President-elect Stephen Mayer called Dahmer "a super strong woman" and said he did not stand for harassment or sexual assault.

In the recordHerald, 1 May 2018

2018-19

Stephen Mayer (president)

11 entries · 4 index lines

11 September2018

Senate rejected first Judicial Council nominee of the term

The senate voted 8-7-1 against confirming Wood Brown, a Pike fraternity member and law clerk, as associate justice of the Judicial Council, after Mayer said his constitutional duty required him to appoint whom he judged best despite recusing himself from the interview process; senators argued the Judicial Council's own top-ranked applicant, not Brown, should have been chosen. Mayer's next nominee, Alex Rivera, was confirmed the following week.

In the recordSGA Senate meeting minutes, 11 Sep 2018

20 September2018

Senate asked WKU to cancel classes on Election Day

SGA unanimously passed Resolution 5-18-F asking the university to cancel classes on Nov. 6, 2018, so students could get to the polls, after a presentation by Francis Wilson of the get-out-the-vote campaign Reg 2 Vote, and approved $300 in support through Bill 7-18-F. The senate also passed Resolutions 1-18-F and 2-18-F, which asked WKU to strike code-of-conduct language barring students from refusing a direction from a university official and from audio recording student-faculty meetings. Mayer's nominee Alex Rivera was confirmed as associate justice of the Judicial Council 12-3 after an earlier nomination had failed.

In the recordHerald, 20 Sep 2018

25 September2018

Academic and Student Affairs directorship filled after two failed tries

The senate confirmed Aubrey Kelly as Director of Academic and Student Affairs 24-3-4, three weeks into the term. Initial nominee Ashley Cox was not confirmed at the first meeting after senators questioned her committee attendance, then withdrew when a family member was hospitalized; her replacement, Anna McAvoy, failed confirmation 6-9-1 on Sept. 11 after a senator raised concerns about her scholarship-grading experience.

In the recordSGA Senate meeting minutes, 25 Sep 2018

26 September2018

First Year Village housing plan presented to SGA

Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds presented plans for a freshman First Year Village of two new pod-style residence halls at the bottom of the Hill, replacing Bemis Lawrence and Barnes-Campbell halls on the site of the Pearce-Ford Tower parking lot. The senate also approved Bill 6-18-F, funding a sustainability film festival, by a 21-4 vote with one abstention.

In the recordHerald, 26 Sep 2018

24 October2018

SGA created a first-generation student scholarship

The senate passed a bill by Campus Improvements Chair Matt Barr creating a recurring $2,000 scholarship for first-generation college students, approved 31-1. It also passed organizational aid Bill 11-18-F, sending $1,400 to Delta Sigma Theta, Phi Beta Sigma and the jump rope club, and allocated $100 to advertise the Campus Safety Walk.

In the recordHerald, 24 Oct 2018

6 December2018

Contested appointment and Identity Evropa denouncement ended the fall term

President Stephen Mayer's nomination of graduate student Emily Anne Pride, daughter of a former SGA adviser, to a vacated senate seat sparked about 90 minutes of debate before she was confirmed 17-9 with two abstentions. The senate then passed Resolution 10-18-F, supporting denouncement of the white nationalist group Identity Evropa and its attempts to recruit on campus, 28-0, and allocated $430 to the Black Leadership Academic Conference through Bill 24-18-F.

In the recordHerald, 6 Dec 2018

27 February2019

Resolution passed to relocate Confederate marker

After lengthy debate, the senate passed Resolution 1-19-S by a 29-1 vote with one abstention, calling for the marker near the Kentucky Museum identifying Bowling Green as the Confederate capital of Kentucky to be relocated to a display inside the museum. Authors Kara Lowry, Conner Hounshell and Symone Whalin argued the marker was a reminder of oppression against people of color, and Mayer said the resolution would go to the WKU Administrative Council. The senate also allocated $1,000 to send the Mock Trial team to a national tournament.

In the recordHerald, 27 Feb 2019

27 March2019

Mayer declined to seek re-election as election codes were set

Mayer announced he would not seek re-election because he was applying to medical schools, and the senate approved the spring 2019 election codes 31-1, with campaigning to begin April 1 and voting on TopNet April 15-16. Chief Justice Jacob McAndrews announced he would resign from the Judicial Council to run for elected office. The senate also passed four spending bills, rejected a change to senator office-hour rules and tabled a bill creating a first-generation senate seat.

In the recordHerald, 27 Mar 2019

3 April2019

Transparency resolution passed after the dean's resignation

A week after Snyder's sudden resignation, the senate passed Resolution 4-19-S by a 30-2 vote, calling on top university officials to provide explanations for major decisions. In the same meeting it rejected Mayer's Judicial Council nominee Wood Brown 17-11, created a senate seat for first-generation college students 33-0, and passed a resolution 33-0 asking WKU to let students' preferred names appear on class rosters, IDs and email addresses, a measure brought by the Transgender Non-Binary student organization.

In the recordHerald, 3 Apr 2019

9 April2019campus

No-confidence vote and provost's resignation shook the university

After Snyder was asked to resign as Potter College dean on March 26, protests from faculty, staff and students led the University Senate to an unprecedented vote of no confidence in Provost Terry Ballman on April 4, and she resigned the next day. Ogden dean Cheryl Stevens was named acting provost, and days later the Comprehensive Academic Program Evaluation committee recommended suspending 101 of WKU's 380 academic programs.

In the recordHerald, 9 Apr 2019

17 April2019

WGK ticket won the spring executive elections

The ticket of Will Harris, Garrett Edmonds and Kenan Mujkanovic won the spring SGA elections, defeating the ticket of Asha McWilliams, Jacob McAndrews and Symone Whalin. Harris was elected student body president to succeed Mayer, Edmonds was re-elected to a second term as executive vice president, and Mujkanovic defeated Whalin for administrative vice president, with results announced at SGA's election party on April 16.

In the recordHerald, 17 Apr 2019

2019-20

Will Harris (president)

10 entries · 2 index lines

17 April2019

Harris-led WGK ticket wins SGA executive election

The WGK ticket of Will Harris, Garrett Edmonds and Kenan Mujkanovic won the spring SGA elections, with Harris defeating Asha McWilliams for student body president. Edmonds was re-elected to a second term as executive vice president and Mujkanovic defeated Symone Whalin for administrative vice president. Results were announced at SGA's election party, with the new officers set to take office at the annual banquet; the Herald's results story reported no turnout figures.

In the recordHerald, 17 Apr 2019

4 September2019

First meeting of the year confirms five executive appointments

At its first official meeting of the semester, the senate confirmed all five of President Will Harris's executive branch nominees: Aubrey Kelley as chief of staff, Ashlynn Evans as chief of public relations, Abbey Norvell as director of academic and student affairs, Paul Brosky as director of information technology and Josh Zaczek as Legislative Research Committee chair. Appointees outlined plans including wider use of counseling center fee vouchers and a revival of the need-based Earn-a-Computer program.

In the recordHerald, 4 Sep 2019

11 September2019

Senate blocks budget over special projects fund

The senate refused to pass the year's budget over a $6,500 special projects fund the executive branch wanted for a sand volleyball court and hammock space at the First Year Village green space. Senators including Anthony Survance objected that the allocation cut into scholarship money, with Survance calling the motion "slimy", and the senate voted to keep $3,000 in its discretionary fund and $35,000 in scholarships. The executive branch pulled the budget, forcing a week's wait before a revised version could be voted on.

In the recordHerald, 11 Sep 2019

19 September2019

Budget passes unanimously with spending stipulations

All 13 senators approved the yearly budget after a compromise added stipulations restricting the special projects fund to the First Year Village plans and redistributing any money unspent by March 3 back to discretionary and voucher funds. The budget's passage let Bills 1-19-F (Greeks Go Green) and 2-19-F (funding for Bowling Green Pride) pass unanimously. The senate also amended its election codes to halve campaign spending maximums, which had been $300 for presidential candidates, $125 for vice presidential candidates and $50 for senate candidates.

In the recordHerald, 19 Sep 2019

24 October2019

Senate passes Resolution 4-19-F against Alpha Xi Delta

The senate voted 24-7 to pass Resolution 4-19-F, authored by senators Symone Whalin and Anthony Survance, supporting disciplinary action up to suspension from Greek affairs against the Epsilon Kappa chapter of Alpha Xi Delta. The resolution followed an August Twitter video showing AXiD members singing a racial slur in a rap song, and the authors said administrative silence signaled the university did not care about minority students. Before passage the senate amended the title to drop a call for outright removal from campus.

In the recordHerald, 24 Oct 2019

30 October2019

Executive board veto of Resolution 4-19-F upheld

The executive board vetoed Resolution 4-19-F by a 4-0 vote with two abstentions, and the senate confirmed the veto at its Tuesday meeting. President Will Harris, one of the abstainers, said the resolution's discrimination claim would have to come from the Student Code of Conduct and no violation had been noted by the Office of Student Conduct, while co-author Anthony Survance accused the executive branch of dragging the issue out. Senators also raised Harris's connection to Alpha Xi Delta as one of its knights, which he rejected as grounds for bias.

In the recordHerald, 30 Oct 2019

Go With the Flow feminine hygiene bill passes unanimously

Bill 1-20-S, funding the Go With the Flow program that supplies feminine hygiene products in campus restrooms, passed the senate unanimously. The bill, carried forward by Campus Improvement Chair Matthew Barr, doubled the program's budget from $588, and a floor amendment from Senator Symone Whalin raised the final amount to $1,300 from senate discretionary funds. Products were to be placed in Grise Hall, DSU, Preston Center, Gary Ransdell Hall and Snell Hall, including gender neutral bathrooms.

The senate voted to pass Bill 3-20-S, allocating $5,000 from the special projects fund to begin planning hammock poles across campus, after the sand volleyball court proposed earlier in the year was deemed too expensive. Planned locations included spots near most residence halls and the Valley, and Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds said he and Harris ran so SGA would be known for more than "scantrons and greenbooks". Legislative Research Chair Josh Zaczek criticized having to vote without seeing budget numbers, and the senate retained power to halt spending during planning.

WKU extends spring break, moves classes online amid COVID-19

WKU announced it would extend spring break by one week and transition to "alternative delivery formats" for classes amid growing coronavirus concerns, with President Tim Caboni recommending that students who could safely return home do so. The announcement came after the University of Kentucky and University of Louisville suspended in-person classes. In-person instruction never resumed that semester, upending the rest of SGA's spring calendar.

20 April2020

With campus closed by COVID-19, SGA postponed its spring elections until at least September so voting could happen in person, and added an "emergency clause" constitutional amendment allowing cabinet terms to be extended until the following election with judicial oversight. The cabinet continued meeting over Zoom every Tuesday. Harris said that after scholarships were awarded, the remainder of SGA's budget would be donated to the WKU Opportunity Fund and Emergency Relief Fund, and SGA gave its remaining food bank goods to the Office of Sustainability for redistribution.

Provost Cheryl Stevens told faculty that students who faced COVID-related problems could opt for a pass grade instead of a B or C, reversing the university's earlier refusal.
