9 February2024

Judicial council censures Salvador León

The SGA judicial council voted 6-0 to censure Administrative Vice President Salvador León after a Feb. 7 hearing on allegations that he spent funds, including a $425.25 Preston Center deposit for Neurodiversity Acceptance Week, before the senate passed the funding bill. León argued text messages showed President Sam Kurtz had accepted the spending, while Kurtz said he asked León multiple times not to spend before the bill passed. The council recommended no further disciplinary action beyond the censure.

In the recordHerald, 9 Feb 2024

15 February2024

Uber voucher program and parking fee measures

President Sam Kurtz and Chief of Staff Donte Reed announced a program of 450 Uber vouchers worth $10 each, distributed through social media giveaways, meeting attendance and SGA events. The senate also passed Resolution 18-23-S supporting a cap on student parking fees at $50 and Bill 19-23-S allocating $700 to help financially vulnerable students pay parking fines, along with $1,045 in Dental Hygiene Center and ID Center vouchers.

In the recordHerald, 15 Feb 2024

5 March2024

Rally trip to Frankfort, new voucher and cleanup plans

Kurtz previewed a senate trip to Frankfort for the Rally for Higher Education, where SGA planned to meet state Rep. Kevin Jackson and other Kentucky campus governments, and urged senators to seek re-election to preserve institutional knowledge. Chief of Staff Donté Reed introduced a need-based scholarship awarding four Uber vouchers and the Community Builder Excellence Scholarship for incoming Bowling Green-area freshmen. Campus Improvements and Sustainability chair Rush Robinson moved Earth Day from April 22 to April 19 and set a tentative Bowling Green cleanup for March 28.

In the recordHerald, 6 Mar 2024

13 March2024

Funding for DEI Week and Spring Fling

At its 20th meeting the senate funded SGA Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Week, four days of themed tabling from March 25 to 28 covering mental health, campus demographics, sexual health and deaf awareness. A $450 bill for the SGA Spring Fling, whose proceeds went to the Kids Cancer Alliance, passed 28-2 after debate among senators over the amount being spent. A $280 bill funded a Hope Harbor Denim Day event for Sexual Assault Prevention Month.

In the recordHerald, 13 Mar 2024

9 April2024

SGA closed the year with a Red Wave tailgate

SGA partnered with WKU Red Wave for the school year's last tailgate before a baseball game against Louisville, featuring winners of a "Battle of the DJs" social-media poll; sophomore Wilson Patterson won the $500 top scholarship prize as "DJ WLZN." Kurtz called the crowd to "savor one last tailgate of the 2023-2024 school year," with SGA grilling food for attendees.

In the recordHerald, 8 Apr 2024

16 April2024

Spring general election opened with over 60 candidates

Voting for the spring 2024 general election opened on TopNet with more than 60 students on the ballot for legislative seats. Kurtz, Chief of Staff Donté Reed and junior senator Ethan Taylor ran unopposed for student body president, executive vice president and administrative vice president respectively; the legislative council ballot included three senior, three junior and three sophomore senator seats, six college seats, an ISEC senator, a first-generation senator, a transfer/non-traditional senator and 14 senator-at-large seats.

In the recordHerald, 15 Apr 2024

17 April2024

23rd Senate holds its final meeting

The 23rd Senate met for the last time with no legislation on the agenda, spending the meeting on senators' final remarks. Kurtz thanked the senate and said in his final report, "We've done a lot of great things this year." Executive Vice President Annie Finch and Administrative Vice President Salvador León also gave closing reports before the 24th Senate's first meeting on April 23.

In the recordHerald, 17 Apr 2024

17 April2024

Kurtz re-elected unopposed to a second term

Running with Chief of Staff Donté Reed for executive vice president and junior senator Ethan Taylor for administrative vice president, Kurtz was re-elected without opposition as the 24th Senate's 34 members were announced the same night. More than 60 students had appeared on the ballot for the spring 2024 general election.

In the recordHerald, 17 Apr 2024

Sam Kurtz (president)

23 April2024

24th Senate installed: Vincent elected speaker, Henderson named chief justice

At the 24th Senate's first meeting, newly elected senators were sworn in and Sarah Vincent, College of Health and Human Services senator, was elected Speaker of the Senate over Sophia Bryant. Senior senator Anne-Marie Wright was appointed Chief of Staff, and Associate Chief Justice Ellen Henderson was appointed Chief Justice. Outgoing Chief Justice Isaac King swore in the new officers, officially opening the 2024-25 term.

In the recordHerald, 24 Apr 2024

27 August2024

Committee chairs and Judicial Council approved at fall opener

At the 24th Senate's first fall meeting, the Senate unanimously approved Kurtz's nominations of Aziz Umarov, Madison Payne, Neill Kane and Sam Dorris to the 2024-25 Judicial Council, and confirmed six committee chairs: Hannah Evans (Legislative Operations), Savanna Kurtz (Student Experience and Enrollment), Ryan Dilts (Outreach and Public Relations), Megan Farmer (DEI), Sophia Bryant (Student Mental Health and Wellbeing) and Annie Finch (Community Relations). President Timothy Caboni addressed the Senate on campus building renovations, the Mahurin Honors College restructuring and WKU's push for R2 research status.

In the recordHerald, 27 Aug 2024

28 August2024

Senate passed $100,000 budget at first meeting

At its first meeting of the year on Aug. 27, the SGA Senate passed a $100,000 budget for 2024-25, including $20,000 for organizational aid, $23,500 for scholarships and $10,705 in legislative discretionary funding. Executive leaders told the Herald editorial board they intended to spend the full allocation, and President Sam Kurtz credited WKU President Caboni with keeping the budget level for several years.

In the recordHerald, 28 Aug 2024

2 October2024

Fall election winners sworn in, school safety bill passed

Five senators elected in the fall election, three freshman senators plus an international and a Gatton Academy senator, were sworn in at the Oct. 1 meeting. The Senate passed three bills, including Bill 4-24-F to make school safety training mandatory for WKU professors and require posted emergency exits in classrooms, and two bills backing a Spooktober fundraiser for the Potter Children's Home Initiative.

In the recordHerald, 2 Oct 2024

22 October2024

Senate backs Myanmar flag, funds organizational aid and calculators

The Senate unanimously passed Resolution 5-24-F backing a Myanmar flag on the empty pole outside the Mahurin Honors College, sought by senators after students said Burmese and Chin students had no flag representing them; Bill 9-24-F distributed $10,000 in fall Organizational Aid funding across 58 graded applications; and Bill 10-24-F added $540 to buy five more calculators for the Borrow-a-Calculator program, which had lent 28 calculators that semester. Kurtz appointed freshman Emaun Riley as ISEC senator and Mahurin Honors College senator Caden Lucas as the Senate's parliamentarian.

In the recordHerald, 23 Oct 2024

7 November2024

Three senators removed for excessive absences

Senators Malick Ibrahim, Myricle Gholston and Karisha Petty were removed from their seats at a Nov. 6 censure meeting after each accumulated at least six unexcused absences from weekly senate meetings. The Judicial Council voted 7-0 to remove them under a constitutional provision requiring removal of any senator censured twice, calling the decision a matter of accountability rather than an attack on character.

In the recordHerald, 7 Nov 2024

5 February2025

Trump DEI order prompted constitutional review

Chief Justice Morgan Gammons said the SGA Constitution might require amendment to its diversity, equity and inclusion provisions after President Trump's executive order directing federal agencies to end DEI mandates. Gammons said the Judicial Council would meet to decide whether an amendment was needed, noting that WKU receives federal funding as a public university. The Senate also filled several appointed positions at the same meeting.

In the recordHerald, 5 Feb 2025

11 February2025

A mental health survey, and a warning about the election

The Senate passed Bill 4-25-S funding a DEI Committee tabling event to gather anonymous mental health survey responses. Dean of Students Martha Sales told the Senate 'you cannot isolate and educate at the same time'. Kurtz warned repeatedly that an unusually senior chamber made the spring election matter more than usual.

In the recordHerald, Feb 2025

26 February2025

Resolution backed Gordon Wilson Hall elevator

The Senate passed Resolution 2-25-S supporting installation of elevators in Gordon Wilson Hall, prompted by wheelchair user Kiersten Washington, whose dance appreciation class was scheduled on the building's third floor. It also passed Resolution 1-25-S supporting 24/7 hours at The Commons at Helm Library during finals week, and Kurtz announced a POLLapalooza effort with a goal of 3,000 voters in the April election.

In the recordHerald, 26 Feb 2025

26 March2025

Resolution supported mental health advisory board

The Senate passed Resolution 4-25-S supporting the formation of a Mental Health and Suicide Prevention Advisory Board to advise upper-level administration on student mental health policy, with Dean of Students Martha Sales planned to oversee its creation. Co-author Emma Harris, the Resident Staff Association president, said Counseling Center staffing shortages had pushed students to rely on resident advisors. The Senate passed eight bills at the same meeting.

In the recordHerald, 26 Mar 2025

4 April2025

Senate voted to rename DEI Committee

Senators unanimously passed Bill 21-25-S, a constitutional amendment restructuring the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Committee and renaming it the Action and Opportunity Committee, following President Trump's executive order dismantling DEI mandates. The meeting initially lacked the 21 members needed for a two-thirds vote, so absent members were called onto Zoom to reach quorum. The amendment then went to a student referendum during the April 13-15 election.

In the recordHerald, 4 Apr 2025

15 April2025

Rush Robinson elected on a turnout of 966

Elected alongside class, college, transfer, first-generation, Intercultural Student Engagement Center and Honors College senators - constituencies the 1966 constitution had no concept of.

In the recordWKU News

16 April2025

Students ratified DEI amendment with 88% of vote

In the spring election, the student body approved Bill 21-25-S, the constitutional amendment renaming the DEI Committee to the Action and Opportunity Committee, with 88% of votes in favor. Committee chair Megan Farmer said the committee at its core was not changing and the rename was meant to better communicate its actions. Results for 31 senate seats were announced the same night.

In the recordHerald, 16 Apr 2025

16 April2025

24th Senate held final meeting

The 24th Senate met for the last time on April 15 with no legislation on the agenda, spending the meeting on farewells. President Sam Kurtz, Vice President Donte Reed and Chief Financial Officer Ethan Taylor each received a standing ovation, and the Senate recorded 295 spring scholarship applications, far above the roughly 40-applicant average of past years.

The Board of Regents administered Robinson's oath of office as student regent, succeeding graduating president Sam Kurtz. At the same meeting the board elected Jan West chair, Doris Thomas vice chair and Melissa Dennison secretary for 2025-26.

Chief Communications Officer Preston Jenkins announced a plan to have four student artists each paint one side of a column in the SGA chambers, incorporating WKU campus elements, with selections due by 19 September.

25 November2025

Senate revived the transcript voucher program

The senate passed Bill 24-25-F, authored by Legislative Operations Committee Chair Caden Lucas, allocating $195 to reestablish the transcript voucher program, giving students one free official transcript a semester. It also funded a new "Professor of the Month" award and ping pong equipment for the DSU recreation area.

WKU Restaurant Group answered senators' questions

Restaurant Group representatives fielded senator questions on the removal of Steak 'n Shake seasoning, kiosks in Subway and adding spicy chicken sandwiches to Chick-fil-A's meal-swipe menu, and said the service handled about 60,000 meal transactions a week.

CPR-voucher bill and Grise Hall accessibility resolution passed

The senate unanimously passed Bill 2-26-S, funding six vouchers for free CPR certification, and Resolution 7-25-F, supporting additional handicapped-accessible restroom stalls in Grise Hall after a student's father said the building had only one large stall.

Senate adopted a fully codified rewrite of its bylaws

The Senate adopted an official codified version of the SGA Executive and Legislative Bylaws, superseding all prior versions, effective 24 February 2026.

24 March2026

SGA funded a tailgate to boost turnout at a baseball game

SGA used its projects fund to host free hot dogs, giveaways and a scholarship drawing before WKU baseball's home game against Louisville, an effort Robinson said answered Athletics Director Todd Stewart's call for more student engagement at games.

2 April2026

Senate learns the Gilbane housing partnership cleared the legislature

At its Thursday meeting SGA senators learned that the Kentucky Legislature had approved WKU's public-private partnership with developer Gilbane, which the Board of Regents had provisionally approved 11 December 2025 to design and build a new residence hall replacing Douglas Keen and Hugh Poland Halls. "WKU is now in the clear to start building the new residence halls," said Senator Jakob Barker, who with Senator Ethan Vietze also sponsored Resolution 7-26-S, backing a crosswalk at Alumni Avenue and Kentucky Street for residents of the 1355 Kentucky Street apartments who Barker's resolution said had to "step into oncoming traffic" to reach the Alumni Square parking garage. The same meeting passed legislation funding textbooks, exam supplies and lab goggles and authorizing a student-experience survey.

7 April2026

Weekly meeting funded a senior cookout, transfer cords and spikeball nets

SGA allocated $602.58 through three bills and a resolution: a senior sunset cookout, 240 transfer-student graduation cords, borrowable spikeball nets, and DSU signage improvements. CFO Gabriel Jerdon said the legislative discretionary fund would have $71.17 left if the following week's final bills all passed as written.

In the recordHerald, 8 Apr 2026

7 April2026

Two tickets take questions in the DSU auditorium

Caden Lucas with Jakob Barker and Will Derryberry against Jaden Marshall with Kaden Blankenship and Miles VanRude. Chief Justice Sophie Stirling moderated questions submitted by the student body.

In the recordHerald, April 2026

14 April2026

25th Senate closes the year having passed 56 bills, the most since 2018-19

The 25th Senate's final meeting passed its last three bills of the year - funding an NPHC preview day, the Office of Sustainability's food pantry, and massage-therapy vouchers for finals week, the latter two amended to spend down the year's remaining $71.17 budget - bringing the year's total to 56 pieces of legislation. Chief Communications Officer Preston Jenkins reported that WKU's new Artificial Intelligence Committee, which he sat on, was in early talks about bulk subscriptions to AI products such as ChatGPT Pro for all students and a possible introductory AI course for freshmen. Guest speakers included a Parking and Transportation representative, who said the bus system's diesel bill had roughly doubled amid rising fuel prices. The Herald identified her as "Ginny Griffin"; the official senate minutes give her name as "Jenny Griffith" - unresolved which is correct.

15 April2026

Turnout jumps 66% in a contested race

1,601 students voted, 635 more than the year before. Lucas won. The clearest evidence in the whole record that WKU turnout tracks whether there is an actual contest.

In the recordWKU News - Lucas elected

16 April2026

Robinson tells the Faculty Senate to look at the dorms

Sitting next to Faculty Regent Shane Spiller during a discussion of WKU housing, Robinson told senators to 'take a field trip' and see the state of the residence halls.

In the recordHerald, April 2026

18 April2026

Year-long mental health push closed with the Out of Darkness Walk

Robinson and Mental Health and Wellbeing Committee chair Veronica Butler spent the year pressing WKU on student mental health, citing data from social work professor Jay Gabbard that 44 percent of students reported depression symptoms and 10 percent had considered suicide in the past year. SGA co-ran Mental Health Week with the WKU Counseling Center and campus NAMI chapter, launched a Toppers Talk About It campaign, and forwarded student recommendations - including moving counseling services out of Potter Hall - through the Counseling Center Review Committee. The year closed with an Out of Darkness suicide-remembrance walk on April 18; incoming president Caden Lucas said the focus would continue.

The red suit jacket changes hands

At the first meeting of the 26th Senate, Robinson handed Lucas the red suit jacket, "the one that Sam (Kurtz) gave me." The same night, Gabby Pace, Cayden Bailey, Maggie Phelps and Jaden Marshall were sworn in to their new roles.

Robinson cast the lone dissenting vote on a tuition increase

At his last meeting as student regent, Robinson voted against a $204, 1.69 percent tuition increase that the rest of the Board of Regents approved, saying the board had to do everything it could to preserve affordability.

Executive candidates face off at SGA town hall

SGA held a town hall in the Downing Student Union Auditorium for the two executive tickets: Caden Lucas with Jakob Barker and Will Derryberry, and Jaden Marshall with Kaden Blankenship and Miles VanRude. Chief Justice Sophie Stirling moderated as the candidates answered 27 questions submitted by students. Both tickets made increasing awareness of SGA operations and outreach to the student body their central campaign promise.

Herald and Revolution Radio hosted a presidential debate

College Heights Herald Editor-in-Chief Jake McMahon and Assistant News Editor Kane Smith sat down with presidential candidates Caden Lucas and Jaden Marshall for a debate co-hosted with campus station Revolution Radio, ahead of voting opening the following Monday on TopNet.

15 April2026

Caden Lucas wins SGA presidential election

Caden Lucas and his ticket of Vice President-elect Jakob Barker and Chief Financial Officer-elect Will Derryberry won the spring election to serve during the 2026-27 academic year, defeating Jaden Marshall's ticket. Lucas, a junior senator, WKU Spiritmaster and chairman of the Hilltoppers Vote Coalition, ran on the motto "Lead, build, deliver" and a promise to make SGA operations more visible to students. The Herald did not publish vote totals or turnout figures; the story also listed the full slate of senators elected to the incoming 26th Senate.

In the recordHerald, 15 Apr 2026

24 April2026

Lucas named a 2026 Truman Scholar

Days after taking SGA's top office, President Caden Lucas was named a 2026 Truman Scholar, WKU's second in the scholarship's history and Kentucky's only recipient that year. The award, chosen from 781 candidates at 305 colleges nationally, provides $30,000 toward graduate or professional study and recognizes commitment to public service.

In the recordWKU News, 24 Apr 2026

28 April2026

26th Senate seated; tie vote for speaker resolved in Butler's favor

At the first meeting of the 26th Senate, outgoing president Rush Robinson passed the traditional red suit jacket to Caden Lucas, and the body swore in Gabi Pace as chief of staff, Cayden Bailey as chief communications officer, Maggie Phelps to the judicial council and defeated presidential candidate Jaden Marshall as an at-large senator. The race for speaker of the senate ended in a 9-9 tie between Amelia Tucker and Veronica Butler, and Chief Justice Sophie Sterling confirmed that neither the constitution nor the bylaws addressed a tie. Outgoing speaker Hadley Whipple ordered a re-vote, which elected Butler as speaker.

In the recordHerald, 28 Apr 2026

11 May2026

Lucas named ODK Circle Leader of the Year

WKU's Omicron Delta Kappa circle named President Caden Lucas its Heather Strode Circle Leader of the Year, an award for a student demonstrating leadership and dedication to the campus community across ODK's five core values.

In the recordWKU News, 11 May 2026

2 June2026

Lucas voices concern over proposed tuition increase

WKU released a proposed 2026-27 budget that would raise tuition by $210 to $6,246 per semester within a $405.1 million operating plan. Lucas, identified as SGA president and soon-to-be student regent, said he was "generally concerned" by a proposal that would raise the cost of attending WKU. He said students deserved both a high-quality education and an affordable way to achieve it.

In the recordHerald, 2 Jun 2026

5 June2026campus

Regents approve tuition increase over student regent's lone no vote

The Board of Regents approved a $204 tuition increase to $6,240 per semester, the sixth consecutive yearly increase, along with a 5% housing rate increase and a 2% meal plan increase as part of a $405 million operating budget. Every regent voted in favor except outgoing SGA president Rush Robinson, casting his final vote as student regent before Lucas took the seat. The board also suspended several majors, including kinesiology and geological sciences, for reworking and mergers.

In the recordHerald, 5 Jun 2026

7 July2026

SGA got a new adviser in Student Activities leadership change

Andrew Rash, who had served as SGA's faculty adviser and Associate Director of Student Activities and Greek Life since 2022, became interim director of the Department of Student Activities on July 1 following the retirement of longtime director Charley Pride. Assistant Director of Student Activities and Leadership and Volunteerism Amelia Kolb took over as SGA's adviser going forward.

Back to the top of the timeline

What this is

A year-by-year record of student government at Western Kentucky University, from the ratification of the Associated Students constitution in April 1966 to the present. Every entry names the source it came from.

Corrections

The names here start with the plaque in the SGA Chambers, and the plaque is known to be wrong in places. Where the archive disagrees with it, this site follows the archive and records the change on the corrections page. If you served, or you know that a year here is wrong, the project wants to hear from you through the Student Government Association office.

Reuse

Text on this site is the work of the project. Photographs, documents and legislation are reproduced from Western Kentucky University's own open archives and from the College Heights Herald and the Talisman; each item names the collection, issue and page it came from and links to the original.

Built 4 August 2026. The whole record is readable as data: years.json. Method and scope are set out on the about page.
